## Phase 50dr (2026-10-10): SIX RAM ADDRESSES DID NOT LAND - ASK THROUGH I/O INSTEAD

**THE UBI FIRE HUNG, AND THE RING STILL PROVES NOTHING.**

```
C18 = 0xC0DE0020   the mach's late_initcall crumb, NOT the panic notifier's step 42 -> a HANG
C1C = 0x80603000   the log address, so the hook ran and armed the safety timer
boot_id moved      and the SAFETY TIMER, not a panic, returned the box
```

The only change from the previous fire is the cmdline, **so the UBI path is what hangs.** And the ring
holds only early boot with my new cmdline in it - **nothing from the driver.**

**AND THE STAMPS ARE STILL NOT MINE.** `0x80606FF0` holds the same kind of static data as the fire before
(`0x847f4811`/`0x847f4c11`, delta exactly `0x400`; previously `0x8494D811`/`0x8494DC11`).

**SIX FIRES WENT INTO RAM ADDRESSES AND NOT ONE OF THEM LANDED:**

```
(void *)0x80607800 as a raw pointer    -> zero, and the write did nothing
diag + 1024                            -> zero
__va(0x80607800)                       -> zero, AND HUNG THE BOOT
ring + 0x3FF0 through luofu_log_b      -> still the same static data at that address
```

**EVERY ONE OF THEM WAS A PLACE I CHOSE.** **THE CHANNEL THIS DRIVER HAS WRITTEN ON EVERY SUCCESSFUL BOOT
IS NOT RAM AT ALL** - it is **`C18`/`C1C`, two memory-mapped registers, written through `fmc->crumb` and
read back with `devmem`.** That is the channel the crumb steps have used all along, **and the file's own
comment says why: "the crumb channel, the one that has always worked, because it is I/O rather than RAM."**

**SO THE TIMER WRITES A CRUMB, FIRST, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE IT DOES:**

```c
luofu_log_ticks++;
if (luofu_fmc_stamp)
	luofu_fmc_crumb(luofu_fmc_stamp, LUOFU_LOG_TICK_STEP, luofu_log_ticks);
```

```
C18 = 0xc0de502d, C1C = tick count   the timer ran, this many times
C18 = 0xc0de502a, C1C = log address  the panic notifier overwrote it
C18 = 0xc0de0020                     a hang - no tick survived
```

**IT IS WRITTEN BEFORE THE DUMP AND BEFORE THE RAM STAMPS, so whatever faults afterwards cannot erase
it** - **which matters, because the last fire HUNG rather than panicked and the tick's own work is the
prime suspect for that.**

**AND THE QUESTION IT ANSWERS IS THE ONE THE RING CANNOT: whether the 500 ms timer runs at all.** Six
fires of evidence say the ring only ever holds the console's registration dump, **and `ticks = 0` in RAM
would be indistinguishable from a write that did not happen** - **which is exactly the ambiguity that has
cost this many fires. An I/O crumb cannot have that ambiguity.**

**Validator clean:** balance 0/0/0, 27 functions with none called before its definition (including
`luofu_fmc_crumb` before the timer uses it), 15 file-scope variables with none used before its
declaration, no undefined macro, no define-after-use, hook get/put balanced.

**Device mutation.** Unchanged: the `kernela` write and its reboots, plus the verified UBI volume in
`mtd16`. The router is healthy.

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50ds (2026-10-10): THE TIMER RUNS 46 TIMES - AND THE BOOT HANGS, NOT PANICS ★★★★★

**THE CRUMB ANSWERED IN ONE READ WHAT SIX FIRES OF RING-INSPECTION COULD NOT:**

```
C18 = 0xC0DE502D     LUOFU_CRUMB_NAND | step 45 - the tick crumb
C1C = 0x0000002E     46 decimal - THE TICK COUNT
```

**THE 500 ms TIMER RUNS. It fired 46 times - about 23 seconds** - **and the crumb SURVIVED because it is
I/O rather than RAM.** **It was never overwritten by step 42 either, so THE BOOT DID NOT PANIC: IT HUNG,
ROUGHHLY 23 SECONDS IN.**

**THAT IS A DIFFERENT FAILURE FROM EVERY PREVIOUS FIRE, AND IT POINTS AT CONCURRENCY.** The boot gets
that far **and then stops entirely** - the shape of a **shared resource under overlapping access.**

**AND THIS DRIVER HAS EXACTLY ONE:**

```c
luofu_fmc_read_page() stages every page through fmc->dma_buf and copies out of fmc->page_buf,
and luofu_mtd_read() calls it in a loop. Both buffers belong to the DEVICE, not to the caller,
AND NOTHING SERIALISED THEM.
```

**That was fine while the only caller was a single-threaded probe. IT IS NOT FINE ONCE UBI IS IN THE
PATH:** `ubiattach` scans with its own workqueue and **`ubi_bgt0d` runs in the background**, so **two reads
can be inside `read_page` at the same time, staging into the same 0x2200 bytes.** **Progress until the
overlap, then no progress at all - which is what the tick crumb measured.**

```c
static DEFINE_MUTEX(luofu_fmc_read_lock);

luofu_mtd_read():
	mutex_lock(&luofu_fmc_read_lock);
	while (done < len) { ... if (ret) break; ... }
	mutex_unlock(&luofu_fmc_read_lock);
```

**The loop BREAKS on error rather than returning, so the unlock runs on every path, and the bounds check
returns before the lock is taken.** The probe's direct calls to `luofu_fmc_read_page()` **stay outside the
lock on purpose** - they run single-threaded at `late_initcall`, before any of this is reachable.

**AND THE CRUMB PAYLOAD NOW CARRIES BOTH NUMBERS, THE LAST INSTRUMENT QUESTION:**

```
C1C = (ticks << 16) | (lines & 0xffff)

high > 0, low > 0   the kmsg walk works and the ring write is what fails
high > 0, low = 0   the walk returns NOTHING, and the log buffer is the problem
```

**Validator clean:** balance 0/0/0, 27 functions, 15 file-scope variables, **no call or use before its
declaration, no undefined macro, no define-after-use, hook get/put balanced, and ONE LOCK WITH ONE UNLOCK
AND NO EARLY RETURN BETWEEN THEM.**

**Device mutation.** Unchanged: the `kernela` write and its reboots, plus the verified UBI volume in
`mtd16`. The router is healthy.


---

## Phase 50dt (2026-10-10): THE THIRD ORDER FAILURE - AND THE CHECKER ITSELF HAD THE GAP

```
luofu-fmc.c:844: error: 'luofu_fmc_read_lock' undeclared (first use in this function)
```

**The mutex went in beside the log globals, 600 lines BELOW `luofu_mtd_read()`'s first use of it.**
**Third time for this class - and this time the validator did not catch it either, which is the part worth
recording.**

**WHY THE CHECKER MISSED IT.** Its variable pattern required the declaration to **end in `=` or `;`**:

```python
r"\s*static\s+(?:const\s+)?[\w\s\*]+?\b(luofu_\w+)\s*(=|;)"
```

**AND `static DEFINE_MUTEX(luofu_fmc_read_lock);` ENDS IN A CLOSING PAREN.** The regex did not match the
line at all, **so the mutex was never entered into the set of things checked, and the order test had
nothing to test.** **A CHECKER THAT MISSES A DECLARATION *FORM* MISSES THE WHOLE ORDER CLASS FOR THAT
FORM.**


**and the checker now also matches macro-declared file-scope state:**

```python
r"\s*static\s+[A-Z_]+\((luofu_\w+)\s*[,)]"

```

**WHAT THE MUTEX IS FOR, UNCHANGED:** `luofu_fmc_read_page()` stages every page through **`fmc->dma_buf`**

probe; **NOT fine with UBI in the path, where `ubiattach` scans from its own workqueue and `ubi_bgt0d`
runs in the background.** The boot **HANGS** rather than faults or panics - **the tick crumb measured 46
ticks, about 23 seconds** - **and a shared staging buffer under overlapping readers is exactly that
shape.**

returns before the lock is taken.**

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50dw (2026-10-10): THE RING WORKS - MY EXTRACTION WAS THE BUG ★★★★★

**TWO FINDINGS FROM THE LAST FIRE, AND THE FIRST ONE IS THAT MY READER WAS WRONG.**

**THE RING WORKS.** Scanning `0x80602000..0x80608000` for the dumper's mark `0xc0de1055` found it at
**exactly one address, `0x80603000`**, **and the text there carries PANIC-ERA content:** stack dumps at
**3.99 s**, frames for **`notifier_call_chain`**, **`blocking_notifier_call_chain`** and
**`pkcs1pad_create`**, and the command line.

**WHAT WAS WRONG WAS MY EXTRACTION.** I had been reading the **FIRST bytes** of the ring and calling them
the state of the boot - **when the dumper writes CIRCULARLY and the NEWEST text is wherever its offset
stopped.**

```
timestamped lines in the ring: 35, spanning 0.000 s to 3.997 s
```

**AND THE CRUMB DECODED: `C1C = 0x002600F2` is 38 ticks and 242 lines.** So the log is readable, the walk
works, and the boot:

```
logged until   ~4 s
ticked until   19 s   (38 x 500 ms)
then STOPPED ENTIRELY - the safety timer never fired either, so TIMERS THEMSELVES STOPPED
```

**THAT IS A HARD HANG, NOT A DEADLOCK THAT YIELDS.** The box's own watchdog is what returned it, **and a
hang that kills timers is a hang with interrupts disabled.**

**SO THE NEXT QUESTION IS WHERE, AND THE ANSWER GOES IN THE CRUMB - THE CHANNEL THAT WORKS.** A phase
global is set at four points and the tick publishes it on every fire:

```
C18 = 0xc0de502d        C1C = (phase << 16) | ticks

1  the probe was entered
2  the timers were armed (inside luofu_log_register)
3  the probe returned
4  late_initcall_sync completed - THE MOUNT IS NEXT
```

**Whichever phase survives is where the boot stopped**, and since the probe's own crumb is overwritten by
the tick every 500 ms, **the phase is the only way to see it after a hard hang.**

**AND THE CHECKER CAUGHT THE ORDER BUG BEFORE THE COMPILER DID:**

```
vars: 17 | use-before-decl: [('luofu_phase', 1477, 1036)]
```

**`luofu_phase` was declared at line 1477 and first set at 1036 - the same order class that has now cost
three builds.** **BUT I RAN THE CHECKER IN THE SAME CELL AS THE COMMIT AND DID NOT READ ITS OUTPUT
FIRST**, so the broken version went out anyway. **THE PROCESS FIX, WHICH IS THE POINT OF RECORDING THIS:
validate in one step, read the result, and only then commit. FOUR BUILDS HAVE NOW GONE INTO THIS CLASS;
THREE OF THEM WERE AVOIDABLE BY READING OUTPUT I ALREADY HAD.**

**Device mutation.** Unchanged: the `kernela` write and its reboots, plus the verified UBI volume in
`mtd16`. The router is healthy.

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50dx (2026-10-10): A MUTEX WHERE ONLY A SPINLOCK IS LEGAL - THAT IS THE HARD HANG ★★★★★

**TWO FINDINGS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE HANG.**

## 1. STEP 42 WAS NEVER THE PANIC NOTIFIER

**The probe calls `luofu_fmc_crumb(fmc, LUOFU_LOG_PANIC_STEP, ...)` IN THE MIDDLE OF ITSELF** - **it is a
generic marker, not a death-path report.** **Every reading I took as "the panic notifier ran" was that
line, which means EVERY FIRE THAT SHOWED `0xC0DE502A` WAS A HANG, not a panic.** That is worth stating
plainly because **it changes the history: there has been no successful panic since the UBI cmdline went
in.**

## 2. THE PHASE CRUMB NAMED THE PLACE, AND THE PRIMITIVE WAS WRONG

```
C1C = 0x0002002F   phase 2, 47 ticks
```

**Phase 2 is set inside `luofu_log_register` at the timer setup. PHASE 1 IS SET ON THE PROBE'S FIRST LINE,
SO THE PROBE NEVER RAN AT ALL** - the hang is **before it, in the UBI attach**, and it is **HARD**: the tick
stopped at 47, **so timers themselves died and the safety timer never fired. The box's own watchdog
returned it.**

**AND THE CAUSE IS THE LOCK I ADDED TWO COMMITS AGO.** It was a **MUTEX**, on the reasoning that two
readers must not stage into `fmc->dma_buf` at once. **THE REASONING WAS RIGHT AND THE PRIMITIVE WAS
WRONG:**

```
UBI CALLS mtd_read() WITH A SPINLOCK HELD, AND A MUTEX SLEEPS.
```

**Sleeping in atomic context is exactly what the measurement looks like from the outside** - **a hard hang,
dead timers, interrupts off, no watchdog but the SoC's own.**

```c
static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(luofu_fmc_read_lock);

spin_lock_irqsave(&luofu_fmc_read_lock, flags);
while (done < len) { ... if (ret) break; ... }
spin_unlock_irqrestore(&luofu_fmc_read_lock, flags);
```

**`irqsave`/`restore` rather than plain `spin_lock`, because this driver's read path never needs interrupts
- its completion condition is a STATUS BIT it polls** - **and UBI may call it with interrupts on or off.**
The loop still **breaks on error so the unlock runs on every path.**

**AND THE RANGE OF THE BUG IS WORTH RECORDING: THE MUTEX WENT IN BEFORE THE UBI CMDLINE DID.** The mutex
alone was fine, because **nothing called `mtd_read` from atomic context.** **It became fatal the moment UBI
was in the path - which is why the hangs started with the cmdline change and not with the lock.**

**Validator, run as its own step this time and read before committing:** balance (0,0,0), 17 file-scope
variables with none used before its declaration, 28 functions with none called before its definition, no
undefined macro, and **one spinlock with one unlock and a single return after it.**

**Device mutation.** Unchanged: the `kernela` write and its reboots, plus the verified UBI volume in
`mtd16`. The router is healthy.

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50dy (2026-10-10): THE PERIODIC DUMP WAS STRANGLING THE KERNEL ★★★★★

**THE LAST FIRE RETURNED THE SAME NUMBERS AS THE ONE BEFORE IT:**

```
C1C = 0x0002002F   phase 2, 47 ticks - IDENTICAL
```

**Same phase, same tick count, two consecutive fires. SO THIS IS DETERMINISTIC, AND THE SPINLOCK WAS NOT
THE CAUSE. A race would move the number.**

**AND THE SHAPE OF THE FAILURE POINTS AT MY OWN INSTRUMENT:**

```
printk stopped at   ~4 s      <- the log's newest entry
the tick stopped at 47        ~23.5 s, when the system finally gave out
the safety timer never fired  so timers died too
the box's own watchdog returned it
```

**PRINTK DIED FIRST WHILE EVERYTHING ELSE KEPT RUNNING.** **And the thing that holds `logbuf_lock` on this
system is `luofu_kmsg_to()`, which walks THE WHOLE LOG - 242 lines when this was measured - with
`kmsg_dump_get_line` taking the lock for each one. FROM A TIMER, WHICH IS SOFTIRQ CONTEXT.** **That is 242
locked iterations with interrupts held off, every 500 ms.**

**AT A 500 ms CADENCE THE KERNEL WAS LOSING A LARGE FRACTION OF ITS INTERRUPT TIME TO MY OWN INSTRUMENT.**
Printk starves first because **it is the thing waiting on the same lock**; the softirq keeps running
because **it is the one holding it**; and eventually the system gives out entirely and **only the SoC
watchdog recovers it.** **A hard, deterministic hang - which is what starvation looks like and what no
race looks like.**

```c
#define LUOFU_LOG_TICK_MS   5000      /* was 500 */
```

**THE PANIC PATH KEEPS ITS FULL WALK.** A panic is **terminal**, so starving it costs nothing, and the full
log is exactly what a panic needs. **Only the periodic one is slowed, and at 5 s a reading still carries
the log from up to 20 s into the boot** - later than anything the 500 ms cadence ever managed to preserve.

**AND THE MEASUREMENT TO WATCH NEXT: IF THE STARVATION WAS THE CAUSE, THE TICK COUNT WILL GROW PAST 47.**
**That number has been identical across two fires and is the cleanest signal this project has had.**

**Validator, run as its own step and read before committing:** balance (0,0,0), 17 file-scope variables
with none used before its declaration, 28 functions with none called before its definition, no undefined
macro. **CLEAN.**

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50dz (2026-10-10): THE HANG IS GONE, A REAL PANIC APPEARED, AND THE RING FINALLY HAS A REASON ★★★★★

**THE STARVATION FIX WORKED, AND IT SHOWED A REAL PANIC FOR THE FIRST TIME.**

```
C18 = 0xC0DE502A     step 42
C1C = 0x00000000     ZERO ticks
```

**The probe's step-42 marker carries `(log_dma & 0xfffff000) | mtd index`, which is never zero - so a zero
payload means this crumb is the PANIC NOTIFIER's, and ZERO TICKS means the boot panicked inside the first
five seconds.** **Where the previous four fires hung at 47 ticks with timers dead, this one PANICKED.**
**The starvation was real and slowing the dump removed it.**

## AND IT EXPOSED WHY THE RING HAS NEVER CARRIED A PANIC

```c
kmsg_dump_get_line_nolock() opens with:  if (!dumper->active) goto out;
```

**`kmsg_dump()` sets `active` on its way INTO a callback and CLEARS IT AGAIN ON THE WAY OUT.** **My panic
notifier runs from the panic notifier chain, which `panic()` calls AFTER `kmsg_dump()` has returned - SO
`active` IS FALSE, THE WALK PRODUCES NOTHING, AND THE RING KEEPS WHATEVER AN EARLIER BOOT LEFT THERE.**

**THAT IS WHY A PANICKING BOOT AND A STALE BOOT LOOK IDENTICAL FROM `devmem`.** The ring read **4152
non-zero bytes on this fire and on the one before it, byte for byte, and I spent several fires reading an
old boot's log as the current one's.**

```c
luofu_kmsg.active = true;
luofu_log_frozen = true;
luofu_kmsg_to(luofu_log_b, &luofu_kmsg);
luofu_kmsg.active = false;
```

**AND THE CRUMB MOVES AFTER THE WALK.** It used to be written first, **which made its line count
meaningless** - `luofu_log_lines` is only set **BY** the walk, so a crumb written before it **always reported
zero lines**, and I read that as **an empty log rather than as an ordering mistake.**

**The timer already did both of these, which is why the timer's walk returned 242 lines. The panic notifier
did not, and that is the whole difference between an instrument that works and one that reports the past.**

**Validator:** balance (0,0,0), 17 file-scope variables, 28 functions, no undefined macro, hook get/put 2/3.
**CLEAN, read before committing.**

**Device mutation.** Unchanged: the `kernela` write and its reboots, plus the verified UBI volume in
`mtd16`. The router is healthy.

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50eb (2026-10-10): THE PHYSICAL ADDRESS WAS RIGHT ALL ALONG - `__va` IS THE QUESTION ★★★★★

```
C1C = 0x000CD603     lines = 0xCD = 205     page bits = 0x603
```

**AND `0x80603000 >> 12` IS `0x80603`, WHOSE LOW TWELVE BITS ARE `0x603` - SO THE MATCH IS EXACT AND
`luofu_log_dma` IS `0x80603000`, EXACTLY WHAT THIS DRIVER ASKED FOR.** **THE ADDRESS WAS NEVER THE
PROBLEM.** **All the guesswork about collision shifts and window bases was chasing something that was
already right.**

## WHAT HAS NEVER BEEN CHECKED IS WHAT `__va()` TURNED IT INTO

```c
luofu_log_b = (void *)__va((phys_addr_t)luofu_log_dma);
```

**On ARM that is `x - PHYS_OFFSET + PAGE_OFFSET`.** **It never gets re-examined after it is assigned, and
every RAM write this driver makes since this phase began has vanished - the ring, the diagnostic buffer,
and every stamp - while every I/O write has stuck.** **That is exactly the shape of a pointer aimed at
memory nothing is listening to.**

**SO THE PANIC CRUMB CARRIES ITS TOP BYTE:**

```
C1C = (lines << 8) | ((luofu_log_b >> 24) & 0xff)

0xC0   __va gave 0xC06xxxxx - the expected kernel virtual address
0x40   it gave 0x406xxxxx - or the physical address unmodified
0x80   it gave 0x806xxxxx - __va was a no-op, so PHYS_OFFSET == PAGE_OFFSET on this SoC
```

**AND ONE OF THOSE IS THE ANSWER, BECAUSE THE RING AT `0x80603000` PHYSICAL DOES HOLD TEXT** - **this
kernel's own first boot, byte for byte, with a newest timestamp of 4.380 s that never moves.**
**SOMETHING WROTE THERE ONCE.** **If `luofu_log_b` is not pointing where that text is, then the writes
vanish for a reason that has nothing to do with the address this driver computed, and everything to do
with the translation applied to it.**

**The line count stays in the payload, so a boot that gets further still reports how much it logged.**

**Validator:** balance (0,0,0), 17 file-scope variables, 28 functions, no undefined macro. **CLEAN.**

**Device mutation.** Unchanged: the `kernela` write and its reboots, plus the verified UBI volume in
`mtd16`. The router is healthy.

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50ec (2026-10-10): THE POINTER IS RIGHT AND THE TRANSLATION IS RIGHT ★★★★★

```
C1C = 0x0000CDC0     lines = 0xCD = 205, top byte = 0xC0
```

**`0xC0` MEANS `__va()` PRODUCED `0xC06xxxxx`, THE EXPECTED KERNEL VIRTUAL ADDRESS.** **So three things are
ruled out in one reading:**

```
the physical address   0x80603000, matched exactly by the page bits two fires ago
the translation        __va gave the kernel virtual address, not the physical one
the walk               205 lines, every time
```

**AND THE WRITES STILL VANISH.** The text at `0x80603000`, read with `devmem`, **is this kernel's FIRST
boot and never changes** - **while every I/O write this driver makes, through the same kind of pointer
arithmetic, sticks.**

## SO THE LAST POSSIBILITY IS A STATEMENT ABOUT TWO PATHS

**What the dumper writes through `luofu_log_b` is not what `devmem` reads at the address the driver
computed.** **That is testable in one word** - read the ring back **through its own pointer** and put the
result in the crumb:

```c
C1C = (lines << 16) | (*(volatile u32 *)(luofu_log_b + 4) & 0xffff);
```

**AND THE REFERENCE IS ALREADY IN HAND, read with `devmem` just now:**

```
0x80603000 = 0xC0DE1055     the ring's MARK is there
0x80603004 = 0x5B3E363C     "<6>[" - the first text
```

```
crumb low 16 == 0x363C   the two paths meet, and the vanishing writes are something else again
crumb low 16 != 0x363C   THE TWO PATHS DO NOT MEET, and that is the fault
```

the probe.**

## BUT THE TEXT IS SPLICED

**`"Zone rangrom [<c0708c50>]"` IS TWO DIFFERENT LINES OVERLAPPED**, **and the trace's frames are cut
through by fragments of older text.** **The ring is 16 KiB of fixed memory that nothing clears between
boots, and the dump only rewrites the first 3.5 KiB of it - so the previous contents show through
everything that is not overwritten.**

```c
memset(p, 0, LUOFU_LOG_KEEP);
```

**AND IT IS HERE RATHER THAN AT REGISTRATION ON PURPOSE.** **An earlier attempt to write to these buffers
while the kernel was alive MOVED THE FAILURE FORWARD AND KILLED THE BOOT** - that is recorded in this file.
**This function now runs only from the panic path and the 5-second tick, and the panic path is terminal,
so zeroing here cannot shorten a boot that is already over.**

**WITH PURE TEXT THE WARNING'S MESSAGE LINE APPEARS FOR THE FIRST TIME - and that line names what
`warn_slowpath_fmt` was complaining about, which is the first concrete thing about this fault that is not
an inference.**

define-after-use, hook get/put 2/3. **CLEAN.**

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50ef (2026-10-10): THE LOCK WAS STARVING EVERYTHING ★★★★★

**THE RING SAID WHERE THE BOOT DIES, IN THE KERNEL'S OWN WORDS:**

```
3.315547  Creating 1...                       <- "Creating 1 UBI device"
3.464127  Registering...                      <- ubi0 registering
3.599879  ubi0: go, 1024K init, 160K bss...   <- ubi0 ATTACHED
4.026379  devtmpfs: mounted
4.053960  "  with a"                          <- AND THE LOG ENDS MID-WORD
```

**THE RAW BYTES ARE UNAMBIGUOUS:** `"...<7>[    4.053960]   with a"` followed by **THIRTY-TWO ZEROS** - the
tail of the window this driver memsets - **and then older text.** **THE WALK WROTE UP TO THAT WORD AND
STOPPED, SO THAT IS THE LOG BUFFER'S LAST ENTRY: THE KERNEL STOPPED PRINTING IN THE MIDDLE OF A MESSAGE.**

**A CPU that stops mid-printk with the log buffer intact is not looping - IT IS BEING STARVED, and the
instrument that did it is THIS LOCK:**

```c
spin_lock_irqsave(&luofu_fmc_read_lock, flags);
while (done < len) { ... luofu_fmc_read_page(...); ... }
spin_unlock_irqrestore(&luofu_fmc_read_lock, flags);
```

**A UBI ATTACH READS 128 KiB ERASE BLOCKS - 64 PAGES PER CALL - AND THIS HELD INTERRUPTS OFF ACROSS THE
WHOLE THING.** **The 180-second safety timer cannot fire with interrupts off. Printk stops. And the SoC
watchdog is what finally resets the box, which is exactly the recovery path every one of these fires has
been showing.**

```c
while (done < len) {
	spin_lock_irqsave(&luofu_fmc_read_lock, flags);
	ret = luofu_fmc_read_page(fmc, row, fmc->page_buf);
	if (ret == 0)
		memcpy(buf + done, fmc->page_buf + off, chunk);
	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&luofu_fmc_read_lock, flags);
	if (ret)
		break;
	done += chunk;
}
```

**`fmc->dma_buf` and `fmc->page_buf` ARE THE ONLY SHARED STATE, and they are touched inside
`luofu_fmc_read_page` - so the lock goes there, per page, held for microseconds instead of seconds.**
The copy moves inside it **because the staging buffer is what it copies from.**

**AND THIS EXPLAINS THE WHOLE PHASE'S MOST STUBBORN FACT: printk dying at ~4 s while the kernel lived on.
IT WAS NOT THE DUMPER STARVING PRINTK. IT WAS THIS LOCK STARVING EVERYTHING, and the dumper was simply the
last thing to get a word in.**

**Validator:** balance (0,0,0), 17 file-scope variables, 28 functions, no undefined macro, no
define-after-use, **one spinlock with one unlock and no early return between them.** **CLEAN.**

**Device mutation.** Unchanged: the `kernela` write and its reboots, plus the verified UBI volume in
`mtd16`. The router is healthy.

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50eg (2026-10-10): THE FRONTIER MOVED, AND THE SLIDE WAS CUTTING LINES IN HALF ★★★★★

**THE PER-PAGE LOCK HELPED, AND THE RING SHOWS IT:**

```
max timestamp  4.053960  ->  4.265227
ubi0: go, 1024K init, 160K bss...   ubi0 ATTACHED
```

**The boot reaches a fifth of a second further - small in wall-clock and large in meaning: the lock WAS
holding interrupts off, and releasing it more often MOVED THE FRONTIER.**

## AND A KERNEL WARNING'S HEADER IS NOW VISIBLE

```
4>[    3.061116] ------------[ c          <- "------------[ cut here ]------------"
```

**BUT ITS BODY IS UNREADABLE, AND THE REASON IS MY OWN SLIDE.** The window was written directly and slid
with `off = 4` whenever the next line would not fit - **WHICH CUTS A LINE IN HALF AND SPLICES THE NEWEST
TEXT INTO THE MIDDLE OF THE OLDEST.** **That is what six apparent "wraps" inside one 3.5 KiB window were,
each between a late timestamp and 0.000000: NOT A CIRCLE, BUT LINES CHOPPED THROUGH.**

```c
static char scratch[LUOFU_LOG_SCRATCH];

if (s + len + 1 > sizeof(scratch)) {
	size_t keep_from = sizeof(scratch) / 2;

	while (keep_from < s && scratch[keep_from] != '\n')
		keep_from++;
	if (keep_from < s)
		keep_from++;

	memmove(scratch, scratch + keep_from, s - keep_from);
	s -= keep_from;
}
```

**Lines accumulate in the scratch first. When it fills, the oldest HALF is dropped and the cut is moved
forward to the next newline - SO EVERY BYTE THAT REACHES THE WINDOW IS A WHOLE LINE.** The window then
takes the tail, **also starting at a line boundary.**

**WITH THAT, THE WARNING'S BODY IS READABLE FOR THE FIRST TIME - and a warning with a stack trace through
`warn_slowpath_fmt` at 3.06 s, JUST BEFORE `ubi0` ATTACHES, is THE MOST CONCRETE THING THIS FAULT HAS
PRODUCED.**

define-after-use. **CLEAN.**

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50eh (2026-10-10): THE ROOTFS MOUNTS - AND THE HOLES WERE UNFLUSHED CACHE ★★★★★

## 1. THE 32-BYTE ZERO HOLES ARE UNFLUSHED CACHE LINES

**The window's text is cut apart by holes that are EXACTLY 32 BYTES - one cache line - scattered
through otherwise-contiguous text.** **That has one mechanical cause: every write to this region goes
through the linear map and is CACHED, and this board is reset by a watchdog with no cache maintenance in
between.** **Dirty lines that happen to be evicted reach DRAM; the rest never leave L1/L2 and are gone when
the vendor image boots.**

**AND THAT IS THE "UNIFYING FACT" THIS PROJECT RECORDED SEVERAL FIRES AGO - every I/O write sticks and
every RAM write seems to vanish - characterised CORRECTLY, explained WRONG:** the crumb registers always
worked because **I/O space is UNCACHED**; the RAM window never did because **it is cached and nobody ever
flushed it.** **And the "the two paths meet" reading two fires ago was true only because the one line it
compared happened to have been evicted before the reset.**

```c
__cpuc_flush_dcache_area(p, LUOFU_LOG_KEEP);
outer_flush_range(__pa(p), __pa(p) + LUOFU_LOG_KEEP);
```

## 2. AND THE LOG SAYS THE ROOTFS MOUNTED

```
1984  >[    4.056766] Run /sbin/init a
2016  s init process..<7>[    4.060848
2048  ]   with arguments:..<7>[    4.0
2080  60852]     /sbin/init..<7>[ ..<4
```

**"Run /sbin/init as init process" WITH "with arguments: /sbin/init" is printed by `kernel_init()` ONLY
AFTER `prepare_namespace()` HAS MOUNTED THE ROOT.** **If the mount had failed the kernel would have
panicked with "VFS: Unable to mount root fs" instead.** **SO THE SQUASHFS ROOTFS IN THE UBI VOLUME MOUNTS
AND THE KERNEL STARTS INIT.**

**AND THE DEATH IS AFTER INIT STARTS, not at the mount.** The same window carries, at 4.271302 and
4.28-4.29:

```
[<c071aed0>]
[<c0708474>] (do_work_pending+0xe4/0x3ac)
Exception stack(0xc0639fb0 to 0xc0639ff8)
```

**which is an exception taken on the syscall/user-return path - AFTER init was exec'd.**

**SO THE NEXT FIRE'S JOB IS DIFFERENT FROM EVERY FIRE SO FAR: NOT "WHY WON'T IT MOUNT" BUT "WHAT IS THIS
EXCEPTION IN THE FIRST USER PROCESS".** **And with the flush, the log that describes it will be the log that
survives.**

**exitcode=0x00000004 = signal 4 = SIGILL.** The kernel reached init, init took an illegal instruction, and
init dying is fatal. **THE KERNEL HALF OF THE EVAL CRITERION IS DONE: UBI attaches, the volume resolves,
the squashfs rootfs MOUNTS, and init is exec'd.**

## AND THE CAUSE IS ONE LINE IN THE ROOTFS

Mounted the volume on the vendor system and read it:

```
DISTRIB_TARGET='armsr/armv7'
DISTRIB_ARCH='arm_cortex-a15_neon-vfpv4'      <-- WRONG CPU
```

**The userspace was built for CORTEX-A15 with VFPv4. Our SoC is a Cortex-A9** (`CPU: ARMv7 Processor
[414fc091]`, part 0xc09). **An A9 has NO hardware divide (sdiv/udiv) and NO VFPv4 (vfma) - so the A15
build legitimately contains instructions this CPU cannot decode. THE MOUNT WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM; THE
USERSPACE WAS BUILT FOR THE WRONG CORE.**

## THE FIX, TAKEN AND VERIFIED ON THE DEVICE

`arm_cortex-a9_vfpv3-d16` is a strict subset of this A9's capability - no idiv, no vfpv4. **The image was
carved straight out of a 25.12.5 mvebu image:** download the smallest `squashfs-sysupgrade.bin`, find
`hsqs`, read bytes_used from the superblock, trim.

```
mvebu/cortexa9    arch_packages = arm_cortex-a9_vfpv3-d16
bcm53xx/generic   arch_packages = arm_cortex-a9
sunxi/cortexa7    arch_packages = arm_cortex-a7_neon-vfpv4     (A7 has idiv+vfpv4 - still wrong)
```

```
squashfs v4.0  block_size=262144  compression=XZ  bytes_used=2852982  inodes=1061
```

**And it is confirmed mounted on the device, not assumed:**

```
DISTRIB_TARGET='mvebu/cortexa9'
DISTRIB_ARCH='arm_cortex-a9_vfpv3-d16'
DISTRIB_RELEASE='25.12.5'
Volume ID: 0 (on ubi1)   Size: 133 LEBs   State: OK   Name: owrt
```

**The vendor's own ubi0 untouched, the volume detached afterwards, /tmp/u unmounted.**

## NOTE FOR THE NEXT FIRE

**With a working userspace there may be NO PANIC, so the panic crumb (step 42) will not be written - the
5-second TICK (step 45) is what will carry the state and the window content.** And the 180-second safety
timer is what brings the box back.

## TWO USERSPACES, TWO BASELINES, THE SAME DEATH

```
armsr/armv7      arm_cortex-a15_neon-vfpv4    -> init killed by signal 4, exitcode 0x00000004
mvebu/cortexa9   arm_cortex-a9_vfpv3-d16      -> init killed by signal 4, exitcode 0x00000004
```

**A rootfs compiled for a STRICT SUBSET of this A9's capability cannot be using an instruction this core
lacks** - so the CPU baseline was NOT the cause. **And the fact that BOTH die identically points at
something the two share, which is the kernel they run on.**

**A HARD-FLOAT USERSPACE TRAPS ON EVERY FLOATING POINT INSTRUCTION IF THE FPU WAS NEVER ENABLED.**

**`CONFIG_VFP` and `CONFIG_NEON` are both set - the config lane asserts them - so the open question is
not whether the code is compiled in, but whether `vfp_init()` actually brought the unit up on this SoC.**

## AND NOTHING IN THE LOG COULD HAVE SAID OTHERWISE

**ARM's `do_undefinstr()` prints `undefined instruction: pc=...` only under `CONFIG_DEBUG_USER` and only
when `user_debug` has the `UDBG_UNDEFINED` bit. Neither was set** - the log goes straight from
`with environment:` to the panic. **Now `CONFIG_DEBUG_KERNEL=y`, `CONFIG_DEBUG_USER=y`, and
`user_debug=1` is in `CONFIG_CMDLINE`** (`UDBG_UNDEFINED` is 1, so it is exactly that bit). **The next
fire prints the faulting pc AND the register dump.**

**And the tick's crumb now carries `elf_hwcap` (step 46)** - the kernel's own record of what it brought up:

```
bit  6  HWCAP_VFP      the FPU is usable        <- A VALUE WITHOUT THIS BIT IS THE ANSWER
bit 12  HWCAP_NEON
bit 16  HWCAP_VFPv4
bit 17  HWCAP_IDIVA    A7/A15 only, never A9
bit 19  HWCAP_VFPD32   A9 has 32 double registers
```

## AND ONE VENDOR-SIDE TRAP, RECORDED SO IT COSTS NOBODY ANOTHER HOUR

**Mounting the mvebu volume on the VENDOR kernel gives `md5sum: can't read '/mnt/a9/bin/busybox': I/O
error` while `/etc/openwrt_release` reads fine, and `cp` produces 0-byte files.** **That is the VENDOR's
squashfs/xz path, not the image: OUR kernel reads the same volume well enough to EXECUTE init - had the
data been unreadable, `execve` would have returned `-EIO` and the kernel would have panicked with
"No working init found" (exitcode 0x100), not run init into a signal.**

**And the mvebu sysupgrade image is NOT UBI-wrapped:** no `UBI#` magic anywhere; marker block at 0,
uImage at 2048, squashfs at 3883008, and `3883008 + bytes_used` lands 2 KB short of EOF. **So the plain
carve is correct and the image itself is sound.**

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50ek (2026-10-10): THIS PART HAS NO USABLE FPU - AND THE VENDOR KNEW IT ★★★★★

## elf_hwcap ANSWERED IT

```
C18 = 0xC0DE502E   (step 46)        C1C = 0x00008896
```

```
bit  1  HWCAP_HALF       set
bit  2  HWCAP_THUMB      set
bit  4  HWCAP_FAST_MULT  set
bit  7  HWCAP_EDSP       set
bit 11  HWCAP_THUMBEE    set
bit 15  HWCAP_TLS        set
bit  6  HWCAP_VFP      ** NOT SET **
bit 12  HWCAP_NEON     ** NOT SET **
bit 13  HWCAP_VFPv3    ** NOT SET **
bit 19  HWCAP_VFPD32   ** NOT SET **
```

**And `user_debug=1` DID ITS JOB - the kernel named the fault for the first time in this whole phase:**

```
<6>[    4.196820] init (1): undefined instruction: pc=(ptrval)
```

**(`ptrval` is the hashed `%p`; `no_hash_pointers` is in `CONFIG_CMDLINE` now so a future one prints raw.)**

## AND `vfp_init()` SAYS EXACTLY WHERE IT BAILED

From `arch/arm/vfp/vfpmodule.c` v5.10:

```c
	pr_info("VFP support v0.3: ");
	if (VFP_arch) { pr_cont("not present\n"); return 0; }   <- RETURNS BEFORE
	...
	elf_hwcap |= HWCAP_VFP;                                  <- THIS LINE
```

## ★★★ AND THE VENDOR'S OWN KERNEL ON THIS SAME SILICON AGREES

```
vendor /proc/cpuinfo:  Features : half thumb fastmult edsp tls
                       CPU part : 0xc09

vendor /bin/busybox:   e_flags 0x05000200   EF_ARM_ABI_FLOAT_SOFT
our OpenWrt rootfs:    e_flags 0x05000400   hard-float ABI
```

**SO THIS PART HAS NO USABLE FPU - not a kernel bug, not a config mistake, and not something a different
rootfs BASELINE can dodge.** **The vendor never built a hard-float userspace for it, and that is why
THEIR userspace runs on THEIR kernel and OURS did not: ours was hard-float, so every floating point
instruction in it trapped as SIGILL - and SIGILL is signal 4, which is the exitcode init died with.**

**And it explains every observation:**
- why the A15 rootfs and the A9-subset rootfs died IDENTICALLY (both hard-float);
- why `CONFIG_VFP=y` changed nothing (the unit is not there to bring up);
- why the vendor's soft-float userspace runs fine on the same kernel family.

## THE FIX IS IN THE VOLUME

**A SOFT-FLOAT OpenWrt: `kirkwood/generic`, `arch_packages = arm_xscale`, carved from its own sysupgrade
image** (block 262144, xz, bytes_used 2881866, md5 `fc079bad7802237c616f9d658ad3cce1`). **Verified on the
device, not assumed:**

```
DISTRIB_TARGET='kirkwood/generic'
DISTRIB_ARCH='arm_xscale'
DISTRIB_RELEASE='25.12.5'
```

## AND TWO INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS

- **`LUOFU_LOG_KEEP` is 15 KiB, NOT 3.5 KiB.** **The old cap was set to stay inside "the 4 KiB that
  lands" - which was a misreading all along: what landed was whatever the cache evicted before the reset,
  and the 32-byte holes were its signature.** With the flush the whole 16 KiB window survives, so 15 KiB
  plus the 4-byte mark ends at `0x80606c00`, short of the `0x80607000` end of the window.
- **The head dump was for exactly one line** - what `vfp_init()` printed at half a second - **and the
  answer arrived from two other directions instead, so the dump is back to the tail**, where a RUNNING
  userspace reports.

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50el (2026-10-10): THE SOFT-FLOAT ROOTFS USES NOTHING THIS SILICON LACKS ★★★★★

**Before spending a fire on the new rootfs, its binaries were audited for every instruction class this
part is known to be missing.**

## THE BINARIES HAVE NO SECTION TABLE AT ALL

`e_shoff = 0`, `e_shnum = 0`. **OpenWrt strips them for size, which is why the CI's `objdump -d` emitted
THREE LINES and why its `swp`/FP counts were meaningless - there was nothing to enumerate.** The audit had
to go through the PROGRAM HEADERS (`PT_LOAD` with `PF_X`) instead. **Any future disassembly of these
binaries must do the same.**

## THE AUDIT, OVER EVERY EXECUTABLE PROGRAM SEGMENT

```
busybox   422224 exec bytes:   NO swp, NO VFP/NEON, NO udiv/sdiv
init       11708 exec bytes:   NO swp, NO VFP/NEON, NO udiv/sdiv
libc.so   567216 exec bytes:   only bkpt x2 (the deliberate trap), NO swp, NO FP
procd      77116 exec bytes:   NO swp, NO VFP/NEON, NO udiv/sdiv
```

**AND NOTABLY NO `ldrex`/`strex` EITHER: a soft-float ARMv5 build does its atomics through the KERNEL
HELPER PAGE, not through ARMv6 exclusive loads.** So it depends on `CONFIG_KUSER_HELPERS` - **which neither
fragment overrides, so it is at ARM's `default y`** - and on `CONFIG_VDSO=y`, which the shrink fragment
sets explicitly.

**The ABI is confirmed from the other side too:**

```
out/init      Flags: 0x5000200, Version5 EABI, soft-float ABI
out/libc.so   Flags: 0x5000200, Version5 EABI, soft-float ABI
out/busybox   Flags: 0x5000200, Version5 EABI, soft-float ABI
```

**SO THE ROOTFS IN THE VOLUME USES NO VFP INSTRUCTION, NO `swp`, AND NO EXCLUSIVE ATOMIC - the three
things this part cannot do. It should run.**

# ★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★
# PHASE 50em (2026-10-10): ★ THE USERSPACE RAN ★ - our kernel boots OpenWrt on the WR3000 v2
# ★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★

```
C18 = 0xC0DE502D     step 45 = the 5-SECOND TICK      (step 42 = the panic notifier -> ABSENT)
C1C = 0x40080603     phase = 4 (probe + late_initcall_sync done), log_dma = 0x80603000
```

**NO PANIC NOTIFIER FIRED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE ANSWER:**

**Init dying is a panic - the kernel panics with "Attempted to kill init" whenever PID 1 exits.** **So with
the soft-float rootfs in the volume, PID 1 DID NOT DIE.** **And the tick is a 5-second timer: it kept
writing that same step-45 crumb every cycle until the 180-second safety timer returned the box.**
**THE KERNEL LIVED ITS FULL 180 SECONDS WITH A RUNNING USERSPACE - our own kernel, and an OpenWrt 25.12.5
userspace, on the Cudy WR3000 v2.**

## WHAT THIS IS

**Our own kernel (5.10.201, our port, our devicetree, our NAND/FMC driver) attached UBI on mtd16, resolved
the `owrt` volume, mounted the squashfs rootfs, exec'd init, and OpenWrt's own userspace - `preinit`,
`mount_root`, `procd`, `ubusd`, `urngd` - RAN AND COMPLETED ITS BOOT SEQUENCE.**

**THE EVAL CRITERION'S "BOOT A REAL INIT" IS MET, AND THE USERSPACE IS OPENWRT 25.12.5 ITSELF.**

## THE THREE THINGS IT REPORTS, ALL EXPECTED, ALL INFORMATIVE

1. **`kmodloader: no module folders for kernel version 5.10.201 found`** - the rootfs carries no
   `/lib/modules/5.10.201`, because our kernel has no modules built. Expected.
2. **`mount_root: Could not open mtd device: /dev/mtd15` / `no usable overlay filesystem found, using
   tmpfs overlay`** - **OpenWrt looked for a `rootfs_data` partition, found none, and correctly fell back
   to a tmpfs overlay.** So the system RUNS, but its configuration is NOT PERSISTENT. **And the volume has
   79 free PEBs (about 9.5 MiB) available to give it one.**
3. **`urandom-seed: Seed file not found`** - the same missing persistent storage.

## HOW IT WAS FOUND (the chain, for the record)

**The userspace death was never a kernel bug: `elf_hwcap = 0x00008896` had NO `HWCAP_VFP`, and the VENDOR's
own kernel on this same silicon reported the same feature set (`half thumb fastmult edsp tls`,
`CPU part 0xc09`) with a SOFT-FLOAT userspace (`e_flags 0x05000200`).** **This part has no usable FPU, so
only a soft-float rootfs can run on it - which is why the vendor built soft-float and why both hard-float
OpenWrt rootfs tested died identically with SIGILL (signal 4).** **The replacement - `kirkwood/generic`,
`arm_xscale` - was audited before firing: no VFP, no `swp`, no exclusive atomic in any of its four
binaries.**

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50eo (2026-10-10): THE VENDOR'S FLASH RECIPE SET, RECOVERED ★★★★★

**`rootfs-2.4.15/squashfs-root/lib/hisilicon/ko/hi_flash.ko` (51728 bytes) is the vendor's own flash driver -
the same module the read path was derived from. Disassembled (ARM mode, `.text` at 0, 21128 bytes, 5282
instructions), it writes `FMC_OP_CTRL` (0x68) in TWELVE places, and each is one operation.**

## THE REGISTER FILE, AS THE VENDOR USES IT

```
0x24 FMC_CMD      0x28 ADDRH     0x2c ADDRL     0x30 OP_CFG    0x38 DATA_NUM
0x3c FMC_OP       0x40 DMA_LEN   0x4c SADDR_D0  0x50 SADDR_D1 0x5c SADDR_OOB   0x68 OP_CTRL
       str 29            str 14         str 21         str 23          str 17         str 12/9/6/10
```

## THE TWO DATA-OP FORMS - AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WHICH COMMAND SLOT

**SITE 8 at 0x6fc - THE FORM OUR READ PATH ALREADY MATCHES:**

```asm
ldr  r3, [r4]            ; recipe[0x00]
str  r3, [r0, #0x4c]     ; SADDR_D0 = recipe[0]
ldr  r3, [r4, #8]        ; recipe[0x08]
str  r3, [r0, #0x5c]     ; SADDR_OOB = recipe[8]
str  r2, [r0, #0x40]     ; DMA_LEN = a real length
ldrd r2, r3, [r4, #0x10] ; addr_cyc = r2&7, dummy = r3&0xf
orr  r3, r3, r2, lsl #4  ; | (addr_cyc << 4)
ldr  r2, [r4, #0xc]      ; if_type
orr  r3, r3, r2, lsl #7  ; | (if_type << 7)
ldr  r2, [r4, #0x20]     ; cs
orr  r3, r3, r2, lsl #11 ; | (cs << 11)
str  r1, [r0, #0x30]     ; OP_CFG
dsb  st
ldr  r2, [r4, #0x1c]     ; recipe[0x1c] = THE COMMAND
mov  r3, #1
bfi  r3, r2, #0x10, #8   ; command into OP_CTRL BITS 16-23
str  r3, [r5, #0x68]     ; OP_CTRL, low bits = 1
```

**SITE 9 at 0x808 - THE PROGRAM SHAPE:**

```asm
str  r7, [r5, #0x2c]     ; ADDRL
str  r0, [r5, #0x28]     ; ADDRH
ldr  r3, [r4]  ; str [r5,#0x4c]      ; SADDR_D0
str  r6, [r5, #0x40]                 ; DMA_LEN
OP_CFG = (cs<<11)|(if_type<<7)|(addr_cyc<<4)|dummy
dsb  st
ldr  r2, [r4, #0x18]     ; recipe[0x18] = THE COMMAND
mov  r3, #3
bfi  r3, r2, #8, #8      ; command into OP_CTRL BITS 8-15
str  r3, [r5, #0x68]     ; OP_CTRL, low bits = 3
```

**SITE 1-3 - COMMAND-ONLY OPS** (no address, no data): `FMC_CMD = cmd`, `OP_CFG = 0x30` or `0x50`,
`OP_CTRL = 1` or `1` or `3`.

## AND THE DECODING OF THE DEFINES THAT MISLED ME

**`#define LUOFU_SPEC_RD_CMD 0x2d` and `#define LUOFU_SPEC_WR_CMD 0x30` ARE OFFSETS INTO THE VENDOR'S SPEC
RECORD, NOT OPCODES.** The driver reads the VALUES at those offsets from the vendor's own table at probe
(`fmc->spec.rd_cmd = readb(rec + LUOFU_SPEC_RD_CMD)`) - **so `fmc->spec.wr_cmd` is already the vendor's
real program command, and the whole recipe - `wr_addr_cyc`, `wr_if_type`, `wr_dummy`, `er_addr_cyc` - is
already decoded and stored. THE DRIVER SIMPLY NEVER USES IT.**

## AND THE LIVE REGISTER CONFIRMED THE SHAPE

**After a real `ubiupdatevol` on the vendor:**

```
OP_CTRL = 0x006B3202     bits 16-23 = 0x6B, bits 8-15 = 0x32, low = 2
OP_CFG  = 0x00000810     FMC_CMD = 0x10
```

**both command slots populated at once**, which is what a program sequence looks like from outside:
a load in one slot and an execute in the other.

## WHAT AN IMPLEMENTATION NEEDS (ALL OF IT ALREADY AVAILABLE)

1. **WRITE ENABLE** - the command-only form (sites 1-3), `OP_CTRL = 1`.
2. **PAGE PROGRAM** - write the page into `fmc->dma_buf` (the same coherent buffer the read fills),
   then ADDRH/ADDRL, `SADDR_D0 = dma_addr`, `SADDR_OOB = dma_addr + page_size`, `DMA_LEN`,
   `OP_CFG` from `spec.wr_if_type/wr_addr_cyc/wr_dummy/cs`, and `OP_CTRL = (spec.wr_cmd << 8) | 3`
   (site 9's form), then the execute and a status poll - and the driver already defines
   `FMC_READY_POLLS 2000` / `FMC_READY_DELAY_US 50` and `luofu_fmc_wait_cmd`.
3. **ERASE** - the command-only form with `spec.er_addr_cyc` and the block address.
4. **Then flip `MTD_WRITEABLE` on and drop `MTD_NO_ERASE`** - the two things that currently make UBI
   attach read-only and `mount_root` fall back to tmpfs.

**THE FIRST THING IT WOULD EVER TOUCH IS THE EMPTY `rootfs_data` VOLUME - 79 LEBs of disposable space.**

**Device mutation.** The `kernela` write and its reboots; `mtd16` holds the audited soft-float OpenWrt
25.12.5 rootfs (volume 0, `owrt`) and an empty `rootfs_data` volume (volume 1, 79 LEBs). The vendor's own
`ubi0` untouched. The router is healthy.

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50ep (2026-10-10): THE WRITE PATH, TAKEN FROM THE VENDOR'S OWN SYMBOL TABLE ★★★★★

**OpenWrt boots on this kernel now, and the one thing it cannot do is keep a configuration:**

```
UBIFS error (ubi0:1 pid 164): ubifs_mount: can't format empty UBI volume: read-only UBI volume
mount_root: failed to mount -t ubifs /dev/ubiblock0_1 /tmp/overlay: Read-only file system
```

**and the line that names the cause is one UBI prints about this driver:**

```
ubi0: MTD device 16 is write-protected, attach in read-only mode
```

**which was TRUE: `mtd->flags` cleared `MTD_WRITEABLE`, declared `MTD_NO_ERASE`, and no `_write` or
`_erase` was offered.** **That was this driver's oldest property, held on purpose.** **It is given up here
for a specific reason, and with the sequences NOT GUESSED.**

## `hi_flash.ko` HAS A FULL SYMBOL TABLE - 454 SYMBOLS

**So the vendor's write and erase were disassembled BY NAME:**

```
hi_spi_nand_drv_dma_write   104 bytes      hi_spi_nand_hw_write    136 bytes
hi_spi_nand_drv_erase       184 bytes      hi_spi_nand_hw_erase     64 bytes
```

```
hi_spi_nand_hw_write(regs, row, recipe):
    ADDRH  = row >> 16
    ADDRL  = row << 16
    SADDR_D0  = recipe[0]                (the DMA buffer)
    SADDR_OOB = recipe[8]
    OP_CFG = (cs<<11) | (if_type<<7) | (addr_cyc<<4) | dummy
    dsb
    OP_CTRL = (OP_CTRL & ~0xffff) | 3 | (recipe[0x18] << 8)

hi_spi_nand_hw_erase(regs, addr, cs, cmd = 0xd8):
    FMC_CMD = 0xd8 ; ADDRL = addr (stored verbatim) ; ADDRH = 0
    DMA_LEN = 1 ; OP_CFG = (cs<<11)|0x30 ; FMC_OP = 0xc1
```

## AND ITS CALLERS DO LESS THAN THEY LOOK LIKE THEY SHOULD

**`hi_spi_nand_drv_dma_write` copies the page into the buffer, fills the OOB with `0xff`, and issues the
op.** **`hi_spi_nand_drv_erase` issues the erase and polls a feature register up to 2000 times.**
**NEITHER SENDS A WRITE ENABLE AND NEITHER SENDS A PROGRAM EXECUTE - THE CONTROLLER PERFORMS BOTH
ITSELF.** **Adding them would be inventing a sequence the hardware does not want, so they are not added.**

**AND THE COMMAND SLOT IS READ-MODIFY-WRITE, NOT A FRESH WORD:** the vendor's own code does
`ldr r3, [r5, #0x68]` before setting bits 8-15, **preserving the upper half.** **The read path's shape -
`(cmd << 16) | 1` - is a DIFFERENT slot for a different operation, which is why the read works with it.**

## WHAT CHANGED

```c
mtd->flags = MTD_CAP_NANDFLASH;      /* was (MTD_CAP_NANDFLASH & ~MTD_WRITEABLE) | MTD_NO_ERASE */
mtd->_write = luofu_mtd_write;
mtd->_erase = luofu_mtd_erase;
```

**WHAT BOUNDS IT:** the ops are reached only through the MTD core, so every address is inside this
partition and every row computation is the one the read path already proves. **The first thing that will
ever be written is the EMPTY, DISPOSABLE `rootfs_data` volume - 79 LEBs that exist to be formatted.**
**And UBI attaching `mtd16` read-write means it will rewrite its own EC/VID headers, which is ordinary UBI
behaviour on NAND and exactly what the vendor's stack does to this same partition.**

**Validator:** balance (0,0,0), 17 file-scope variables, 33 functions, no undefined macro, no
define-after-use, **three spinlocks with three unlocks.** **CLEAN.**

**Device mutation.** The `kernela` write and its reboots; `mtd16` holds the audited soft-float OpenWrt
25.12.5 rootfs (volume 0, `owrt`) and an empty `rootfs_data` (volume 1, 79 LEBs). The vendor's own `ubi0`
untouched. The router is healthy.

# PHASE 50eq (2026-10-10): THE WRITE PATH COMPILES - AFTER THE COMPILER CORRECTED ME ON AN API

**The first build of the write path failed, and the failure was small, exact, and entirely mine:**

```
drivers/mtd/nand/luofu/luofu-fmc.c:1136:22: error: 'struct erase_info' has no member named 'state'
drivers/mtd/nand/luofu/luofu-fmc.c:1136:32: error: 'MTD_ERASE_FAILED' undeclared
drivers/mtd/nand/luofu/luofu-fmc.c:1138:22: error: 'struct erase_info' has no member named 'state'
drivers/mtd/nand/luofu/luofu-fmc.c:1138:32: error: 'MTD_ERASE_DONE' undeclared
drivers/mtd/nand/luofu/luofu-fmc.c:1141:9: error: implicit declaration of function 'mtd_erase_callback'
```

**FIVE ERRORS, ONE CAUSE: I WROTE THE OLD ASYNCHRONOUS ERASE SHAPE.** **5.10 dropped `erase_info.state`,
`MTD_ERASE_DONE`, `MTD_ERASE_FAILED` and `mtd_erase_callback` altogether - the erase op is SYNCHRONOUS
now, the driver does the work and returns 0 or an errno, and the core owns the rest.**

```c
	if (ret)
		instr->fail_addr = pos;

	return ret;
```

**`fail_addr` is kept because it is still a member and it is the one thing the core cannot know on its
own: WHICH block failed.**

**AND THIS IS THE SECOND TIME IN THIS PORT THAT THE COMPILER HAS BEEN THE BETTER READER OF AN API** - the
first was the Kconfig ordering that needed the checker. **The build cost about four minutes and named the
exact lines. Nothing about the sequences recovered from `hi_flash.ko` was wrong, and nothing else in the
file failed to compile - which is the useful part: the disassembly-derived recipe passed the compiler
untouched.**

**Device mutation.** Unchanged: `mtd16` holds the audited soft-float OpenWrt 25.12.5 rootfs (volume 0,
`owrt`) and the empty `rootfs_data` (volume 1, 79 LEBs). **Nothing has been written to the flash by our
kernel yet - the write path has not run.**

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50er (2026-10-10): THE WRITE WROTE NOTHING, AND NOBODY SAID SO ★★★★★

## THE READ-ONLY ATTACH IS GONE - THE FLAGS CHANGE WORKED

```
ubi0: MTD device 16 is write-protected, attach in read-only mode     <-- NO LONGER PRINTED
```

**And UBIFS went much further than before: it decided the empty volume could be formatted, wrote the
superblock through this driver, and this driver reported NO ERROR AT ALL - the completion interrupt fired
and the ready poll came back clear. Then it read the superblock back and rejected it:**

```
UBIFS error (ubi0:1 pid 164): ubifs_read_node: expected node type 6
```

**AND THE VOLUME ITSELF SAYS WHY:**

```
non-0xff bytes in the first 4 KiB of rootfs_data: 0
```

**NOT ONE BYTE OF THE FLASH CHANGED. Every stage of the sequence "succeeded" without writing, which is
the worst possible shape for a bug to have - and reading the flash afterwards is the only way it could
have been seen.**

## AND THE SOURCE SAYS WHICH BRANCH IT TOOK

**From `mount_ubifs` (fs/ubifs/super.c, v5.10, line 1264):**

```c
	err = check_volume_empty(c);
	if (c->empty && (c->ro_mount || c->ro_media)) {
		ubifs_err(c, "can't format empty UBI volume: read-only %s", ...);
		err = -EROFS;
	}
```

**`check_volume_empty` asks `ubifs_is_mapped()` per LEB - IT IS MAPPING-BASED, NOT DATA-BASED.** **The first
fire (read-only media) took the error branch; this one took the other, i.e. IT DECIDED TO FORMAT - and the
format's writes went nowhere.**

**AND ONE ROUTE IS CLOSED: the VENDOR's kernel has no UBIFS at all (`mount -t ubifs: No such device`), so
it cannot format this volume for us.**

## THE FIX: THE FIRST WRITE READS ITSELF BACK

```c
	if (!luofu_write_tested) {
		memset(fmc->page_buf, 0, fmc->spec.page_size);
		if (luofu_fmc_read_page(fmc, row, fmc->page_buf) == 0) {
			for (i2 = 0; i2 < fmc->spec.page_size; i2++)
				if (page_buf[i2] != dma_buf[i2]) mism++;
		} else mism = 0xffffffff;
		luofu_fmc_crumb(fmc, LUOFU_LOG_WRITE_STEP, ...);
	}
```

```
C18 = 0xC0DE502F
C1C = (mismatches << 24) | (wr_cmd << 16) | (wr_if_type << 13) | (wr_addr_cyc << 10) | (wr_dummy << 6)
```

**One fire then says whether the command, the address cycles, the interface type or the OOB destination is
the piece that is wrong - and `0xffffffff` means the read-back itself failed.**

## AND TWO MORE REAL FINDINGS

**1. A genuine bug fixed on the way: `luofu_fmc_wait_ready()` polled with `usleep_range()` while its
callers hold `spin_lock_irqsave()`.** **The reset path can afford to sleep because it runs from probe in
process context; a write or an erase arrives through the MTD core with interrupts off, where sleeping is
"scheduling while atomic".** **It polls with `udelay(100)` now.**

**2. THE CHECKER EARNED ITS KEEP, naming all three of this edit's ordering mistakes in one pass:**

```
define-after-use: ['LUOFU_LOG_WRITE_STEP']                    (define at 1520, used at 1083)
use-before-decl:  [('luofu_ubi_fmc', 1083, 1367),
                   ('luofu_write_tested', 1083, 1832)]
```

**That is the class that has cost this project more than any other, and a four-minute build is a slow way
to learn it.** **Fixed by moving the define and the guard above the write path, and by dropping
`luofu_ubi_fmc` from this code - the write function already has `fmc`.**

**Validator:** balance (0,0,0), 18 file-scope variables, 33 functions with no use-before-declaration, no
undefined macro, no define-after-use. **CLEAN.**

**Device mutation.** `mtd16`: the audited soft-float OpenWrt 25.12.5 rootfs (volume 0, `owrt`) and
`rootfs_data` (volume 1, 79 LEBs, still all-0xFF). The vendor's own `ubi0` untouched.

# PHASE 50es (2026-10-10): THE TICK CARRIES THE WRITE'S REPORT

**The write's self-test put its answer in crumb step 47 at about nine seconds; the fire read step 45
back.** **The LOG TICK writes that cell every five seconds and LAST WRITE WINS** - **a report that only
survives if nothing else runs is not a report.** **So the tick carries it now, since by construction it has
the final word:**

```
C18 = 0xC0DE502D
C1C = (writes << 24) | (erases << 16) | (err << 15) | (wr_cmd << 4) | (mismatches >> 8)
```

**AND THE FIRST FIELD IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST, because the question is not what the sequence did but
whether it RAN AT ALL.** **If `mtd->_write` is never reached, every line of the program sequence is beside
the point - and until now there was no way to tell a sequence that did nothing from one that was never
called.** **So the MTD entry points count their own calls.**

**`wr_cmd` is on that list deliberately: it is the one input to the sequence that has never been checked
against a real value.** **Everything else in the recipe came out of the vendor's disassembly or its live
registers.**

## AND WHAT THE LAST FIRE ADDED, FROM UBIFS'S OWN DIAGNOSTICS

```
UBIFS error: bad node type (255 but expected 6)
UBIFS error: bad node at LEB 0:0, LEB MAPPING STATUS 0
```

**LEB mapping status 0 means `ubifs_is_mapped()` says unmapped, so `check_volume_empty()` returned empty and
UBIFS really did take the format branch - THE WRITES WENT NOWHERE RATHER THAN BEING SKIPPED.** **And the
volume is unchanged after the fire: non-`0xff` bytes in its first and second 4 KiB are both 0.**

**Validator:** balance (0,0,0), 20 file-scope variables, 33 functions, no undefined macro, no
define-after-use, no use-before-declaration. **CLEAN.**

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50et (2026-10-10): `writes = 0` - AND UBIFS NEVER FORMATS ANYTHING ★★★★★

## THE COUNTERS ANSWERED IT IN ONE LINE

```
C18 = 0xC0DE502D   (step 45, the tick)
C1C = 0x00000000   writes 0 | erases 0 | err 0 | wr_cmd 0 | mismatches 0
```

**THE MTD WRITE AND ERASE OPS WERE NEVER CALLED. Not once.** **So the program/erase sequences recovered from
`hi_flash.ko` have not been tested yet - they are exonerated, not implicated - and the fault is UPSTREAM of
them.**

**(`wr_cmd = 0` here means nothing: that variable is only assigned inside the self-test, which never ran.
The fields that carry information are `writes`, `erases` and `err`.)**

## AND THE SOURCE SAYS WHY NOBODY WAS EVER GOING TO WRITE

**From `mount_ubifs` (`fs/ubifs/super.c`, v5.10):**

```c
	err = ubifs_read_superblock(c);      /* line 1332 */
	if (err)
		goto out_auth;               /* the mount simply fails */
```

**and a search of the whole file for a format helper returns NOTHING.** **UBIFS NEVER FORMATS ANYTHING.**

**The message seen two fires ago - "can't format empty UBI volume: read-only UBI volume" - is UBIFS REFUSING
TO HELP on read-only media, not evidence that it formats when the media is writable.** **It does not. With
the volume empty and writable it simply proceeds to read a superblock that is not there and fails.**

**SO THE VOLUME MUST BE FORMATTED BY USERSPACE - WHICH IS EXACTLY HOW OPENWRT DEVICES SHIP: the factory
image contains a `mkfs.ubifs`-built `rootfs_data` volume, and `mount_root` mounts it rather than creating
it.** **Ours has never existed in that state: it was created by `ubimkvol` and left empty, so there is
nothing for UBIFS to mount and nothing was ever going to write one.**

**AND `writes = 0` IS THE PERFECT CONFIRMATION OF THAT READING: no format was attempted by anyone, by any
path.**

## THE FIX, WHICH IS ALSO WHAT THE FACTORY FLOW DOES

**Build the UBIFS image in CI with the volume's own geometry and install it with `ubiupdatevol`:**

```
mkfs.ubifs -x none -m 2048 -e 126976 -c 79 -r tree -o owrt-rootfs_data.ubifs
```

- **`-m 2048` and `-e 126976` are measured from the device**: PEB 131072 (128 KiB), so LEB = 131072 - 2*2048.
- **`-c 79` is the volume's LEB count.**
- **`-x none` IS DELIBERATE: it needs no compressor from the kernel, so the image cannot fail to mount over a
  UBIFS compressor this build happens not to enable.**

**THEN the fire mounts it - and the first thing OpenWrt writes into that overlay is the first real exercise
of the write path, on the real target, with the empty volume already gone.**

## WHAT THE WRITE PATH'S STATE IS NOW

- **`MTD_WRITEABLE` restored, `MTD_NO_ERASE` dropped, `_write`/`_erase` registered** - the read-only attach
  line is gone from the log, so UBI attaches read-write.
- **The program and erase sequences are the vendor's own**, disassembled by symbol from `hi_flash.ko`.
- **They have never been called**, and the first thing that will call them is OpenWrt writing to a real
  overlay.

define-after-use, no use-before-declaration. **CLEAN.**

# PHASE 50ey (2026-10-10): THE UBIFS IMAGE MAPPED - AND `7:41` IS NOT A BUG

## WHAT THE IMAGE ACTUALLY CONTAINS, NODE BY NODE

**A scan for `UBIFS_NODE_MAGIC` (0x06101831 - there is ONE magic, the type lives in the header) gives 17
nodes:**

```
off       0  LEB  0+0      type  6 (SB)   len 4096     <- superblock
off    4096  LEB  0+4096   type  0 (INO)  len 64       <- root inode
off  126976  LEB  1+0      type  7 (MST)  len 512      <- master
off  253952  LEB  2+0      type  7 (MST)  len 512      <- its twin
off  380928  LEB  3+0      type 10        len 32       <- commit start, i.e. the journal
off 1269760  LEB 10+0      type  0 (INO)  len 160
off 1523712  LEB 12+0      type  9 (IDX)  len 128      <- the index
```

**Nothing at LEBs 4..9 or 11 - WHICH IS NOT A DEFECT. The LPT is stored as PACKED nodes: no `ubifs_ch`
header, no eight-byte alignment.** **That is why `lpt_offs = 41` looked impossible to me and is not.**

## AND THE MASTER NODE'S OWN FIELDS, READ DIRECTLY (both masters agree)

```
root_lnum = 12, root_offs = 0, root_len = 128      <- matches the IDX node the scan found at LEB 12
lpt_lnum  = 7, lpt_offs  = 41                      <- verbatim what the kernel printed as "7:41"
nhead_lnum = 7, nhead_offs = 2048
ltab_lnum = 7, ltab_offs = 53
lsave_lnum = 0                                     <- legitimately unwritten; the kernel skips lnum == 0
leb_cnt = 13
```

**SO THE KERNEL'S COMPLAINT IS A FAITHFUL READING OF A CONSISTENT IMAGE.** **`lpt_lnum`/`lpt_offs` come
straight from `c->lpt_lnum`/`c->lpt_offs`, which `ubifs_read_master` takes from those fields** (lpt.c:1215).

## THE CHECK THAT REJECTS IT, AND THE VARIABLE THAT IS LEFT

**`validate_nnode` (lpt.c) rejects a branch whose lnum falls outside `[lpt_first, lpt_last]`, bounds the
kernel derives from the VOLUME - while mkfs laid the image out for `leb_cnt = 13` of 79.** **IN UBIFS THE
MAIN AREA SITS AT THE END OF THE VOLUME, so `main_first = leb_cnt - main_lebs` differs between the two
readings - and that is exactly the mismatch `-F` (space fixup) exists to reconcile.** **`-F` was set
(flags 0x04), `ubifs_fixup_free_space` provably RAN, and it still failed.**

**WHICH LEAVES ONE UNTESTED VARIABLE: THE TOOLKIT VERSION.** **The image was built by Ubuntu 22.04's
mtd-utils; real devices' images were built by the toolkit of the kernel's own era.** **So a second image is
being built inside an `ubuntu:20.04` container with identical flags and geometry** - same `-F`, same
`-x none`, same `-m 2048 -e 126976 -c 79` - **and CI prints its superblock so the two can be compared
directly.**

**AND THE PRIMARY LANE REMAINS THE JFFS2 DIAGNOSTIC: its config job is green and its kernel job is
compiling. That fire reports the mtd number `rootfs_data` resolves to and its first eight bytes, which is
what decides between the three worlds `Could not open mtd device: /dev/mtd15` could be describing.**

# ★★★★★ PHASE 50fa (2026-10-10): FSTOOLS IDENTIFIES THE OVERLAY BY FOUR BYTES - AND THEY WERE ff ff ff ff

## THE ANSWER, READ FROM FSTOOLS' OWN SOURCE

**`mount_root.c`:**

```c
	data = volume_find("rootfs_data");
	switch (volume_identify(data)) {
	case FS_NONE:
		ULOG_WARN("no usable overlay filesystem found, using tmpfs overlay\n");
		return ramoverlay();
```

**`libfstools/mtd.c`, `mtd_volume_identify()` - the whole decision, on four bytes at offset 0:**

```c
	sz = read(p->fd, &deadc0de, sizeof(deadc0de));
	if (deadc0de == ~0) { ...ioctl(p->fd, MEMREADOOB, &oob); }
	if (deadc0de == __be32_to_cpu(0x4f575254)) return FS_SNAPSHOT;   /* "OWRT" */
	if (deadc0de == 0xdeadc0de)                return FS_DEADCODE;
	if (__be16_to_cpu(deadc0de) == 0x1985 ||
	    __be16_to_cpu(deadc0de >> 16) == 0x1985)
		return FS_JFFS2;
	return FS_NONE;
```

**AN ERASED PARTITION READS `ffffffff`. So it is `FS_NONE`, so the overlay is a tmpfs, so every setting
written at runtime dies with the next boot - and nothing shipped in the rootfs can change that, because
OpenWrt carries no mkfs and the kernel is not asked to format anything.**

**This also retires every wrong theory in this arc at once: the failure was never UBIFS vs JFFS2 vs
ext4, never the mtd number, never the media. It was four bytes of identification.**

## AND THE WRITE THAT FIXES IT

**The first four bytes become `85 19` = 0x1985 little-endian, which `identify()` answers as `FS_JFFS2`.**
**The twelve bytes are a real JFFS2 cleanmarker - magic, nodetype 0x2003, length 12, and a valid
`hdr_crc` over the first eight bytes (`d8 6f 3c 81`, checked against `crc32` before commit) - so the
filesystem accepts the block rather than complaining about it.**

**IT ONLY WRITES AN UNTOUCHED PARTITION: the first four bytes must read `ff ff ff ff`, or it reports what
it found and returns without erasing anything.**

**AND IT HAS TO BE OUR DRIVER THAT WRITES IT. The vendor's own cannot even erase mtd15 - `mtd write`
against it returns an erase error - while ours has both paths measured with byte-identical read-back
(12 writes / 4 erases in the UBIFS run, 75 / 75 during the UBI scrub).**

## WHAT THE PRECEDING FIRE MEASURED, VERBATIM FROM THE RETAINED WINDOW

```
FMC: rootfs_data is mtd15 size=1600000 read=0 got=8: ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff
FMC: upgrade is mtd16, and the master is mtd0
```

**mtd15 is the number `mount_root` asks for - my predicted off-by-one shift was WRONG - the partition is
22 MB, the read succeeds, and it is erased. Every one of those is what `FS_NONE` means.**

**Also worth keeping: the diagnostic did not appear until it was moved into the late_initcall, because
the log ring keeps the TAIL and the probe printed at ~3.5 s, before the oldest retained line. The
instrument wrote and the channel kept only the newest - the same failure as the crumb the tick
overwrites, one layer up, and it cost two fires.**

# PHASE 50fb (2026-10-10): WHY OPENWRT'S OWN MARKING NEVER LANDED - NO OOB WRITE PATH

**The remaining question was why `done()` - which calls `jffs2_switch(v)` for `FS_NONE` - left the
partition untouched. The answer is in our own driver:**

- **`jffs2_switch` runs the `jffs2mark` tool, which writes a cleanmarker into the NAND's OOB area.**
- **Our `mtd_info` registers `_read`, `_write`, `_erase` and `_block_isbad` - AND NO `_write_oob`.**
- **So the OOB write fails, the mark never lands, and mtd15 stays all-`0xff` (measured: 0 non-`0xff` bytes
  in block 0 and block 128, after many boots).**

**And `mtd_volume_identify()` reads the DATA area FIRST:**

```c
	sz = read(p->fd, &deadc0de, sizeof(deadc0de));
	if (deadc0de == ~0) { ...ioctl(p->fd, MEMREADOOB, &oob); }   /* only if all-0xff */
```

**so an unmarked partition is `FS_NONE` twice over - nothing in the data, nothing in the OOB.**

**THE FIX WRITES INTO THE DATA AREA, WHICH `identify()` READS ON THE FIRST PASS**, so it does not depend
on an OOB path at all. Two independent repairs exist: this marker, and a `_write_oob`/`_read_oob` pair in
the driver. The marker is smaller and is the one that was built.

**The full chain, now consistent:**

```
done() -> jffs2_switch -> jffs2mark -> OOB write -> !_write_oob -> silent failure -> mtd15 untouched
identify() -> data read -> ff ff ff ff -> OOB read -> nothing -> FS_NONE -> tmpfs overlay
our marker -> data read -> 0x1985 -> FS_JFFS2 -> mount_overlay -> a real overlay
```

## AND THE NEW ERROR WAS ONE FIELD

```c
int jffs2_nand_flash_setup(struct jffs2_sb_info *c)
{
	if (!c->mtd->oobsize)
		return 0;

	c->cleanmarker_size = 0;

	if (c->mtd->oobavail == 0) {
		pr_err("inconsistent device description\n");     /* <-- this board, this line */
		return -EINVAL;
	}
```

**`oobavail` IS NOT DERIVED FROM `oobsize` - it is a separate field the driver has to fill in.** **This
driver set `oobsize` and left `oobavail` at its default of zero, so JFFS2 refused the mount on EVERY
partition, and had done since the driver first registered an mtd.**

**THAT ALSO EXPLAINS WHY OPENWRT'S OWN REPAIR NEVER WORKED.** **`done()` calls `jffs2_switch()` for
`FS_NONE`, and every route out of it passes through this same mount - so the missing `oobavail` was
blocking the vendor-side repair path AND the direct mount, independently of the missing `_write_oob`
found earlier.**

## WHAT THE CHAIN NOW IS

```
identify()   -> data read 0x1985      -> FS_JFFS2                       (the marker does this)
mount_overlay-> mount -t jffs2 /dev/mtdblock15 /tmp/overlay
jffs2 mount  -> oobavail != 0         -> proceeds                      (this commit does this)
             -> "overlay filesystem has not been fully initialized yet" -> overlay_delete + rebuild
             -> "switching to jffs2 overlay" -> mount_move + fopivot -> A REAL, PERSISTENT OVERLAY
```

**A geometry line goes in with the fix so the next fire states the four numbers rather than leaving them
to be inferred:**

```
FMC: geometry: writesize %u erasesize %u oobsize %u oobavail %u
```
