# PHASE 50fd (2026-10-10): THE MARKER WAS WRITTEN, AND JFFS2 ASKED FOR THE OOB NEXT

## TWO FIXES LANDED AT ONCE, AND THE ERROR MOVED WITH EACH

```
FMC: rootfs_data is mtd15 size=1600000 read=0 got=8: ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff
FMC: geometry: writesize 2048 erasesize 131072 oobsize 64 oobavail 64
FMC: wrote the jffs2 marker; read back 0x20031985 (identifies as FS_JFFS2)
jffs2: cannot read OOB for EB at 00000000, requested 8 bytes, read 0 bytes, error -95
mount_root: failed to mount -t jffs2 /dev/mtdblock15 /tmp/overlay: I/O error
```

**The `oobavail` line is visible and correct, the marker was written and read back as `0x20031985`, and
the mount now reaches JFFS2 itself. `-95` is `-EOPNOTSUPP` - this driver registers no `_read_oob`, and
JFFS2 wants its cleanmarker from the spare area.**

## THE WAY OUT IS THREE LINES OF JFFS2'S OWN CODE

```c
int jffs2_nand_flash_setup(struct jffs2_sb_info *c)
{
	if (!c->mtd->oobsize)
		return 0;
```

**A device that declares no OOB is mounted the ordinary way, with the cleanmarker IN BAND - and the
twelve bytes already being written are exactly that, a `struct jffs2_unknown_node` with a valid
`hdr_crc`. So the partition declares `oobsize = 0`, and no OOB implementation is needed at all.**

**IT IS SET ON THE PARTITION AND NOT ON THE MASTER, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT: `mtd16` keeps the real
geometry, so UBI's attach - which carries the rootfs that already mounts and boots - cannot be disturbed
by a change made for the overlay's benefit. `rootfs_data` is the only mtd that says `oobsize 0`, and it
is the only one JFFS2 is asked to mount.**

## AND ONE OBSERVATION WORTH KEEPING FROM THIS FIRE

**`rootfs_data` read `ff ff ff ff` at 4.56 s even though the previous fire had written a marker into it
and reported "already carries 0x20031985".** **Something erased that block between the two boots** - most
plausibly the failed JFFS2 mount itself, which is known to erase blocks it cannot use. **It does not
change the sequence (the marker is rewritten whenever the first four bytes are `ff`), but it does mean
the marker is not assumed to persist across a failed mount.**


---

# PHASE 50fe (2026-10-10): JFFS2 SCANS THE PARTITION - A WRONG CRC FLAVOUR AND 1.5 MB OF LEFTOVER DATA

**Reaching JFFS2's scanner at all is the progress: the OOB-less declaration did its job and the mount is
now inside the filesystem instead of being refused by its geometry.**

```
FMC: wrote the jffs2 marker; read back 0x20031985 (identifies as FS_JFFS2)
jffs2: jffs2_scan_eraseblock(): Node at 0x00000000 {0x1985, 0x2003, 0x0000000c)
      has invalid CRC 0x813c6fd8 (calculated 0xe41eb0b1)
jffs2: Magic bitmask 0x1985 not found at 0x00000004: 0x000c instead
jffs2: Incompatible feature node (0xe009) found at offset 0x00181758
mount_root: failed to mount -t jffs2 /dev/mtdblock15 /tmp/overlay: I/O error
```

## FAULT ONE, AND IT WAS MINE: THE KERNEL'S crc32 IS NOT zlib's

**Checked against JFFS2's own printed number rather than guessed:**

```
zlib.crc32(header, 0xffffffff) ^ 0xffffffff  ==  0xe41eb0b1      <- exactly what jffs2 calculated
```

**init ~0 with no final complement. The four bytes are `b1 b0 1e e4`.**

## FAULT TWO, AND IT WAS THE PARTITION'S: DATA AT 1.5 MB

**`Incompatible feature node (0xe009) found at offset 0x00181758` is what actually stops the mount.**
**`mtd15` had only ever been probed at block 0 and block 128, where it is erased - it is NOT erased
everywhere.** **A partition clean at the start and carrying junk further in has never held a filesystem,
and JFFS2 will not adopt it.**

## SO THE WHOLE PARTITION IS ERASED BEFORE MARKING - AND THE GUARD IS WHAT MAKES THAT SAFE

**The erase runs only behind the existing check that the first four bytes read `ff ff ff ff`, and a
filesystem that has ever been mounted writes block 0. So the destructive path is UNREACHABLE for a live
overlay and cannot eat user data on a later boot, while a never-formatted partition gets the clean slate
JFFS2 requires.**

**This is the third distinct obstacle found and removed in three consecutive fires, each one revealed
only after the previous was cleared: `oobavail` zero -> JFFS2 refused the device; no OOB ops -> JFFS2
refused the cleanmarker path; wrong CRC and 1.5 MB of junk -> JFFS2 refused the scan.**


## AND THE BUILD CAUGHT THE SAME CLASS AGAIN: `__aeabi_uldivmod` (2026-10-10)

```
arm-linux-gnueabihf-ld: drivers/mtd/nand/luofu/luofu-fmc.o: in function `luofu_fmc_ubi_probe':
luofu-fmc.c:(.init.text+0x30c): undefined reference to `__aeabi_uldivmod'
```

**`part->size` is a 64-bit `loff_t` and `part->erasesize` is 32-bit, so the erase loop's block count
pulled in libgcc's 64-bit divide - and the kernel does not link libgcc.** **`div_u64()` is the kernel's
own divider for a 64-by-32 unsigned quotient, and the count is now computed once before the loop.**

**THIS IS THE SECOND TIME THIS EXACT CLASS HAS COST A BUILD** - the first was `__aeabi_ldivmod` from a
64-bit modulo in the mtd write path, fixed with `div_u64_rem`. **Both times the compiler was the reader
and I was not.** **The check applied this time was the class rather than the instance: every remaining
division in the function was walked, and no other 64-bit operator division is left in the new code.**


## PHASE 50ff (2026-10-10): THE ERASE WAS A NO-OP - WRONG ADDRESS ENCODING

```
FMC: erased 176 blocks of rootfs_data before marking it
FMC: wrote the jffs2 marker; read back 0x20031985
jffs2: Incompatible feature node (0xe009) found at offset 0x00181758     <- THE SAME JUNK
```

**176 erase commands were accepted and changed nothing.** **The partition was byte-identical after a
whole-partition erase - the same node at the same offset that JFFS2 has refused from the start.**

**THE CAUSE WAS AN ENCODING I HAD ALREADY READ ONCE AND DID NOT APPLY:**

```
hi_spi_nand_hw_erase(regs, addr, cs, cmd):  ADDRH = 0 ; ADDRL = addr   (VERBATIM)
```

**while the WRITE path does `ADDRH = row >> 16; ADDRL = row << 16`. THE TWO OPS DO NOT SHARE AN ADDRESS
ENCODING, and this driver copied the write's shift into the erase - so every erase carried its address in
the wrong half of the register.** **`ADDRH = 0` is consistent with a page row: a 128 KiB block is 64
pages and the device has about 15,104 of them, inside a 16-bit field.**

**IT LIVED THIS LONG BECAUSE ONLY THE WRITE PATH WAS EVER MEASURED.** **`mism` counts how many bytes a
page differs by after programming - it certifies writes and says nothing whatsoever about erases - and
because the two paths shared a divisor they looked like one code path.**

**SO AN ERASE IS NOW READ BACK BEFORE IT IS TRUSTED**, which is the check whose absence let this survive:

```
FMC: after the erase, rootfs_data begins 0x%08x (erased / STILL HOLDS DATA)
```

**An erase cannot be verified by its own return value, so it is verified by reading the flash afterwards -
the same discipline the write path already uses.**

**(A first attempt at this fix also changed the divisor to `erasesize`; that part was wrong, because the
row is a page row matching `ADDRH = 0`, and it was reverted before the commit.)**


## PHASE 50fg (2026-10-10): THE ERASE ADDRESS IS A BLOCK NUMBER - AND BLOCK 0 HID IT

```
FMC: erased 176 blocks of rootfs_data before marking it
FMC: after the erase, rootfs_data begins 0xffffffff (erased)          <- the erase works now
FMC: wrote the jffs2 marker; read back 0x20031985 (identifies as FS_JFFS2)
jffs2: Incompatible feature node (0xe009) found at offset 0x00621798   <- 6.4 MB; the last fire said 1.5 MB
```

**THE OFFSET MOVING IS THE TELL.** **The unerased region is not a fixed piece of flash - it is wherever
the loop failed to reach, so blocks 1..175 were never touched.**

**AND BLOCK 0 IS WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE.** **It is the one address where a page row and a block number are
the SAME VALUE**, so it erases correctly under either convention, and a read-back that samples only the
start of the partition reports `erased` while the other 175 blocks keep everything.

**SO BOTH CHANGES WERE NEEDED, NOT EITHER: the erase address is the block index (`pos / erasesize`) AND
it is stored verbatim with `ADDRH = 0`.** **The previous commit reverted the divisor and kept the
unshifting - it fixed the half block 0 could not distinguish.** **`ADDRH = 0` is consistent with a block
index on this part: 176 blocks, comfortably inside 16 bits.**

**AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS FIXED TOO, because an instrument that cannot fail for the right reason is worse
than none:**

```
FMC: after the erase, block 0 of 176 begins 0xffffffff (erased)
FMC: after the erase, block 175 of 176 begins 0xffffffff (erased)
```

**Sampling both ends is the difference between a check and a formality. The write path is untouched and
still page-addressed with the shift - which is exactly what makes the marker read back correctly, and
confirms the two ops genuinely do not share an encoding.**


## PHASE 50fh (2026-10-10): A READ-BACK OF ERASED FLASH PROVES NOTHING

```
FMC: after the erase, block 0 of 175 begins 0xffffffff (erased)
FMC: after the erase, block 175 of 175 begins 0xffffffff (erased)
jffs2: Incompatible feature node (0xe009) found at offset 0x00321bc8
```

**BOTH ENDS READ `ff`, AND THE CHECK WAS VACUOUS: the partition was already erased at every address
sampled, so it could not have failed whatever the erase did.** **It was an improvement on sampling one
block and still not an instrument.**

**And JFFS2 gave a THIRD offset - `0x00181758`, then `0x00621798`, now `0x00321bc8`.** **An offset that
moves with each boot is not a fixed piece of bad flash, and a check that reads erased data cannot
distinguish "the erase still misses blocks" from "something else is being read as a node".**

**SO THE ERASE IS NOW PROVEN THE ONLY WAY IT CAN BE - WRITE FIRST, THEN ERASE:**

```
FMC: erase self-test: block 175 planted as 0x5a5a5a5a
FMC: erase self-test: block 175 reads 0xffffffff after erasing it (ERASE WORKS)
                         ... or 0x5a5a5a5a (ERASE DID NOTHING)
```

**A page of `0x5a` is written into the last block, read back to confirm it landed, the block is erased
through the same path, and read again.** **The last block is chosen deliberately: it is the furthest
address from the one the old page-row encoding got right by accident, so it fails loudly if the
addressing is still wrong.**

**It sits behind the same guard as everything else - the first four bytes must read `ff` - so it only
ever touches a partition that has never held a filesystem, and it runs before the marker so the partition
ends fully erased either way.**

**THE LESSON, WHICH IS THE PROJECT'S OLDEST ONE IN A NEW COAT: an instrument must be able to fail for the
reason being tested.** **Reading erased flash to test an erase cannot fail, exactly as a crumb that a
later writer overwrites cannot report, and as a probe that prints before the log's retention point cannot
be read.**


## PHASE 50fi (2026-10-10): THE SELF-TEST SETTLED THE ERASE ENCODING

```
FMC: erase self-test: block 175 planted as 0x00000000
FMC: erase self-test: block 175 reads 0x5a5a5a5a after erasing it (ERASE DID NOTHING)
```

**The pattern was on the flash - the same address returned two different values on two consecutive reads -
so the write landed and the erase left it there.** **Block 175 is the only place that can show this; block
0 is address 0 under every encoding, which is why five fires of judging by block 0 said nothing.**

**THREE ENCODINGS HAVE NOW BEEN RUN AGAINST A KNOWN PATTERN, AND ONLY ONE DID ANYTHING:**

| encoding | result |
|---|---|
| page row, shifted (`row << 16`) | partition byte-identical - nothing erased |
| **page row, unshifted (`row`)** | **JFFS2's complaint MOVED - erasing happened** |
| block index, unshifted (`pos / erasesize`) | `ERASE DID NOTHING` on a planted pattern |

**The middle row is what this commit restores: the page row of the block's first page, stored verbatim.**
**It is also what the vendor's wrapper does - `ADDRH = 0 ; ADDRL = addr` verbatim - and `ADDRH = 0` fits
a page row here: 15,104 pages, inside 16 bits.**

**SO THE ERASE AND THE WRITE DIFFER BY EXACTLY THE SHIFT AND NOTHING ELSE**, which is what the driver
looked like one commit before the divisor was moved - and that move was made on a reading of block 0 that
could not distinguish the encodings. **The self-test is what actually decided it, and it stays in the
build so the next fire confirms rather than assumes.**

**Two fires were spent on wrong encodings because the instrument could not fail. The instrument that
could fail answered in one.**


## PHASE 50fj (2026-10-10): THE SELF-TEST'S OWN FIRST READ WAS THE ANOMALY

```
FMC: erase self-test: block 175 planted as 0x00000000
FMC: erase self-test: block 175 reads 0x5a5a5a5a after erasing it (ERASE DID NOTHING)
```

**Zeros are neither what was written (`0x5a`) nor what erased flash reads (`0xff`) - they are the DMA
buffer's initial contents, so that read did not happen and reported no error. The next read at the same
address returned the pattern. The read path is unreliable at row 11,200, and a verdict resting on that read
is worth nothing.**

**AND EVERY "NOTHING WAS ERASED" CONCLUSION IN THIS ARC HAS BEEN READ AT A BLOCK WHERE THE READ PATH WAS
NEVER SEPARATELY PROVEN.** **The reads that do work - every boot, through squashfs - are in the first few
megabytes of mtd16.** **Row 11,200 is far outside anything exercised before.**

**SO THE PROBE NOW COVERS THREE BLOCKS, EACH CHOSEN FOR WHAT IT CAN SHOW:**

| block | why |
|---|---|
| 1 | low, where the rootfs proves the read path every boot |
| 25 | exactly where JFFS2 complains (`0x00321bc8`) - the block in dispute |
| `nblocks - 1` | the far end, the one that caught the address encoding |

**Each is planted with its own byte pattern, read back, erased, and read again - and the read-back reports
THREE outcomes rather than two, because "read returned ZEROS" is a third thing and it is the one that has
been misleading me:**

```
planted 0x5a5a5a5a, read back ...   matches / DOES NOT MATCH
reads ... after erasing             ERASE WORKS / ERASE DID NOTHING / read returned ZEROS
```

**An instrument that reports only the two answers I expected cannot tell me when it is broken.**


## PHASE 50fk (2026-10-10): JFFS2 READ BACK MY PLANTED PATTERN

```
jffs2: Magic bitmask 0x1985 not found at 0x00020000: 0x5a5a instead
```

**`0x00020000` is block 1; `0x5a5a` is exactly what the self-test wrote there.** **Three facts from one
line, read out by a witness I did not build: the WRITE works at block 1, the READ is reliable there, and
the ERASE left the pattern in place.**

**AND MY SELF-TEST'S OWN LINES WERE BEING DROWNED.** **JFFS2 logs a line per 16 bytes of every block it
dislikes - thousands of lines - and the log ring keeps the TAIL, so the measurement was pushed out of the
window by the very problem it was measuring.** **So the verdicts now ride the CRUMB, the one channel proven
to survive:**

```
C1C = (writes << 24) | (erases << 16) | (err << 15) | (luofu_e_test << 3) | (mism & 7)
      luofu_e_test = (t1 << 8) | (t25 << 4) | (tlast)
```

**one nibble per probe block - 1 ERASE WORKS, 2 ERASE DID NOTHING, 3 read returned zeros, 4 read failed,
6 the plant did not read back - so "the erase is broken" and "the read path is broken" are distinguishable
answers rather than one ambiguous one.**

**AND THE ERASE GOES BACK TO A BLOCK NUMBER (`pos / erasesize`), THE ENCODING THAT HAS NOT ACTUALLY BEEN
DISPROVEN.** **The page-row run is the one JFFS2 just refuted on a planted pattern; the block-number run was
judged by a read at block 175 that returned zeros - a read since established as not evidence.** **Three
encodings tried, and only one has been tested against a pattern it could fail on.**


## ★★★★★ PHASE 50fl (2026-10-10): THE MISSING WRITE ENABLE - WHY EVERY ERASE DID NOTHING

**The relocation table named it. The call sites in `hi_spi_nand_drv_erase` decode as `0xebfffffe` -
placeholders patched at load time - so the disassembly could not show the target and `.rel.text` could:**

```
hi_spi_nand_drv_erase(dev, addr):
    hi_fmc_write_reg_en(regs)               <-- MISSING FROM THIS DRIVER
    hi_spi_nand_hw_erase(regs, addr, cs, 0xd8)
    hi_fmc_status_check(regs)
```

**And its body is explicit:**

```
r7 = (*regs >> 5) & 7            save the three interface bits
*regs = (*regs & ~(7 << 5))
*(regs + 0x24) = 0x06            FMC_CMD = WRITE ENABLE
*(regs + 0x3c) = 0x81            FMC_OP  = SEND COMMAND
poll (regs + 0x3c) & 1           bounded, delay between reads
*regs |= r7 << 5                 restore
```

**A CHIP THAT HAS NOT BEEN WRITE-ENABLED REFUSES THE FOLLOWING BLOCK ERASE, AND THE CONTROLLER REPORTS NO
ERROR FOR IT.** **That is precisely what three address encodings looked like from outside - a command
accepted and a partition byte-identical afterwards - and it is why the self-test said `ERASE DID NOTHING`
whatever went into `ADDRL`. THE ADDRESS WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM.**

**AND THE HARDWARE SEQUENCE IS OTHERWISE IDENTICAL TO OURS.** **`hi_spi_nand_hw_erase`, decoded in full:
`ADDRL = addr` verbatim, `ADDRH = 0`, `CMD = 0xd8`, `DMA_LEN = 1`, `OP_CFG = (cs<<11)|0x30`, `OP = 0xc1`.**

**SO THE ADDRESS GOES BACK TO A PAGE ROW** (`pos / writesize`) - the encoding the vendor's own mtd erase
derives with a shift, and the one whose run showed JFFS2's complaint **moving**. **The block-number verdict
came from an erase with no write enable behind it, so it was never a test of the address at all.**

**THE PROGRAM PATH NEEDS NO EQUIVALENT - its command carries the enable itself - which is why the marker
has always written correctly while nothing was ever erased.** **And JFFS2 reading the planted `0x5a5a` back
off block 1 is what proved it.**


## ★★★★★ PHASE 50fm (2026-10-10): ERASE WORKS - AND A RACE ATE PART OF THE PARTITION

```
C1C = 0x4FFE0888   writes 79 | erases 254 | err 0
  block 1    : ERASE WORKS
  block 25   : ERASE WORKS
  last block : ERASE WORKS
```

**THE WRITE ENABLE WAS THE ERASE'S WHOLE PROBLEM.** **Everything tried before it was address guesswork
against a chip that was refusing the command anyway - three encodings, five fires, all of them measuring a
chip that had never been told the erase was coming.**

**BUT A WHOLE-PARTITION ERASE STILL LEFT ~500 KB BEHIND, AND THE VENDOR'S OWN DRIVER SAYS THE DATA IS REAL
RATHER THAN A READ ARTIFACT:**

```
offset 0x4595e4    32 non-ff bytes      offset 0x321bc8    0 non-ff
offset 0x00621798  32 non-ff bytes      offset 0x181758    0 non-ff
first 8 MiB        521,750 non-ff bytes
```

**and sampling every eighth block found only block 96 dirty** - **a scattering, at a DIFFERENT set each
boot, which is exactly how it presented from outside: JFFS2 naming a new offset every time.**

**THE CAUSE IS A RACE THE LOOP CANNOT SEE.** **176 erase commands are issued back to back, each carrying a
single WRITE ENABLE, and any block still busy when the next command arrives loses its erase.** **The
three-block self-test could never expose it - each of its erases is separated by a read and a fresh write
enable.**

**SO EVERY BLOCK IS NOW VERIFIED AND RE-ERASED IF IT DID NOT TAKE, up to three tries, with the count that
needed a second pass reported.** **The check is the same one the self-test uses, so the loop proves itself
rather than trusting its own return value - which is the discipline this whole arc has been teaching.**

# PHASE 50fn (2026-10-10): THE BOARD IS STRANDED - WHAT IS READY, AND THE HAZARD I INTRODUCED

## THE BOX

**Booted into our kernel and stuck there: the Ethernet link is down (our kernel has no network driver,
so a down link is what our kernel looks like), ssh and ping both time out, and a plain power cycle did not
clear it.** **The last fire's watcher timed out mid-cycle, so the fire never reached its own revert of the
boot selector.**

**The recovery door is ARMED and proven working:**

- host alias `192.168.1.88` on the Ethernet interface - still present from a previous session
- a TFTP read server on `0.0.0.0:69` (**PID 23916 - the ORIGINAL one, which survived its cell being
  killed; the "restart" I attempted never started and wrote no log**)
- served file `build/tmp/recovery/recovery.bin` = the genuine 2.4.15 (20,975,775 bytes)
- **`tools/tftp_server.py` is a WRITE receiver and cannot serve this: the u-boot sends an RRQ and needs a
  reader, which is why `build/tmp/tftp_read_server.py` exists**

**AND IT HAS FETCHED ONCE:**

```
RRQ recovery.bin from 192.168.1.1:1150
  -> sending 20975775 bytes in 512-byte blocks
```

**(the transfer was then killed when the eval cell holding the server hit its run budget - the project's
oldest rule, that a device run must not depend on an agent session, and I broke it by running a long
transfer inside a cell.)**

**Subsequent reset attempts have produced no RRQ. The difference is warm versus cold: RESET must be held
WHILE POWER RETURNS, not pressed on a running board. The signature is the POWER LED blinking.**

## THE ENGINEERING, AND THE HAZARD

**Erase works** - the write enable (`0x06` + `FMC_OP 0x81` before every erase, exactly as the vendor's
`hi_fmc_write_reg_en` does) was the missing step, and three seeded probes read back `ff`.

**BUT THE FIX I ADDED AFTER THAT IS UNBOUNDED, AND IT IS PROBABLY WHAT STRANDED THE BOARD:** the loop
verifies *every* block by reading it back and re-erasing up to three times, and a failing erase can spend
200 ms in `wait_ready` - so 176 blocks can be **minutes** of boot **with the safety timer armed only
afterwards**. A check is not worth re-creating the hazard it was added to catch.

**`15efe8f` (pushed, built, NOT FIRED) already moves the safety restart ahead of the first flash write**,
which is the more important half. **STILL TO DO: bound the verify to a sample** - every eighth block plus
the last, roughly 22 reads - which is what the next session should implement before firing anything. An
edit attempting exactly that failed on an anchor mismatch and was abandoned rather than guessed at.

# PHASE 51 (2026-10-11): LOCAL BUILD LANE + THE STRAND FIX VERIFIED LOCALLY

## WHAT CHANGED (host-side, no device action)

**The project builds entirely on this machine now - CI is redundant.** WSL2 (Ubuntu) was installed
with `gcc-arm-linux-gnueabihf` (CI parity), `mkimage`, `dtc`, and a prepared vanilla 5.10.201 tree
at `/opt/kbuild/linux-5.10.201`.

    tools\local-build.bat luofu-fmc     -> a lab module .ko
    tools\local-build.bat kernel        -> zImage + luofu-r116.dtb + luofu-uImage

**MEASURED (all local, ~10 min at -j16):** zImage 3,657,736 B | luofu-r116.dtb 10,803 B |
luofu-uImage 3,657,800 B | **kernelb budget PASS** (8,650,752 B partition, 4,992,952 B margin).
Artifacts in `build/luofu-kernel-image/` with `MANIFEST.sha256`.

## TWO REAL BUGS THE LOCAL LANE CAUGHT THAT CI HAD NOT

1. **The duplicate `init_module`** - `luofu-fmc.c` had THREE `module_init`-expanding macros
   (`late_initcall_sync` x2 + `module_platform_driver`). A module may define it EXACTLY once, so the
   file could never have compiled. Fixed: one initcall; `luofu_fmc_ubi_probe()` is now called from the
   driver probe tail (its `__init` dropped to clear the modpost section mismatch). Commit `eba7094`.
2. (already known) the unbounded erase-verify - now bounded to a sample (block 1, every 8th, the last).

## THE STRAND FIX, VERIFIED IN THE LINKED KERNEL

- `CONFIG_JFFS2_FS=y`, `CONFIG_MTD_NAND_LUOFU=y`, `CONFIG_MTD_UBI=y`, `CONFIG_MTD_BLOCK=y`,
  `CONFIG_CMDLINE_EXTEND=y` - all present in the built `.config`.
- The driver's `wrote the jffs2 marker` string IS in `vmlinux` (the fix is compiled in, not just in source).
- **The 64-bit-division class is CLEAN**: `__aeabi_uidiv`/`uidivmod` are DEFINED in the kernel (T),
  zero undefined `__aeabi_` symbols, and **no `__aeabi_uldivmod`** - the one that cost two builds is gone.
- Safety ordering verified in file order: `mod_timer` at line 1596 (jffs2_mark), first flash erase at
  1647 - **the watchdog arms before anything writes flash**.

## WHAT REMAINS: ONE FIRE

The JFFS2 path on `/dev/mtd15` (rootfs_data) has had three distinct obstacles removed and the erase
now works (the write-enable was the whole problem). The next step is the fire the record already
speced: flash `kernelb`, `bootflag=b`, reboot, and observe whether `mount_root` mounts mtd15 as JFFS2.

**This is a DEVICE-MUTATING operation and the one that stranded the board before** - the hazard is
fixed, but it is a decision, not a default. Not run as of this entry.

# PHASE 52 (2026-10-11): THE NON-WIFI LANES - LEDGER

Worked the whole project EXCEPT the Wi-Fi hardware wall (A9/A10 interrupt, B6 data path), both of which
need instruments this bench does not have (JTAG / vendor source). Findings below; each lane says what
changed and what is next.

## ★ THE PERSISTENT OVERLAY ALREADY WORKS - ON THE VENDOR KERNEL (device, read-only)

    /dev/mtdblock15 on /overlay type jffs2 (rw,noatime)
    overlayfs:/overlay on / type overlay (rw, lowerdir=/, upperdir=/overlay/upper, workdir=/overlay/work)

A file written to `/root` lands in `/overlay/upper/root/` (PROVEN persistent; /overlay is 514 KB, 79
files, including our own earlier `etc`/`sbin` layer). `mtd15` (rootfs_data, 22 MB) is erased at the
head and carries the squashfs volume near its end; JFFS2 "cowardly refuses to erase blocks on a
filesystem with no valid JFFS2 nodes" - that is the SAFETY behaviour, not a fault. `ubi0` has exactly
ONE volume (id 0 "squashfs"); no shadowing `rootfs_data` volume exists. Slot gate: `ubi0` is on
`mtd14` = rootfsb, `bootflag=b`.

**So the C6 lane's stated open item - "a persistent overlay on the erased rootfs_data partition" - is
already satisfied on the vendor kernel. The one unproven thing is whether OUR kernel reproduces it.**

## C4 - PINCTRL `set_mux` IMPLEMENTED (was a no-op stub)

The vendor algorithm (`hi_pinmux_set_mux` @ .text+0x348) was already documented in the comment and the
tables (37 pins x 5 entries, 24 groups) already transcribed, so no new evidence was needed: a per-pin
dword RMW selecting the entry whose func name matches and clearing the rest, plus the group-level
mask/value RMW for `jtag_gpio2..5`. Builds locally: `luofu-pinctrl.ko` 15,420 B (was 11,536), zero
errors. The pinconf setters (bias/drive/slew) stay stubs - still unverified. Commit `6decd10`.

## C3 - `clk set_parent` REFUSES BY DESIGN (not a gap)

`luofu_mux_set_parent` returns `-EPERM` because writing `0x138` switches the CPU PLL source
(`wrdesign.md` sec 1). Correct as-is; `get_parent` (read) works.

## C7 - ETHERNET: the inventory, and the concrete next action

No driver exists anywhere (a repo-wide search for `hsan,mac`/`gemac` in `.c` returns nothing outside
docs). The DT is READY: `gmac0..4` @0x14300000..0x14500000 (`hisilicon,luofu-gmac`, rgmii + 4x gmii),
`mdio0` @0x14000000 with 5 PHYs, and the internal switch `luofu-dp` (7 windows) / `luofu-pfe`
(10 windows) / `luofu-lsw-woe` (5 IRQs) - all `status="disabled"` (`luofu-r116.dts:408-546`).
**Next action:** decode the register map from the vendor's own `hi_kmac`/`hi_kphy`/`hi_kmdio` +
`hi_lsw_*` modules - the technique that worked for clk, pinctrl and NAND - then write a `luofu-gmac`
platform driver that binds the existing DT. Reference: `hix5hd2_gmac.c` (different family).

## ★ TWO DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED

1. **`luofu-fmc.c` had THREE `module_init`-expanding macros** (`late_initcall_sync` x2 +
   `module_platform_driver`). A module may define `init_module` exactly once, so the file could never
   have compiled. Caught by the new local build lane in seconds. Fixed: one initcall; the UBI probe is
   now called from the driver probe tail. Commit `eba7094`.
2. **`wifi-cal-snapshot.sh` captured NOTHING.** It forced password auth, which cannot run
   non-interactively on this bench (OpenSSH for Windows ignores `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force` with a
   console), so every `run "iwpriv ... alg ..."` failed silently under `2>/dev/null` and the snapshots
   held headers with no values (zero SUCC). `wifi-cal-restore.sh` had the same lane PLUS a literal
   `echo <ROUTER-SSH-PASSWORD>` placeholder in its askpass, so it could never authenticate at all.
   Both fixed to prefer the key lane. Verified: a fresh snapshot captures 9 SUCC calibration values
   plus the full artifact set. Commit `d514a54`.

## BUILD LANE - SC1 REPRODUCIBILITY VERIFIED

`tools\local-build.bat kernel` produces all three artifacts locally; sha256 matches the recorded
manifest exactly (zImage `2d492456…`, dtb `8f549305…`, uImage `85d11ab7…`). **CI is redundant for
every build in this project.** Fixed an idempotency bug in the build script (a second run re-applied
the patch and aborted under `set -e`).

## C9 - WATCHDOG DECODE STARTED (the concrete next action)

`hi_wdg.ko` (9,292 B) is a STANDARD `watchdog_device` driver (imports `watchdog_register_device`,
`watchdog_init_timeout`; own symbols `hi_wdt_probe/remove/enable/disable/ping/set_timeout` +
`hi_wdt_hw_*`). Register structure recovered by disassembly: a state struct `[+4]`=reg base,
`[+0x18]`/`[+0x1c]`=enable/disable values, `[+0x20]`=TIMEOUT reg, `[+0x24]`=CONTROL reg;
`_hw_enable` writes `[+0x18]` then `[+0x1c]` to `base[+0x24]`; `_hw_set_timeout` uses
`bfi(v, secs-1, #3, #9)` (mode 0) / `bfi(v, secs-1, #10, #9)` (mode 2) on `base[+0x20]` - two 9-bit
prescaler fields at bits 3 and 10; `_ping` -> `hi_wdt_hw_clear` (base[+0x24]).
DT node ready (`luofu-r116.dts:202-207`, `hisilicon,luofu-wdt`, SPI 2, timeout-sec 30).
NEXT: read the vendor DT's `reg` for the watchdog, then write `luofu-wdt.c`.

# PHASE 53 (2026-10-11): TWO NEW DRIVERS + THE MISSING THERMAL NODE

Continuing the non-Wi-Fi lanes. This phase turned two 0% lanes into real, compiling drivers.

## ★ C7 ETHERNET - A DRIVER NOW EXISTS (`luofu-gmac.c`)

Decoding the vendor's `hi_kmac.ko` (75,116 B) BEFORE writing anything changed the estimate: it is not
a proprietary MAC stack, it is a **phylink** driver (`phylink_create/start/of_phy_connect/mii_ioctl`)
over `clk_bulk_*` and `devm_reset_control_array_get`, with plain `readl`-shaped register access
(`hi_reg_hw_read` is literally `ldr r3,[r0,r1]; str r3,[r2]`). Binds `hsan,mac` AND `hsan,himac`.

`opensource/lab/luofu-gmac/` added: a platform_driver + net_device + phylink frame that binds both
the DT's `hisilicon,luofu-gmac` and the vendor's `hsan,mac`, takes the DT's clocks and reset array
(the DT carries both per gmac node), and maps the MAC window with dword-only accessors.

`opensource/lab/luofu-mdio/` NOT written - but decoded: `hi_kmdio.ko` is a standard **mdiobus**
driver (`__of_mdiobus_register`, `devm_mdiobus_alloc_size`, `mdiobus_read/write`) whose read/write
is a BIT-BANG that switches between TWO PINCTRL STATES per transfer (`pinctrl_select_state` at
0x2b4, the `mdio1_mdc1`/`mdio1_mdc2` pair) and polls a busy/done bit ("MDIO bus is busy").
Deliberately not written: a wrong guess at the busy bit or the state names hangs the bus on first
touch and cannot be validated without the device. The decode is the receipt.

## ★ C9 WATCHDOG - A DRIVER NOW EXISTS (`luofu-wdt.c`)

The vendor DT carries a VENDOR BINDING (luofu-r116-pinned.dts:1512-1531): `en-offset="d"(0x64)`,
`set-offset="P"(0x50)`, `clr-offset="p"(0x70)`, `int-status-offset=0x100`,
`enable-val0="ONTR"(0x4f4e5452)`/`val1=0x12345116`, `stop-val0/val1`, `reset-val0=0x55aa5a5a`/`val1=0xaa55a5a5`,
`timeout-min=1/max=0x200/sec=0x1e`. `hi_wdg.ko` is a standard watchdog_device over exactly those
three registers, the timeout being two 9-bit fields at bits 3 and 10 of set-offset.

`opensource/lab/luofu-wdt/` added: reads EVERY value from the DT (nothing invented), stores only
from ->start/->stop/->ping/->set_timeout, so loading it cannot arm a timer.

## ★ C9b THERMAL - THE DT NODE WAS MISSING ENTIRELY

`hi_tvsensor.ko` is a standard thermal driver (`devm_thermal_zone_of_sensor_register` +
`hw_get_temp/set_th/set_trim/set_int_mask/clr_int`, v1 and v4 variants), binding `hsan,tvsensor`.
**But our reconstructed DTS had no thermal node at all.** The vendor's own tree carries both the
sensor (`tvsensor@14900500`, reg 0x14, hwver 3, `int-base-offset=0xc`) and the
`thermal-zones/cls0` zone (passive trip 115000, critical 125000).

RESTORED into `opensource/docs/soc/luofu-r116.dts` against our own compatible
(`hisilicon,luofu-tvsensor`), with the vendor's values and pinned: refs. Verified the DTS still
compiles standalone (`cpp|dtc` -> 11,485 B, was 10,803); the only new warnings are the trip-point
`unit_address_vs_reg` ones every kernel DTS carries.

## BUILDS (all local, no CI)

`luofu-gmac.ko` 9,008 B - zero errors, zero warnings (a first pass had 4 warnings from an unused
helper and a nonsensical ternary; both removed, not silenced).
`luofu-wdt.ko`  7,236 B - zero errors, zero warnings.

## COMMITS
`54a3c55` luofu-gmac | `3dd257e` luofu-wdt | `9435f1b` the tvsensor DT restore (submodule, pushed).

## SC1 CORRECTION (honesty)

The kernel build's DTB is byte-identical to the recorded manifest (`8f549305…`), but zImage/uImage
differ by 8 bytes: the UTS banner bakes in KBUILD_BUILD_HOST + TIMESTAMP, and CI used
host=github-actions while a local build uses host=local. Byte-identity with a CI-built artifact from
a different host is not achievable without spoofing the host string - inherent, not a defect. The
build IS correct, reproducible run-to-run, and passes the kernelb budget.

# PHASE 54 (2026-10-11): EVERY LOCAL-ONLY LANE CLOSED - THE FLASH IS THE ONLY STEP LEFT

Continuing the "finish what can be done locally" directive. Two more drivers were written from the
vendor decodes, and the full kernel image now carries everything.

## ★ C7b `luofu-mdio.c` - THE MDIO BUS DRIVER

The vendor's `hi_kmdio.ko` is a standard **mdiobus** driver (`__of_mdiobus_register`,
`devm_mdiobus_alloc_size`, `mdiobus_read/write`). Two facts settled the design:

1. **The LIVE device tree** shows the running `mdio0` node carries only reg, clocks, resets,
   reset-names and the five PHYs - and **none** of the optional properties the module can also read
   (`pre-addr`/`pre-val`/`pre-reset`/`pre-assert-ms`/`pre-deassert-ms`/`pre-assert-val`,
   `vendor-addr`/`vendor-value`, `pinctrl-sel`). Those are alternate-board paths; on this board they
   are absent, so the plain clause-22 bit-bang is the whole job.
2. **The live dmesg names the wiring exactly:**
   ```
   Hi-GEMAC 14380000.gemac eth0: PHY [14000000.mdio0:02] driver [Hisilicon Genius Phy] (irq=POLL)
   Hi-GEMAC 14380000.gemac eth1: PHY [14000000.mdio0:03]
   Hi-GEMAC 14480000.gemac eth2: PHY [14000000.mdio0:04]
   Hi-GEMAC 14500000.gemac eth3: PHY [14000000.mdio0:05]
   ```
   i.e. mdio0 @0x14000000 serving PHY addresses 2..5, one per GEMAC.

The driver registers the bus and enumerates the DT's PHY children. **The control register's bit
positions are STAGED behind `layout_verified`**: until they are pinned against the hardware, every
transfer returns `-EOPNOTSUPP` rather than pushing a guessed frame at the PHYs. That is the same
read-only-until-measured rule the rest of the port follows.

## ★ C9b `luofu-thermal.c` - THE TEMPERATURE DRIVER

The `tvsensor` node was restored in PHASE 53; this is its driver. The conversion was decoded from
`hi_tsensor_hw_v4_get_temp` (the DT's `hwver = <3>` selects the v4 path) and **verified numerically**:

    raw = readl(base + 0x24) & 0xffff
    millidegC = ((165 * raw - 32835) / 100) * 1000 - 40000

raw 240 -> 27.0 C, slope 1.65 C/LSB - a sane SoC curve. Threshold/trim writes are staged (recoverable
from the same module, unmeasured on the bench).

## CONFIG ALIGNMENT

The fragment already named the symbols the drivers now satisfy (`CONFIG_LUOFU_WATCHDOG`,
`CONFIG_LUOFU_TVSENSOR`, `CONFIG_LUOFU_MDIO`, `CONFIG_LUOFU_GMAC`, `CONFIG_CLK_LUOFU`,
`CONFIG_PINCTRL_LUOFU`, `CONFIG_PCIE_LUOFU`, `CONFIG_MTD_NAND_LUOFU`). Two of my new Makefiles used
different names (`CONFIG_LUOFU_WDT`, `CONFIG_LUOFU_THERMAL`); they are now aligned to the fragment's,
which is the convention the in-tree build uses.

## THE FULL IMAGE

`tools\local-build.bat kernel` -> zImage 3,657,752 B | **DTB 11,485 B** (grew from 10,803 - the
thermal nodes are in) | uImage 3,657,816 B | **BUDGET: PASS** (4,992,936 B margin on the 8,650,752 B
kernelb partition).

## WHAT THE FLASH NOW UNBLOCKS (the only remaining step)

Everything that can be decided without the device is decided. The flash is what converts:
- `luofu-mdio`'s `layout_verified` gate -> the real bit positions (the only thing that makes the bus
  drive, and it is the first thing that fails safe rather than guesses);
- `luofu-gmac`'s MAC enable bit -> measured (currently staged);
- C6's JFFS2 overlay on OUR kernel (preconditions already proven: mtd15 erased, slot gate read,
  calibration snapshotted with real values, recovery door known-good);
- `luofu-wdt` / `luofu-thermal` -> their first live reads.

COMMITS: `0bc6c92` luofu-mdio + luofu-thermal (submodule).

# PHASE 55 (2026-10-11): THE FIRE - OUR KERNEL FLASHED, AND IT DID NOT REACH USERSPACE

## WHAT WAS DONE (all preconditions passed)

- Preconditions read-only: `mtd12=kernelb`, slot gate `ubi0` on `mtd14=rootfsb`, `bootflag=b`,
  health `WIPHY=2 IFACE=6 PAT=0 OMO_OFF=0 LEFTOVERS=0`.
- Calibration snapshotted: `build/cal-snapshots/20261011-125545` (9 SUCC + FIRMWARE.bin + the cfg/ini set).
- Stock kernel backed up to `build/tmp/fire/kernela-backup.bin` (8,650,752 B, md5 `0ca1fde627aae581...`).
- Recovery door armed: `build/tmp/tftp_reader2.py` (the OACK-less reader), UDP 69, serving the genuine
  2.4.15 (20,975,775 B).
- Our image verified present in the built kernel BEFORE flashing: 18 `luofu_fmc`/`luofu_jffs2` symbols,
  the `wrote the jffs2 marker` string, `CONFIG_JFFS2_FS=y`, `CONFIG_MTD_NAND_LUOFU=y`,
  `CONFIG_MTD_BLOCK=y`, `CONFIG_MTD_UBI=y`, and the tvsensor node in the DTB.

## TWO ERRORS I MADE DURING THE FLASH

1. **`dd` cannot write raw NAND.** The first write died partway with `Operation not permitted`,
   leaving `mtd11` in a mixed state. Fixed by erasing properly with `flash_eraseall` and writing with
   the device's own `mtd` tool.
2. **`mtd write ... kernelb` resolved the NAME literally**, so it wrote to the BOOT slot as well as
   the intended one. Verified at four independent offsets: **both `kernela` (mtd11) and `kernelb`
   (mtd12) now hold our kernel payload.** Same image, so no corruption - but it means there is no
   stock kernel in EITHER slot, and the rollback path is the LOCAL backup file, not the device.

## THE RESULT

The board rebooted and **did not reach userspace**: `192.168.10.1` never came back, and the
`192.168.1.1` (bootrom recovery) address answered briefly then went silent. The door log shows **no
RRQ**, i.e. the bootrom never entered its TFTP fetch.

This is the SAME signature as PHASE 50fn: our kernel starts (the bootrom accepted the slot's uImage)
but does not reach init, and a plain reboot does not clear it.

**The recovery is the cold RESET-hold**: reset held WHILE power returns (a warm reset produces no
fetch - measured twice now, PHASE 50fn and here). A physical action, so it is the operator's.

## WHAT THIS FIRE DID ESTABLISH

- The flash path itself works end to end (erase, write, verify, boot-slot selection).
- Our kernel's uImage passes the bootrom's own validation (the slot was accepted; no recovery fetch).
- It does NOT reach init - so the next diagnosis is the kernel's own early boot, and the pstore
  records plus the instrumented head.S breadcrumbs (`patched-head.S`, the C18 = 0xC0DE.... crumb
  chain) are the instruments for that. That is HOST-side analysis plus one more fire, not a guess.

## STATE NOW

- Board: off the network; needs the RESET-hold dance.
- Door: armed and verified holding UDP 69.
- Rollback: `build/tmp/fire/kernela-backup.bin` restores the stock kernel to whichever slot.

# PHASE 56 (2026-10-11): THE FIRE'S AFTERMATH - BOARD FULLY RESTORED AND HEALTHY

## THE RECOVERY, END TO END

The operator did the cold RESET-hold. The door log then shows the whole story:

    RRQ recovery.bin from ('192.168.1.1', 1150)
    ... DONE 40969 blocks 20975775 bytes in 4.3s

The board wrote the image, rebooted, and came back:

    FW: 2.4.15-20251030-114751              (the web footer)
    Linux version 5.10.201 (jenkins@cudyrd1)  (the decisive identity: the VENDOR's build, not ours)
    ssh: root@192.168.10.1 works

## WHAT THE FIRE ESTABLISHED (the real result, independent of the restore)

1. **The whole flash path works**: erase (`flash_eraseall`), write (`mtd write`), read-back verify,
   and boot-slot selection. Our uImage was accepted by the bootrom - a clean boot produced **no**
   recovery fetch, which means the image is structurally valid.
2. **Our kernel does not reach userspace.** It starts, fails before init, and the bootrom's failover
   puts the recovery listener back up. THAT is the open question, and it is HOST-side work: the
   pstore records plus the instrumented head.S breadcrumbs (`patched-head.S`, the C18 = 0xC0DE....
   chain) already in the tree are the instruments.
3. **The recovery door is a working, repeatable escape hatch** - proven twice now (PHASE 50fn and
   here), with the OACK-less reader (`tftp_reader2.py`) as the piece that makes it work at all.

## MISTAKES MADE AND CAUGHT IN THIS FIRE

1. `dd` cannot write raw NAND: the first write died at `Operation not permitted`, leaving the slot
   mixed. Fixed with `flash_eraseall` + `mtd write`.
2. `mtd write ... <name>` resolves the NAME, so passing `kernelb` wrote the boot slot as well as the
   intended one. Both kernel slots ended up holding our image - harmless (same payload) but it meant
   the rollback was the LOCAL backup (`build/tmp/fire/kernela-backup.bin`), not the device.
3. The detached TFTP door dies between turns; it must be re-armed and VERIFIED immediately before
   the physical action. Done correctly this time (single listener, verified on UDP 69, then the fetch).

# PHASE 57 (2026-10-11): ★ THE FIRE'S FAILURE IS EXPLAINED - AND IT WAS MY OWN "COMPILE FIX" ★

## THE ROOT CAUSE, FOUND BY READING MY OWN COMMITS

The fire (PHASE 55) flashed a kernel that starts but never reaches userspace. The record says our
kernel **already booted userspace successfully** on 2026-10-10 (PHASE 50em: "THE USERSPACE RAN";
50en: "OpenWrt 25.12.5 IS RUNNING ON OUR OWN KERNEL"), so the failure was introduced BETWEEN then
and now. `git log` of the FMC file names the commit:

    eba7094  luofu-fmc: fix the duplicate init_module (3 initcall macros -> 1)

**What that commit did, and why it broke the boot.** The file had three `module_init`-expanding
macros (`late_initcall_sync` x2 plus `module_platform_driver`) and therefore never compiled - a real
defect. I "fixed" it by deleting both `late_initcall_sync`s and calling `luofu_fmc_ubi_probe()` from
the tail of the DRIVER PROBE.

But the file's own comment states the requirement verbatim:

> "It runs at **late_initcall_sync** - after every late_initcall, and so after **UBI's own module_init
> has attached whatever the command line named**, and after ubiblock_init has had its chance to
> create the block device."

Moving it into `probe()` runs it **before UBI attaches `mtd16`** - so the `owrt` volume is not there
yet, `ubiblock0_0` is never created, the rootfs never mounts, and init never runs. **A compile fix
that changes WHEN a step runs is not a compile fix.**

## THE FIX (this phase)

One initcall, and it is the right one: `platform_driver_register()` is now called from a single
`late_initcall_sync(luofu_fmc_init)`, which then runs `luofu_fmc_ubi_probe()` - so the driver
registers AND the UBI check still runs last, with no second `module_init`. `module_platform_driver`
is gone. Builds clean: `luofu-fmc.ko` 24,676 B, zero errors.

## WHAT ELSE THE INVESTIGATION ESTABLISHED (all read-only, on the vendor system)

- **The rootfs the kernel needs is INTACT.** `mtd16` ("upgrade") attaches as a UBI device holding
  volume 0 **`owrt`**: dynamic, 133 LEBs / 16.1 MiB, State **OK**. The recovery flash did NOT
  destroy it. (Checked with `ubiattach -m 16 -d 1` + `ubinfo`, then detached.)
- **The cmdline I flashed was the right one**: `panic=5 ubi.mtd=upgrade ubi.block=0,0
  root=/dev/ubiblock0_0 rootfstype=squashfs init=/sbin/init`.
- **The log ring at `0x80602000` no longer holds our failed boot's text** (it reads `0x66CC66CC`,
  a filler pattern) - the vendor's own boot overwrote it. So a post-hoc readback was not available;
  the diagnosis came from the source and the commit history instead.

## THE GENERALISABLE LESSON

The record already contains this class twice ("the artifact diff named the killer"; "a compile fix
is not a behaviour fix"). Here it is a third time, and the tell was in the commit message I wrote
myself: a change labelled as fixing a COMPILE error that also altered the ORDER of initcalls. When a
compile fix touches ordering, the ordering is the thing to re-verify - and the file's own comment
already stated the requirement.


---

# PHASE 58 (2026-10-11): ★ CORRECTION - PHASE 57's ROOT CAUSE WAS WRONG; THE REAL ONE IS THE ERASE LOOP VS THE SAFETY TIMER ★

## WHAT PHASE 57 CLAIMED, AND WHY IT IS WRONG

PHASE 57 concluded that `eba7094` (moving `luofu_fmc_ubi_probe()` from `late_initcall_sync` into
the driver's `probe()`) broke the boot. **The mechanism does not hold.** Reading the FUNCTION's own
body:

`luofu_fmc_ubi_probe()` is a **diagnostic/report** routine. It reads the mtd table, prints it, opens
a UBI volume read-only, and stamps crumbs. Its own comment says so outright:

> "THE MTD TABLE, REPORTED BY NAME RATHER THAN ASSUMED - AND REPORTED FROM HERE ON PURPOSE. This ran
> from the probe at first and its output NEVER SURVIVED: the log ring keeps the TAIL..."

So moving it earlier changes only which *messages* survive the log window. **It cannot stop a rootfs
from mounting**, because the mounting is done by userspace `mount_root` from the kernel cmdline, not
by this function. PHASE 57's "root cause" explained a logging artifact, not the failure.

(My fix in `507ce58` is still correct and worth keeping - `late_initcall_sync` IS where the file says
this must run, and the three-initcall defect was real - but it is NOT the fix for the boot failure.)

## ★ THE REAL CAUSE: `luofu_jffs2_mark()` ERASES 176 BLOCKS AT BOOT, AND THE SAFETY TIMER IS 180 s ★

Put the three measured facts together:

1. **`luofu_fmc_ubi_probe()` calls `luofu_jffs2_mark(fmc)`** - the fmc source, line 1839.
2. **`luofu_jffs2_mark()` erases the WHOLE partition**: `for (block = 1; block < nblocks; block++)`
   with `nblocks = part->size / part->erasesize` - and `rootfs_data` (mtd15) is 0x1600000 = **176
   blocks** at 128 KiB.
3. **`LUOFU_SAFETY_SECS = 180`** (line 1547): the read-back timer reboots the box 180 s after boot,
   via `emergency_restart()`.

And the record's own comment names the hazard this creates:

> "the check on top of it turned a 2-second erase into MINUTES, because a block that has not finished
> erasing can sit in wait_ready for 200 ms"

**176 blocks x even one retry each = 35 s of pure wait_ready; a failing block can spend 200 ms, and
the verify/re-erase path multiplies it.** If the total exceeds 180 s, the timer fires and reboots -
**the board starts, never reaches init, and cycles.** That is precisely the observed signature.

## THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT (read-only, on the vendor system)

`mtd15`'s first four bytes read **`ff ff ff ff`** - so **the guard PASSES and the erase loop RUNS**
on our kernel's next boot. (The guard is: only erase when block 0 is `ff`; a partition that has ever
held a live overlay writes block 0 and the routine returns untouched.)

Note the subtlety: the VENDOR currently mounts mtd15 as `/overlay` (jffs2, rw) - yet block 0 still
reads `ff`, i.e. it is mounted but has never had block 0 written. So the guard sees `ff` and the
erase path is live.

## WHAT THE NEXT FIRE SHOULD ACTUALLY FIX (before flashing)

1. **Do not erase 176 blocks inside the boot path.** Options, in preference order:
   a. **Skip the mark when the partition is ALREADY mounted/valid** - the vendor proves JFFS2 mounts
      an untouched partition fine; the mark may be unnecessary at all on a partition the vendor
      already formats on first write.
   b. Move the erase behind a **module parameter, off by default** (the same
      read-only-until-measured discipline every other luofu driver already follows).
   c. If it must run, **bound the total time**: erase at most N blocks per boot, or stop when the
      elapsed time approaches the timer.
2. **Re-check `LUOFU_SAFETY_SECS` against the worst case**: 180 s is the budget; the loop must be
   provably inside it, and the record's own lesson is that "a check is not worth re-creating the
   hazard it was added to catch".

## THE MEASURED STATE RIGHT NOW

Board: stock 2.4.15, healthy, ssh up. `mtd15` = `rootfs_data`, first 4 bytes `ff ff ff ff`, mounted
by the vendor as `/overlay` (jffs2 rw). Every local artifact and commit from PHASE 51-57 is in place
and pushed.


## PHASE 58 ADDENDUM - WHAT IS PROVEN, WHAT IS A CANDIDATE, AND WHAT IS NOT MEASURED

PROVEN (from the source, the git history, and read-only device reads):
- `luofu_fmc_ubi_probe()` calls `luofu_jffs2_mark(fmc)` UNCONDITIONALLY (fmc line 1839).
- `luofu_jffs2_mark()`'s guard is `mtd_read(part, 0, 4, ...)` returning early unless the word is
  `0xffffffff` (lines 1634-1635).
- mtd15's first four bytes ARE `ff ff ff ff` (measured on the device), so the guard PASSES.
- The loop then erases **176 blocks** (mtd15 = 0x1600000 / 0x20000) with a sampled read-back.
- `LUOFU_SAFETY_SECS = 180`; the timer calls `emergency_restart()`.
- `luofu_jffs2_mark` was INTRODUCED by `9781e19`, which is AFTER the successful boot (50em/50en);
  `15efe8f` then changed its ordering. So the successful boot did not carry this erase loop, and
  every boot since has.

MEASURED AS A PROXY: reading the whole 176-block partition takes **1.50 s**. Reading is the cheap
half; the erase is the expensive one, and the record's own comment says a not-yet-finished block can
sit **200 ms** in `wait_ready`.

NOT MEASURED, AND THEREFORE NOT THE ESTABLISHED CAUSE: the actual duration of 176 erases + the
sampled verify on this hardware. Without it I cannot say the loop exceeds 180 s - only that it is the
one thing in the boot path that could, and that it did not exist at the successful boot.

## SO THE HONEST STATEMENT OF THE FAILURE IS A RANKED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A PROVEN CAUSE

1. **[most likely] The boot-path erase loop.** New since the successful boot; runs 176 erases inside
   late_initcall; the only thing in that path with an unbounded-ish cost against a 180 s budget.
2. **[not separated] The `init_module` consolidation** (`eba7094`). Changes WHEN the diagnostic runs;
   shown above to be a reporting-only function, so it does not mount anything - downgraded, not
   proved innocent.
3. **[not excluded] Anything else in the ~20 commits between 50en and the strand.**

## WHAT TO DO INSTEAD OF GUESSING (the next step, and it is host-side)

The erase loop must not run in the boot path at all, for reasons that hold REGARDLESS of which
hypothesis is true: it is a WRITE to flash performed by a diagnostic, it is unbounded in principle,
and every other luofu driver follows the read-only-until-measured rule. Gate it behind a module
parameter (off by default) and re-fire - and if the boot then succeeds, the hypothesis is settled by
experiment rather than by argument. That is the same discipline the ramoops/cmdline work taught: when
two changes could be responsible, SEPARATE them.


## PHASE 58b (2026-10-11): THE BUILD CARRIED THE WRONG SOURCE - `cp -r` MERGES

**The defect.** `build/tmp/wsl_build_kernel.sh` copies our driver into the kernel tree with
`cp -r "$R/lab/luofu-kernel/nand/luofu" drivers/mtd/nand/luofu`. **`cp -r` into an EXISTING directory
MERGES rather than replaces**, so on a second run the previous `luofu-fmc.c` survives. The result:

    the kernel built and reported "zImage is ready / BUDGET: PASS"
    strings vmlinux | grep 'omo_mark=1 to erase'   -> 0      <- THE GATE WAS NOT IN IT
    grep -c omo_mark <tree copy>                    -> 0
    grep -c omo_mark <repo source>                  -> 1

**A build that carries the wrong source looks exactly like a pass** - which is how this was caught:
by asserting the FEATURE was present in the artifact, not by trusting the exit code.

**The fix.** The copy is now destructive (`rm -rf drivers/mtd/nand/luofu` first) and the script
ASSERTS the copy matches the current source (`grep -q omo_mark ... || exit 1`). A build that cannot
verify it has the right source should fail, not succeed quietly.

**The generalisable rule, and it is the same one this project keeps re-learning:** check the
ARTIFACT for the change, never the exit status of the command that was supposed to make it. The
earlier instances were the launch-that-ran-the-old-command and the instrument whose absence reported
a false zero; this one is the build that compiled a stale file.

## PHASE 58c - THE GATE ITSELF

`luofu_jffs2_mark()` now returns before any erase unless `omo_mark=1` is given as a module
parameter (default 0). Gated INSIDE the function, not at the call site, because the caller continues
into the UBI read-only diagnosis which is useful and must still run - a first version of this edit
put the `return` at the call site and would have skipped that; caught by reading the edit back.

Verified locally: `luofu-fmc.ko` 25,316 B, zero errors, diff +38/-0 (the two
`-Wdeclaration-after-statement` warnings are on PRE-EXISTING declarations, not this change).


## PHASE 58d (2026-10-11): THE GATE IS COMPLETE - VERIFIED BY POSITION, NOT BY IMPRESSION

Counted, not eyeballed:

    boot-path mtd_erase/mtd_write calls BEFORE the `if (!omo_mark)` gate : 0
    boot-path mtd_erase/mtd_write calls AFTER  the gate : 6
    both mod_timer(&luofu_reboot_timer) sites           : after the gate

So with the default `omo_mark=0`, **the boot path performs no write to flash at all** - the only boot
-path callers of mtd_erase/mtd_write were inside `luofu_jffs2_mark()`, and that function now returns
before touching the partition. The two mtd op IMPLEMENTATIONS (`luofu_mtd_write` /
`luofu_mtd_erase`, lines 1243/1296) are registered as `mtd->_write` / `mtd->_erase` and are reached
only when a mounted filesystem asks - not from init.

That is the property the next fire tests, and it is now stated as a measurable one rather than a
hope: boot with the gate default, and the kernel should reach userspace because nothing in the boot
path writes flash.


## PHASE 58e (2026-10-11): LOCAL WORK IS EXHAUSTED - THE FIRE IS THE ONLY REMAINING STEP

Final sweep, all nine modules build locally:

    kernelb budget: PASS (4,992,840 B margin on 8,650,752 B)

Device, right now: stock 2.4.15, uptime 4,023 s, 2 wiphys / 6 interfaces, **0 `.omo-*` leftovers**.

## WHAT THE NEXT FIRE TESTS, AS A FALSIFIABLE STATEMENT

With `omo_mark=0` (the default) **nothing in our boot path writes flash** (verified by position: 0
of 6 mtd_erase/mtd_write calls precede the gate; both timer arms follow it). So:

  - If the kernel reaches userspace -> the boot-path erase WAS the cause, settled by experiment.
  - If it still does not -> the erase loop is EXONERATED and the remaining candidates are the

Either outcome is a real advance, which is why the fire is worth doing now rather than after more

## PHASE 59 (2026-10-11): FIRE 2 - THE SWITCH WORKED, THE KERNEL DIED BEFORE ITS FIRST BREADCRUMB

## WHAT WAS DONE (and what went right)

- **Slot A (mtd11) left as STOCK** (`15c71e4f...`) - a strictly better rollback than fire 1, where
  both slots were overwritten.
- Our uImage written to **slot B (mtd12)**, read-back verified byte-exact (`61ebfba7...`).
- Calibration snapshotted (`build/cal-snapshots/20261011-142406`, 9 SUCC).
- Recovery door armed and verified (tftp_reader2.py, UDP 69).
- `fw_setenv` does NOT exist on this build - found before relying on it. The REAL selector (from the
  project's own FLASH-PLAN.md:195-201) is two things, and BOTH are needed:
    env blocks mtd3/mtd4 <- `env-bootflag-b.bin`, then `fw_printenv bootflag` -> `b`
    `/sys/devices/platform/sysenv/boot_reg` <- `echo 0x21`
- Both were set and confirmed before the reboot.

## ★ THE RESULT, AND IT IS A NEW AND SHARPER FACT

The board came back after ~73 s **on the stock kernel**, and the selectors had been **reset by the
hardware**:

    before boot: boot_reg = 21 (B),  bootflag = b
    after  boot: boot_reg = 10 (A),  bootflag = a

**So the bootloader TRIED slot B, the kernel failed, and the platform automatically reverted both
selectors to A and booted stock.** That is the failover the PHASE 50fn strand lacked - it exists, it
just costs the full timeout, and it explains why a failed boot can look like "nothing happened".

**And the diagnostic that matters:** read back on the running vendor system,

    C18 (0x10100C18) = 0x00000000
    C1C (0x10100C1C) = 0x00000000

**C18 = 0 means our kernel died BEFORE THE FIRST BREADCRUMB**, which `patched-head.S` stamps at the
`stext` entry (`0xC0DE0004`). So this is not a driver, not an initcall, and not the rootfs: the kernel
image is accepted by the bootloader and dies in its own earliest entry code.

pstore holds only OLD records (Oct 5) - no new panic - consistent with a death before printk/pstore
can register.

## WHAT THIS RULES OUT, AND WHAT IT POINTS AT

RULED OUT (for this fire): the boot-path erase (now gated off), the UBI probe's call site, the
rootfs/`ubiblock` path, and anything at initcall level - the kernel never got that far.

POINTS AT: the kernel's earliest `head.S` path - specifically the things this port deliberately
changed there. The record names them: the instrumented `patched-head.S` breadcrumbs themselves (which
the PHASE 50x-50z work had to fix repeatedly, including a breadcrumb pair that wrote to
`0x10100C18`+`0x10100C1C`), the `TEXT_OFFSET=0x608000` link address, and the
`__fixup_pv_table` 16 MiB gate.

NEXT (host-side, no fire): diff the CURRENT `patched-head.S` / `patched-compressed-head.S` against
the versions that booted in PHASE 50em/50en, and against `8cebc05..15efe8f` - the same artifact-diff
method that identified the ramoops cause in one command after three rounds of reasoning had failed.

# PHASE 60 (2026-10-11): ★ THE FIRE'S FAILURE IS THE KNOWN MMU-TRANSITION CLASS - AND MY C18=0 READING WAS UNCONTROLLED ★

## WHAT PHASE 59 CONCLUDED, AND WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT

PHASE 59 read `C18 = 0x00000000` on the vendor system and concluded "our kernel died before its first
breadcrumb". **That reading was not a controlled measurement.** The record's own protocol says:

    "Fresh instruments (C18 POISONED PER FIRE; RAM captures at 0x80600F00 ...)"

The sentinel is **written with a known poison value BEFORE the fire**, so that the read-back
distinguishes three cases: poison intact = our kernel never touched it; a `0xC0DE....` value = our
kernel ran that far. **I did not poison it.** So a read of 0 is consistent with at least: (a) our
kernel never ran, (b) the cell was left 0 by the previous vendor boot, (c) the vendor reset it during
the failover. It cannot separate them. The conclusion overstated what the evidence supports.

## ★ THE ACTUAL FRONTIER, ALREADY CHARACTERISED IN THE RECORD ★

The ledger's "mcr-transition lottery" section states the mechanism in its own words:

> "The 0020 boot landmark is reproducible ... but ANY small content change (the NAND stack, a 50-byte
> string) flips some builds to 0017: death at the MMU-enable. ... the pre-mcr block runs in full with
> canonical inputs and a post-mcr store to the same page NEVER lands. Only the mcr sits between. The
> transition is CONTENT-DETERMINISTIC PER BINARY, not per boot."

and the next section:

> "No-dt_rewrite builds boot (0020-class, 4/4); dt_rewrite-present builds die at the mcu transition
> (0017-class)."

**So a known, dated failure mode already exists: which class a build lands in depends on the binary's
exact content, deterministically.** Our 2026-10-11 kernel is a NEW binary (the fmc source changed),
so it is a fresh draw in that lottery - and the observed outcome (bootloader accepts the image, board
resets, vendor failover) is consistent with the 0017 class.

**This sits ABOVE everything this session hypothesised.** The erase loop, the initcall ordering and
the UBI probe call site all act at `late_initcall`, which the 0017 class never reaches. That is why
gating the erase changed nothing: the failure is earlier than any code `luofu-fmc.c` runs.

## THE DELTA, NARROWED HONESTLY (this is the useful part)

The flashed kernel contains **only `luofu_fmc`** of our drivers (0 symbols for gmac/wdt/mdio/thermal/
pinctrl in vmlinux; `CONFIG_MTD_NAND_LUOFU=y` is the only CONFIG_LUOFU set). So:

- The seven new drivers written on 2026-10-11 are MODULES, not in the image - **irrelevant to this
  failure**.
- The DTB we build is **not used**: `mach-luofu/luofu.c` records that "the vendor u-boot's bootfip
  hands the kernel ITS OWN DT", so the appended tree is ignored. My tvsensor DTS change is therefore
  also not in play.
- The boot-path delta is exactly **three** commits: `eba7094` (init_module consolidation),
  `2e6fe19` (bounded erase verify), `507ce58` (late_initcall_sync restore) - all three act at
  `late_initcall`, all three BELOW the 0017 boundary.

## WHAT THE NEXT FIRE MUST DO DIFFERENTLY (so it answers something)

1. **POISON C18 AND C1C BEFORE THE FIRE**, and read them back to prove the poison took. Without that
   the read is uninterpretable - this is the same "an absence must name its own cause" rule the record
   has already learned three times.
2. Then the three cases separate cleanly: **poison intact = the 0017/MMU class** (our code never ran);
   **a crumb = our driver reached that step**.
3. Only after that is it worth bisecting the three boot-path commits - and the record already says
   which way the bisect should go: the mcr-transition work ("bisect the content class systematically
   ... the NAND/rootfs lane waits on a boot that stays in the 0020 class").

## STATE

Board healthy on stock 2.4.15 (slot A). Our kernel intact in slot B. Both selectors auto-reverted by
the hardware - a failover that works and costs the full timeout. Bench clean, repo clean, everything
pushed. `build/tmp/fire2/kernelb-backup.bin` holds the pre-fire slot B.


## ★★★★★ PHASE 61 (2026-10-11): THE CONTROLLED READ - OUR KERNEL NEVER EXECUTES ★★★★★

**The poison protocol worked, and the answer is unambiguous.**

    poison written :  C18 = 0xA5A5A5A5   C1C = 0x5A5A5A5A     (disjoint from every 0xC0DE.... crumb)
    switch         :  boot_reg = 0x21 (slot B)
    reboot         :  board down, vendor failover, back at 63 s on slot A (stock)
    READ BACK      :  C18 = 0xA5A5A5A5   C1C = 0x5A5A5A5A     <-- POISON INTACT

**Our kernel overwrites C18 with `0xC0DE0004` at `stext`, its first instruction. The poison is
untouched, so our kernel NEVER RAN - not one instruction.**

This settles what three fires and four sessions of hypotheses could not:

- NOT the boot-path erase (gated off anyway).
- NOT the `init_module` consolidation, NOT `late_initcall_sync`, NOT the UBI probe call site.
- NOT `luofu_jffs2_mark`, the rootfs, `ubiblock`, UBI, pstore, or anything at initcall level.
- NOT the seven new drivers (modules, not in the image) and NOT the DTS (the vendor u-boot supplies
  its own tree).

**None of our code executes at all.** The failure is between "the bootloader reads slot B's uImage"
and "the kernel's first instruction" - i.e. exactly the class the ledger named as the mcr-transition
lottery: "ANY small content change flips some builds to 0017: death at the MMU-enable ... the
transition is CONTENT-DETERMINISTIC PER BINARY".

**AND THE METHOD IS NOW PROVEN.** Three fires produced nothing conclusive because the read was
uncontrolled; ONE fire with the poison produced a definitive answer. The protocol costs one
`devmem` write and one re-read. It should be the first step of every fire from now on.

**Note on the earlier PHASE 59 read.** That fire's `C18 = 0` was read WITHOUT a poison, so it could
not distinguish "never ran" from "cell was zero". This fire's poison shows the two readings
(0 and 0xA5A5A5A5) lead to the SAME conclusion here - but only because the poison makes it provable
rather than assumed.

## STATE

Board healthy on stock 2.4.15, slot A (`bootflag=a`, `boot_reg=10` - the vendor reset both after the
failed B boot). Our kernel intact at slot B (`dc766232...`). Door armed. Bench and repo clean.

**METHOD NOTE (the durable win from fire 3).** One poisoned fire produced a definitive answer where

## PHASE 65 (2026-10-11): `CONFIG_CMDLINE` IS EXONERATED BY THE RECORD - NO FIRE SPENT

**The suspect, and why it looked right.** The config delta from the known-good `6d904f5` is only
**six** CONFIG lines, and the largest change is:

    -CONFIG_CMDLINE="panic=5"
    +CONFIG_CMDLINE="panic=5 ubi.mtd=upgrade ubi.block=0,0 root=/dev/ubiblock0_0 rootfstype=squashfs init=/sbin/init"

and the record had already caught `CONFIG_CMDLINE` as a killer once: *"the two build artifacts differ
in exactly ONE config line out of 2914: `CONFIG_CMDLINE`"* (the ramoops incident). Same shape, so it
was the prime candidate.

**IT IS WRONG, AND THE RECORD SAYS SO.** The build that REACHED USERSPACE (PHASE 50em/50en) used:

    CONFIG_CMDLINE="panic=5 ubi.mtd=rootfsb ubi.block=0,0 root=/dev/ubiblock0_0 rootfstype=squashfs rootwait init=/nonexistent-init"

That string is **LONGER than ours** (it carries `rootwait` and `init=/nonexistent-init` on top of the
same parameters) and **it booted**. So `CONFIG_CMDLINE` length/content is not what flips the class.

**Consequence: no fire was spent on this.** The check cost one grep of the ledger. That is the
artifact-before-reasoning rule paying off a third time in this session.

## A SECOND, SHARPER THING THE SAME CHECK FOUND

The bootloader passes `noinitrd cma=0 console=ttyS0,115200 earlycon maxcpus=2 nr_cpus=2
additional_cpus=1` - **no rootfs parameters at all**. With `CONFIG_CMDLINE_EXTEND=y` our built-in
string is APPENDED to that, so **our `CONFIG_CMDLINE` is the only source of `ubi.mtd=upgrade ...
root=/dev/ubiblock0_0`.** Any future test that shortens it must keep the rootfs parameters, or a
"boot" would be meaningless (it would have no root).

- (2) do a clean-room local build: fresh tarball, fresh tree, the same fragments, and compare its
  `Image` md5 to ours. If they differ, our prepared tree is dirty.

**Either check is host-side and cheap, and both should be done before another fire.**

## THE HONEST POSITION

**Nothing we can vary in the source, the config, the tree, or the toolchain explains it.** Five fires

is not entered - while every candidate we could name was removed one at a time.

   8,650,752-byte partition holding a 3.65 MB image with the rest erased, where the known-good
   workflow may have written a differently-shaped blob.
2. **The bootloader's own validation.** The record's fire protocol used `exp.sh`, which writes the
   image a specific way; our manual `mtd write` may not reproduce it. NOTE: the read-back md5 equals
   the file's md5, so the BYTES are right - but the record's `8cebc05..15efe8f` family wrote via a
   different tool and there may be an alignment or a header the bootloader needs beyond the uImage
   header, with the rest of the slot in a state our erase left different from the known-good runs.
3. **Something environmental on the bench** - but the vendor kernel boots from slot A perfectly on
   every one of those same boots, so the bench, the cable, the power and the failover all work.

**THE NEXT STEP IS HOST-SIDE AND IT IS THE ONE THING NEVER COMPARED: what EXACTLY is in the rest of
slot B, byte for byte, in a build that booted versus ours?** We hold `build/tmp/fire2/kernelb-backup.bin`

bootloader was happily booting from at some point. Diffing its post-image region against what our
write leaves is free, needs no fire, and has never been done.


# ★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★
# PHASE 70 (2026-10-11): ★ THE BUG IS FOUND - I WAS FLASHING A BARE uImage ★
# WHEN THE SLOT REQUIRES kernel + THREE DEVICE TREES
# ★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★★

## THE MEASUREMENT (host-side, free, from a slot that the bootloader booted)

`build/tmp/fire2/kernelb-backup.bin` - the slot B content captured BEFORE tonight's writes - maps as:

    @0x000000  uImage  size=4,294,096 B   ends 0x418610
    @0x418610  DTB      size=31,220 B     ends 0x420004
    @0x420064  DTB      size=4,592 B      ends 0x421254
    @0x421254  DTB      size=4,920 B      ends 0x4227FF
    non-ff region total: 4,335,616 B of the 8,650,752 B partition

**The kernelb slice is: the kernel uImage PLUS THREE device tree blobs** - the base DTB and two
overlays. The record already says so, in its own words:

> "vendor slice: uImage 4294160 B + base DTB 31220 B + **overlays 4592 + 4920 B** = 4334892 B"

and the CI lane produces exactly that set (`linux-5.10.201/arch/arm/boot/dts/luofu-r116.dtb` +
`luofu-uImage`, with the overlay DTBs from the dtbs build).

## ★ WHAT I DID WRONG, IN ONE LINE ★

**Every image fired tonight was a BARE uImage (~3.65 MB) with NOTHING appended, written after
`flash_eraseall` wiped the whole slot - so all three device trees were erased and never replaced.**

    our write leaves  : [uImage 3.65 MB][ff ff ff ... to the end of the 8.25 MB partition]
    the slot requires : [uImage][base DTB][overlay DTB][overlay DTB][ff...]

The bootloader reads the kernel, then looks for the device tree it has always had there, finds erased
flash, and **never enters the kernel** - which is EXACTLY what the poison protocol reported, five
separate times: C18 is never overwritten, because the kernel'first instruction never runs.

## WHY THIS SURVIVED SEVEN FIRES

It explains every observation and is invisible to every test we ran:

- the poison intact in every fire -> correct: the bootloader never hands control over;
- the vendor failover works -> correct: the bootloader treated the slot as invalid;
- removing the driver/config/head-reader changed nothing -> correct: none of it is ever reached;
- the compiler made no difference -> correct: same reason;
- the read-back md5 matched -> correct: OUR bytes were written exactly, they were just the WRONG SET
  of bytes for the slot;
- and the record's `exp.sh` path (which booted 50em/50en) writes the full slice, so it never hit this.

**THE LESSON, AND IT IS THE SESSION'S OWN: I verified the TRANSFER (md5 of what I sent == what landed)
and never verified the LAYOUT (that what I sent was the thing the consumer expects).** The md5 match
felt like proof and was proof of the wrong proposition. That is the same shape as the `cp -r` stale
source earlier tonight: check the artifact against the CONSUMER'S contract, not against your own copy.

## THE FIX (host-side, ready to test)

Build the full slice and write it: uImage + luofu-r116.dtb + the two overlay DTBs, in that order, at
offset 0 of the slot. The base DTB is what our build already produces
(`build/luofu-kernel-image/luofu-r116.dtb`); the two overlays need identifying from the backup (they
are at known offsets and sizes) or from the vendor vendor's dtb set.

**NEXT: reconstruct the slice from the backup + our uImage and fire it.**

## THE TEST THAT SEPARATED PATH FROM BUILD

Eight fires failed identically through a MANUAL flash procedure
(`flash_eraseall` + `mtd write` + `boot_reg=0x21` + `bootflag=b` + reboot), and never once did a
build of ours boot. Before bisecting further, the question was whether the PATH or the BUILD is at
fault. So a **known-good image was fired through the identical manual procedure**.

**The known-good image:** `build/tmp/fire2/kernelb-backup.bin` (8,650,752 B, md5 `15c71e4f...`) - the
contents of slot B captured before any of tonight's writes, i.e. a slot the bootloader was booting.

**Result:**

    down -> back in ~63 s
    boot_reg = 0x11        <-- SLOT B, and NOT reset (the failover did not fire)
    bootflag = b
    ubi0 on  = mtd14       <-- rootfsb = SLOT B
    kernel   = Linux WR3000 5.10.201   (the vendor kernel)
    C18      = 0xA5A5A5A5  (still the poison - correct: the VENDOR kernel never writes it)

**THE MANUAL FLASH PATH WORKS PERFECTLY.** The same procedure, the same slot, the same selectors, and
the board boots slot B and stays there - with the selectors NOT reverting, which is the signature of a
SUCCESSFUL B boot versus every previous failure.

## ★ WHAT THIS SETTLES ★

- **The `boot_reg` reset is a SUCCESS INDICATOR, not a side effect.** After every failed B boot it read
  `10`; after this successful one it reads `11`. That is a cheap, reliable pass/fail signal for all
  future fires: **if `boot_reg` is still `0x11` after the reboot, the slot BOOTED.**
- **Our builds are genuinely the problem** - the 0017/0020 content class the record named on
  2026-10-09 and never finished characterising ("Next pass: bisect the content class systematically").
  Everything the record has been built on since then has been built on a base that was never
