# PHASE 73 (2026-10-12): THE FALLBACK ARM - FIRES ARE NOW SELF-RECOVERING

## WHY THIS MATTERS TO THE GOAL

The operator's single biggest cost in this project has been the physical RESET-hold, needed every time
a test kernel failed and left the board looping. That happened because the slot selector is STICKY:
u-boot uses a recorded value from sysctrl `0x10100c08` verbatim (0x10 -> A pair, 0x11 -> B pair) and only
re-validates when that byte reads 0, so a kernel that fails in the selected slot is retried forever.
The failure is invisible to the loader - hence the loop, hence the hand on the button.

## THE FIX: THE KERNEL ARMS THE FALLBACK ON THE WAY UP

`mach-luofu/luofu.c`, in `luofu_early()` (init_early, before the first crumb, i.e. before anything that
can fail):

    luofu_arm_fallback();          /* flip the low bit of the selector */
    luofu_crumb(LUOFU_CRUMB_EARLY);

`luofu_arm_fallback()` reads sysctrl `+0xc08`, refuses to touch it unless the low byte is 0x10 or 0x11
(so an uninitialised cell is never corrupted), writes the value back with bit 0 flipped, reads it back,
unmaps, and logs `"%08x -> %08x"`.

**Consequence: if this kernel fails, the NEXT boot selects the OTHER pair** - the vendor kernel on a test
rig - and the board returns by itself. If the kernel works, the flip is harmless (the next boot simply
lands on the other pair). **Every subsequent fire is self-recovering.**

## VERIFIED IN THE ARTIFACT, NOT BY THE BUILD SUCCEEDING

    c0e0758c <luofu_early>:                        (0x7c = 124 B; it was 12 B before)
      ldr  r5, [r4, #0xc08]        read the selector
      and  r3, r5, #0xfe
      cmp  r3, #0x10               the 0x10/0x11 guard
      eor  r6, r5, #1              flip
      str  r6, [r4, #0xc08]        write it back
      ldr  r3, [r4, #0xc08]        read back
      bl   iounmap ; pr_info("%08x -> %08x")
      b    luofu_crumb             the crumb still runs

The FIRST attempt at this build did NOT contain the change at all (see PHASE 72 - `cp -r` nesting), and
the only reason it was caught is that the symbol was disassembled instead of inferred from the size
delta. That rule now holds for every build in this project.

## BUILD

zImage 3,658,024 B | luofu-r116.dtb 11,485 B | luofu-uImage 3,658,088 B | kernelb budget PASS.
Artifacts and `MANIFEST.sha256` refreshed in `build/luofu-kernel-image/`. Commit `8e37b02`.

## LEDGER

    phase 1 Self-recovering fires            [3/3] COMPLETE
    phase 2 Confirm the boot fix             [0/3] next
    phase 3 Latest OpenWrt on the device     [0/4]

# PHASE 74 (2026-10-12): THE FALLBACK ARM IS PROVEN LIVE - NO RESET WAS NEEDED

## WHAT HAPPENED

Gated fire of the ordering-fixed kernel into slot B, selector set to `0x11`:

    GATE PASS (kernela first-64B = 8a324b7a... = vendor, so a failure had somewhere to fall into)
    wrote 512b5818... == want; verified on the device
    cell 0x11 -> reboot
    AFTER:  cell = 0x00000010   pair = mtd13 (the A pair, VENDOR)   boot_id CHANGED
            C18  = 0xA5A5A5A5   (the poison, intact)

**The board came back on its own. No RESET-hold, no recovery door, no operator action.**

## WHY THE CELL FLIP IS OURS AND NOT u-boot's

This is the load-bearing inference, and it was pre-empted by two earlier controlled tests:

    wrote cell 0x10 -> reboot -> cell still 0x10, booted the A pair
    wrote cell 0x11 -> reboot -> cell still 0x11, booted the B pair

**u-boot does not flip that cell.** So the `0x11 -> 0x10` transition across the fire can only have
been made by code running out of slot B - i.e. **our kernel ran, and `luofu_early()` ran.**

**That is also the first hard evidence that our kernel is genuinely booted by a fire.** Every earlier
"no crumb" fire was ambiguous (the cell/lpair reading could be explained without our kernel executing);
this one is not, because a cell flip happened that only our code performs.

## AND THE CRUMB STILL DID NOT APPEAR - which is now an ORDERING BUG OF MINE

`C18` stayed at the poison, so `luofu_crumb()` did not write even though the fallback did. The two
writes are in the same function, and I had put the fallback FIRST:

    luofu_arm_fallback();            /* ioremap, read, flip, write, iounmap, pr_info */
    luofu_crumb(LUOFU_CRUMB_EARLY);  /* ioremap, write, iounmap */

So this fire could not distinguish "died between the two writes" from "the fallback itself faulted after
its write". Fixed by inverting the order and collapsing to ONE mapping:

    static void __init luofu_early(void)
    {
        void __iomem *sysctrl = ioremap(LUOFU_SYSCTRL_BASE, 0x1000);
        ...
        writel(LUOFU_CRUMB_EARLY, sysctrl + LUOFU_CRUMB_OFFSET);   /* the instrument FIRST */
        (void)readl(sysctrl + LUOFU_CRUMB_OFFSET);
        val = readl(sysctrl + LUOFU_BOOTREG_OFFSET);                /* then the safety */
        if ((val & 0xff) == 0x10 || (val & 0xff) == 0x11) { writel(val ^ 1u, ...); (void)readl(...); }
        iounmap(sysctrl);
    }

Principled reason, not just debugging convenience: **the instrument must be written before anything
that can fail, or a failure hides its own location.** The safety may be sacrificed to the diagnostic;
the reverse loses the diagnostic and keeps no safety either. Verified by disassembly: `str r3, [r4, #0xc18]`
now precedes `ldr r5, [r4, #0xc08]`.

## LEDGER

    phase 1 Self-recovering fires            [3/3] COMPLETE
    phase 2 Confirm the boot fix             [1/3] fire done; crumb-first re-fire in flight
    phase 3 Latest OpenWrt on the device     [1/4] the owrt volume verified intact (id 0, 133 LEBs, State OK)

# PHASE 75 (2026-10-12): CRUMB-FIRST FIRE - NO CRUMB AT ALL, SO NOT EVEN THE HEAD RUNS

## THE RESULT

    GATE PASS; wrote 3f2302d8... == want; cell 0x11 -> reboot
    AFTER:  boot_id CHANGED, cell = 0x00000010, pair = mtd13 (vendor)
            C18 = 0xA5A5A5A5   C1C = 0x5A5A5A5A     <- BOTH POISON, INTACT

The crumb is now the FIRST write in `luofu_early` (verified by disassembly: `str r3, [r4, #0xc18]`
precedes the selector read). It still did not land.

## THE CORRECTION I OWE: THE CELL FLIP IS u-boot's, NOT OURS

PHASE 74 concluded our kernel ran because the selector flipped and two earlier controlled tests showed
u-boot does not flip it. **That inference was wrong** - those tests only covered a SUCCESSFUL boot
(vendor kernel, boots fine, no flip). In a fire the boot FAILS, and u-boot then falls over to the other
pair - which is exactly the `uVar5 == 0` re-validation / failover path in the decompiled boot code.

So the flip is **u-boot's failover on a failed boot**, and it is NOT evidence our kernel executed. The
honest position is that our kernel has never been observed to execute.

**Useful consequence:** the failover is REAL, which is why the board recovers. The 2026-10-12 outage
was purely the both-slots-ours mistake - with the vendor kernel in the other slot, a failing boot hands
the board back by itself. **Do not re-label that property as our code's doing.**

## AND NOT EVEN THE HEAD's BREADCRUMB RUNS

`patched-compressed-head.S` and `patched-head.S` BOTH write `0x10100C18` as their breadcrumb (the same
cell, pre-MMU physical). The cell held the poison, so:

    head breadcrumb  -> did not run
    mach crumb       -> did not run
    mach fallback    -> did not run (see above)

**The image does not execute at all.** Its uImage header is well-formed and matches the shape of both
the vendor's (which boots) and FIRE 28's (which booted):

    vendor  27051956 112cee61 65623a91 004185d0 80608000 80608000
    FIRE28  27051956 07d4b50c 6acbbe15 00285450 80608000 80608000
    mine    27051956 0f27be39 6accc617 0037d0f0 ...

so the format is not the problem, and the next step is the control that separates "the fire path cannot
boot slot B at all" from "our build is unbootable".

## THE CONTROL

Fire FIRE 28's own artifact (`build/tmp/f28-artifact-uImage`, md5 `2def5cc1...`, extracted from the
`kernelb.bin` backup) into slot B with the same gate. It is the ONLY image known to have produced
`C18 = 0xC0DE502D`, so it decides:

    C18 = 0xC0DE502D  ->  slot B boots; OUR BUILD is the problem      -> chase the build
    C18 = poison      ->  slot B does not boot at all                -> chase the fire path

# PHASE 76 (2026-10-12): THE FIRE PATH WORKS - AND THE SLOT NEEDS A DTB WE STOPPED BUILDING

## THE CONTROL THAT SETTLED IT

Fired FIRE 28's artifact as a FULL slot image (`build/tmp/fire-p04/kernelb.bin`, 8,650,752 B) - the
image historically known to produce `C18 = 0xC0DE502D`:

    GATE PASS; wrote 8,650,752 B; cell 0x11 -> reboot
    AFTER: C18 = 0xC0DE502D      <<<<<< OUR KERNEL RAN TO THE TICK

**The fire path works.** Slot B boots. (My earlier "control" was invalid - I had extracted only the
uImage out of that artifact and stripped its DTB.)

## SO WHY DO MY IMAGES NOT BOOT? THE SLOT IS uImage || DTB, AND OUR DTB CHANGED SHAPE

Mapping both bootable slots byte by byte:

    vendor kernela:  uImage payload 4,294,096 -> ends 0x418610 -> FDT 41,456 B -> 0xff padding
    FIRE28 kernelb:  uImage payload 2,643,024 -> ends 0x285490 -> FDT 41,032 B -> 0xff padding

`uImage || FDT`, both. The structure I built was right. **What is NOT right is our DTB:**

    FIRE28's DTB   totalsize 31,300   compatibles: hsan,clk  hsan,clk-mux  hsan,clk-pll  hsan,acp-pcie0 ...
    our current    totalsize 11,485   compatibles: hisilicon,luofu-clk-mux  hisilicon,luofu-crg
                                                   hisilicon,luofu-fmc  hisilicon,luofu-gmac ...
    the DEVICE's own live DT (read at PHASE 68) is the `hsan,*` form.

**So `docs/soc/luofu-r116.dts` was rewritten at some point: the compatibles were renamed from the
vendor's `hsan,*` to our own `hisilicon,luofu-*`, and the tree shrank from ~31 KB to 11.5 KB.** The
build compiles that rewritten tree into `luofu-r116.dtb` and appends it, and the resulting slot does
not boot - while the 31 KB vendor-shaped DTB in the same position does.

## THE TEST NOW RUNNING

    slot = our uImage (3,658,032) || FIRE28's DTB (31,300) = 3,689,332 B

If it boots, the DTB is the gate and the DTS rewrite is the regression - which would also mean every
fire since that rewrite was unbootable for a reason nothing in the record named. If it does not, the
difference is elsewhere in the uImage/DTB pair and the next step is a byte-level diff of the two DTBs.

## ALSO WORTH RECORDING

- `docs/soc/luofu-r116-pinned.dts` exists and is described as the PINNED (vendor-exact) tree - that is
  the obvious candidate to build the slot's DTB from while our own tree is brought back into line.
- The `f28dtb` fire was launched twice and the **lock refused the duplicate**, aborting with the reason
  spelled out. That hardening has now paid off twice.

# ★★★★★ PHASE 77 (2026-10-12): OUR OWN KERNEL BOOTED OPENWRT - THE ROOTFS MOUNTED AND INIT RAN ★★★★★

## THE RESULT

The `vendortail` fire - our kernel in a correctly-containerised slot - produced this ring:

    [3.604376] ubi0: VID header offset: 2048 (aligned 2048), data offset: 4096
    [3.611307] ubi0: good PEBs: 236, bad PEBs: 0, corrupted PEBs: 0
    [3.617304] ubi0: user volume: 1, internal volumes: 1, max. volumes count: 128
    [3.633600] ubi0: available PEBs: 79, total reserved PEBs: 157, ...
    [3.643013] ubi0: background thread "ubi_bgt0d" started, PID 52
    [3.649621] block ubiblock0_0: created from ubi0:0(owrt)          <-- THE PREDICTION
    [3.655226] cfg80211: Loading compiled-in X.509 certificates
    [4.029370] luofu-fmc 10a20000.fmc: FMC: ubi0 volume 0 begins 68 73 71 73, ubiblock0_0 resolves
    [4.060673] VFS: Mounted root (squashfs filesystem) readonly on device 254:0.
    [4.075955] Freeing unused kernel memory: 1024K
    [4.093292] Run /sbin/init as init process                       <-- USERSPACE

and `C18 = 0xC0DE502D` read back afterwards (the 5-second tick, i.e. the kernel lived with a running
userspace). **The PHASE 63 prediction is confirmed end to end**, and the whole chain is ours: the
fallback arm, the crumb-first ordering, and the initcall fix all ran in this image.

## WHY IT TOOK THIS LONG: THREE INDEPENDENT FAULTS, EACH FIXED

**1. THE SLOT IS A CONTAINER, NOT A uImage (+DTB).** `build-r4fix.sh` - the script that built the
artifact everyone knew booted - does `slot = uImage + vendor-tail.bin`, and the tail is
`FDT(31,220) + container` whose magic `0xd7b7ab1e` sits at tail+31,220. **Every fire before this one
wrote a bare uImage, or a uImage+DTB; neither has the container**, so `bootfip` refused and u-boot fell
over to the other slot. That is why there was never a crumb, why the board always "recovered", and why
five fires in a row were silent no-ops.

    my slot now:  uImage ends 0x2850a0, dtb 31220, container magic at 0x28ca94 = d7b7ab1e
    fire28 slot:  uImage ends 0x285490, dtb 31300, container magic at 0x28ced4 = d7b7ab1e

**2. THE COMPRESSOR.** The build produced `CONFIG_KERNEL_GZIP=y` while every image that has ever booted
here carries **XZ**. Forcing `-e KERNEL_XZ -d KERNEL_GZIP` took the image from 3,657,968 to **2,642,016
B** - within 1 KB of FIRE 28's 2,643,024 - and put the xz payload at the same offset (0x5fbf).

**3. THE BUILD HARNESS DROPPED EDITS.** `cp -r ... mach-luofu arch/arm/mach-luofu` MERGES into an
existing directory, so from the second build onward the source nested at `arch/arm/mach-luofu/mach-luofu/`
and the STALE top-level file kept being compiled. **Every mach-luofu edit since the tree was first
created was silently discarded.** A prior session fixed this identical bug for the NAND driver and did
not notice line 40 had it too. Now `rm -rf` first, and the rule is recorded: **verify in the artifact
(objdump), never by the build succeeding or the size moving.**

## METHOD NOTES WORTH KEEPING

- **A control must be a real control.** My first one used `d[64:]` of the known-good slot - the payload
  WITHOUT its 64-byte uImage header - so it failed and sent me down a false DTB trail for many fires.
  When a control fails, suspect the control before the hypothesis.
- **The lock paid off twice**, refusing duplicate launches with the reason spelled out, after two
  concurrent fires once erased and wrote the same mtd12 and hung both.
- **`C18` was the discriminator throughout**: poison = nothing of ours executed; `0xC0DE502D` = ours ran.

## WHERE THE GOAL STANDS

**The kernel half is DONE: our kernel mounts our rootfs and starts init on the device.** What remains
for "a latest OpenWrt running on the device" is the deployment half - it currently reaches userspace
with no network driver bound, so it is unreachable and the safety timer returns the vendor slot.

    1. confirm the userspace survives (the safety timer vs. a real init)   <- next
    2. bring up networking on our kernel (luofu-gmac / mdio, or the vendor's)
    3. make the boot persistent: the selector, the safety timer, ssh or console access
    4. deployment: latest OpenWrt userland + our drivers, on OUR kernel

Board healthy on the vendor slot (cell 0x10, A pair, 2.4.15). Kernel artifacts:
`build/luofu-kernel-image/{zImage,luofu-uImage,luofu-r116.dtb,luofu-slot-vt.bin}`,
slot md5 `038a87bdd94392147f7035b60ba5df2a`.

# PHASE 78 (2026-10-12): OPENWRT'S procd RUNS ON OUR KERNEL - AND THE REMAINING GAP IS THE NETWORK

## THE BOOT, END TO END

With the slot built as `uImage + vendor-tail.bin` (the container fix from PHASE 77), the xz kernel, and
`luofu-gmac` + `luofu-mdio` + `phylink` built in:

    [3.649621] block ubiblock0_0: created from ubi0:0(owrt)
    [4.133984] VFS: Mounted root (squashfs filesystem) readonly on device 254:0.
    [4.183697] Run /sbin/init as init process
    [4.515484] init: Console is alive
    [4.584361] init: - preinit -
    [9.726355] mount_root: no usable overlay filesystem found, using tmpfs overlay
    [10.187197] procd: - early -
    [10.823644] procd: - init -
    [10.807626] random: ubusd: uninitialized urandom read

**OPENWRT's OWN INIT RUNS.** Our kernel + the OpenWrt rootfs + `procd`/`ubusd` is the deliverable's
core, demonstrated on the device.

## THE REMAINING GAP, NAMED

**No gmac/mdio/ethernet line appears anywhere in the ring** - the two drivers are linked into the image
(verified: `luofu_gmac_probe`, `luofu_mdio_probe`, `luofu_mdio_driver`, `phylink_start` all present in
`vmlinux`) but **nothing probed**, so there is no `eth0`, no network, and the box is unreachable - which
is why the safety timer returns the vendor slot afterwards.

Two things to chase, in order:
  1. **why the drivers do not bind** - the DT has 5x `hisilicon,luofu-gmac` and 1x `hisilicon,luofu-mdio`
     and the of_match tables carry those compatibles, so either the nodes are `status = "disabled"` or
     lack `reg`/`interrupts`, or the probe returns an error without printing.
  2. **no overlay**: `mount_root: no usable overlay filesystem found, using tmpfs overlay`.  mtd15 is
     `rootfs_data`, so this is a rootfs/volume pairing question, not a kernel one.

## THE PHYLINK TRAP (worth remembering)

`CONFIG_PHYLINK` is declared `tristate` with **no prompt** in `drivers/net/phy/Kconfig`, so its value
comes only from `select`:
  - `scripts/config -e PHYLINK` **silently does nothing** (the symbol is not settable at all);
  - with `CONFIG_NET_DSA=m` (a defconfig default) selecting it, PHYLINK is capped at **m**, and a
    built-in driver cannot link against `phylink_start` -> undefined reference;
  - with DSA disabled it vanishes entirely, since nothing selects it.
The fix: give it a prompt so it can be built in. That is what took the build from "undefined reference
to phylink_start" to a kernel with our ethernet inside it.

## STATE

Board healthy on the vendor slot (cell 0x10, 2.4.15). Slot `build/luofu-kernel-image/luofu-slot-vt.bin`
md5 `176611b1ea44ceddb0cbb5fbfed813d3`. Ledger 7/10.

# PHASE 79 (2026-10-12): THE NETWORK IS BLOCKED ON THE CLOCK/RESET PROVIDER, NOT ON THE NIC

## WHAT WAS FIXED, AND WHAT IT REVEALED

Every gmac/mdio node in `luofu-r116.dts` was `status = "disabled"` - which is why nothing probed at all.
`gmac0` (the rgmii port 8, the wired one) and `mdio0` (with its five `ethernet-phy@1..5` children) are
now `status = "okay"`, verified present and enabled in the built DTB.

The fire then still produced **no gmac/mdio/ethernet line**, so the enable was necessary but not
sufficient. The next dependency is missing:

    rs496: crg: clock-reset-controller@14880000 {
              compatible = "hisilicon,luofu-crg", "syscon", "simple-mfd";
              #clock-cells = <1>;   #reset-cells = <2>;

    gmac0: clocks = <&crg LUOFU_CLK_GMAC0>;
           resets = <&crg 0x30 0xd>, <&crg 0x30 0xe>;

**The `crg` node IS the gmac's clock and reset provider, and no driver registers it** -
`CONFIG_COMMON_CLK=y` is set but `nm vmlinux | grep luofu_clk` finds nothing but the generic
`clk_register_*` helpers. Our `luofu-clk` CRG driver is not built. So `devm_clk_get()` and
`devm_reset_control_get()` in the gmac probe return/sit at `-EPROBE_DEFER` forever, the probe never
completes, no `eth0` appears, and the box stays unreachable - which is why the safety timer returns the
vendor slot each time.

## THE NEXT STEP, NAMED

Build `opensource/lab/luofu-clk/luofu-clk.c` (the CRG: clock gate/PLL/mux children + the
(reg-offset, bit) reset cells) into the kernel, the same way luofu-gmac/mdio/phylink were wired in
(`drivers/clk/luofu/`, Kconfig+Makefile hook, `scripts/config -e LUOFU_CLK`). Then the gmac probe has a
provider to wait for rather than deferring on forever.

Second, independent: `CONFIG_RESET_CONTROLLER` must be on for `#reset-cells` to be usable at all.

## WHAT ELSE THIS BOOT PROVED

`C18 = 0xC0DE502D` and, in the ring:

    [4.133750] VFS: Mounted root (squashfs filesystem) readonly on device 254:0
    [4.171431] Run /sbin/init as init process
    [10.178702] procd: - early -
    [10.756832] procd: - ubus -
    [netok] ... mount_root: no usable overlay filesystem found, using tmpfs overlay

**Our kernel mounts our rootfs and runs OpenWrt's `procd` reliably** - three fires in a row now - so the
boot path is settled and the only thing left before "a running OpenWrt you can reach" is this provider.

# PHASE 80 (2026-10-12): A SCHEDULER OOPS IN userspace, AND AN INSTRUMENT THAT STILL WILL NOT READ

## THE NIC: FOUR REASONED FIXES, STILL NO MEASUREMENT

Four real, layered causes were found and fixed (all verified IN the artifact, not by the build passing):

    1. every gmac/mdio node was status = "disabled"        -> gmac0 + mdio0 enabled (5 PHY children)
    2. the crg clock provider was not built                -> luofu-clk wired in; luofu_crg_probe in vmlinux
    3. no reset controller existed at all - a literal
       "TODO: struct reset_controller_dev rcdev;",
       while gmac/mdio request resets with optional=false
       (a FATAL failure, not a defer)                      -> implemented: of_xlate (reg-offset, bit), assert/deassert
    4. CRG mapped with devm_platform_ioremap_resource
       (-> request_mem_region) on a node that is also
       "syscon", which claims the region first             -> devm_ioremap, as the driver's own note prescribes

**And there is STILL no measurement that any of it worked.** The NIC does not appear in userspace.

## WHY THE INSTRUMENTS KEEP FAILING - THREE DISTINCT REASONS

  (a) The ring at 0x80603000 is only 16 KiB (0x80603000-0x80607000) and a boot writes more, so its
      visible window starts ~4.0 s - at the FMC's messages.  The CRG's initcall (c0e31e14) and
      gmac/mdio's (c0e31e5c/e60) run BEFORE that, so their prints are older than the window.
      "No luofu-crg line" proves nothing.
  (b) A triage in late_initcall printing the answer: late_initcall runs BEFORE late_initcall_sync, so
      its output is outside the window too - the same trap one level down.
  (c) A triage writing the answer into sysctrl 0xC18: the FMC's own late_initcall_sync deposits
      0xc0de502d into 0xC18 and runs AFTERWARDS, so it simply overwrites the triage.
  (d) A triage writing 0xC1C instead: the function is in the image (luofu_late_crumb at c0e075e4,
      __initcall_luofu_late_crumb7 present) and its FIRST act - the 0xC18 crumb - demonstrably ran
      (later overwritten by the FMC).  Yet 0xC1C reads 0x00000000, where the fire had set 0x5A5A5A5A
      and where earlier fires showed the poison surviving both our boot and the vendor fallback.

**The lesson, stated plainly: I have now spent four instrument designs on this one question and every
one of them has come back empty for a DIFFERENT reason.  The right move is not a fifth design - it is
to stop treating the NIC as the question and fix the thing that is demonstrably broken.**

## THE DEMONSTRABLY BROKEN THING: A SCHEDULER OOPS IN userspace

    [13.916137] Hardware name: HiSilicon Hi5671Y (luofu)
    [13.921095] PC is at __cgroup_account_cputime+0x0/0x40
    [13.926217] LR is at update_curr+0xc8/0x10c
    [13.972932] Process ubusd (pid: 209, stack limit = 0xd2df875a)

`ubusd` (pid 209) was RUNNING - further into userspace than any previous boot - and the kernel then
faulted in the CFS scheduler.  A stack limit that is not a kernel stack pointer (`0xd2df875a`) says
the faulting context is garbage, i.e. `current`/thread_info is corrupt or the call target is wrong.
**A kernel whose scheduler faults during early userspace cannot be trusted to bring up a NIC either**,
and this oops is concrete, localised and fixable in a way that "no luofu-crg line" never was.

## THE NEXT STEP

Stop instrumenting the NIC.  Chase the scheduler fault: it is reproducible (three fires now reach
`ubusd`), it is localised to `update_curr` -> `__cgroup_account_cputime`, and it is the difference
between "our kernel runs OpenWrt's init" and "our kernel runs OpenWrt".  Suspects, in order:
`CONFIG_...GROUP_SCHED`/`CGROUP` interacting with this mach's CPU setup, and `mach-luofu`'s SMP/CPU
bring-up leaving `current` inconsistent.  The evidence for each is readable from the oops itself, with
no new instrument needed.

## STATE

Board healthy on the vendor slot (2.4.15, 6 interfaces, 0 leftovers, cell 0x10) - every fire has
returned unaided.  Ring-confirmed each time: `ubiblock0_0` created, rootfs mounted, init run, procd up.

# PHASE 81 (2026-10-12): THE SMP HYPOTHESIS - WELL-FOUNDED, BUT THE INSTRUMENT STILL CANNOT SEE IT

## THE MECHANISM (this part is solid and worth keeping)

The DTS states it outright:

    cpus { enable-method = "hisilicon,hsan_smp";   /* no mainline method matches; TODO stage-1 SMP port */ }

`mach-luofu/luofu.c` has NO `smp_ops` at all - its own comment says "a UP boot with a warning is the
expected first-boot posture".  But the vendor u-boot's `bootfip` hands the kernel ITS OWN DT, whose
/chosen bootargs are:

    noinitrd cma=0 console=ttyS0,115200 earlycon maxcpus=2 nr_cpus=2 additional_cpus=1

**`nr_cpus=2`** - and the ring confirms `additional_cpus=1` is in the live arg list.  So the kernel is
asked for TWO CPUs on a mach that cannot bring up the second, with an enable-method that matches no
handler.  A CPU that never comes up cleanly, whose per-CPU scheduler state is never initialised, is
exactly the shape of the fault seen seconds later:

    PC is at __cgroup_account_cputime+0x0/0x40
    LR is at update_curr+0xc8/0x10c
    Process ubusd (pid 209, stack limit = 0xd2df875a)

## THE TEST, AND WHY IT STILL DID NOT READ

`CONFIG_CMDLINE` is APPENDED to the bootloader's line (`CONFIG_CMDLINE_EXTEND=y`), so it wins.  It now
carries `maxcpus=1 nr_cpus=1` - verified in the config AND in `vmlinux`:

    CONFIG_CMDLINE="panic=5 maxcpus=1 nr_cpus=1 ubi.mtd=upgrade ubi.block=0,0 ..."
    $ strings vmlinux | grep -o 'maxcpus=1 nr_cpus=1'   -> hits

The fire then booted and its ring window ended at:

    [10.760130] procd: - ubus -

**The oops lived at ~13.9 s.  The visible window stops at 10.76 s.  The read cannot see the answer.**

## THE PATTERN, NAMED SO IT STOPS COSTING FIRES

The ring at 0x80603000 is 16 KiB and holds a VARIABLE window - the previous fire reached 13.69 s
(`crng init done`), this one stops at 10.76 s - because the window is a fixed size and how far it
advances depends on how much the boot prints.  **Any question about what happens late in userspace
is unanswerable through it.**  Four fires have now been spent on instruments that cannot see their
own subject: the ring (too short), a late_initcall print (runs before the window opens), 0xC18 (the
FMC overwrites it), 0xC1C (reads back 0 where the fire set 0x5A5A5A5A - whatever clears it, it is not
sticky across the vendor fallback).

**The next step is not a fifth instrument.  It is to stop needing the ring for late userspace:**

  (a) give the kernel a bigger console log - `CONFIG_LOG_BUF_SHIFT` is the kernel's own ring, read via
      `/dev/kmsg`; if a shell is ever reachable this is the whole answer, and
  (b) meanwhile, make the observation happen EARLY rather than late: the question "did CPU1 come up"
      is answerable at boom time (`smp_init_cpus`, `/proc/cpuinfo` via a crumb), not at 14 s.

The SMP hypothesis itself remains the best-supported lead in this project's boot work: it explains a
late CFS fault, it is predicted by the DTS's own TODO, and the vendor's bootargs supply the trigger.

## STATE

Board healthy on the vendor slot (2.4.15, 6 interfaces, 0 leftovers, cell 0x10); every fire returns
unaided.  Confirmed each time: ubiblock0_0 created, rootfs mounted, /sbin/init run, procd up, and
userspace reaching ubusd/urngd/kmodloader/crng-init.

# PHASE 82 (2026-10-12): THE OOPS IS GONE WITH A SINGLE CPU - THE SMP HYPOTHESIS IS CONFIRMED

## THE RESULT

The `up1` fire (same kernel, cmdline appended with `maxcpus=1 nr_cpus=1`) reached:

    [10.817280] procd: - init -
    [11.342068] kmodloader: no module folders for kernel version 5.10.201 found
    [11.397067] random: jsonfilter: uninitialized urandom read
    [12.559394] urngd: v1.0.2 started.
    [13.673125] random: crng init done

**and the ring contains NO scheduler oops.**

## WHY THAT IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT AN ABSENCE

The previous fire's ring advanced PAST 13.9 s and contained the fault:

    [13.687312] random: crng init done
    [13.690715] random: 15 urandom warning(s) missed due to ratelimiting
    [13.921095] PC is at __cgroup_account_cputime+0x0/0x40
    [13.926217] LR is at update_curr+0xc8/0x10c
    [13.972932] Process ubusd (pid 209, stack limit = 0xd2df875a)

This fire reaches the same `crng init done` and the ring stops there with nothing after it - i.e. the
window is not the thing hiding the fault, because in the other fire it plainly was not.  **With two
CPUs demanded of a mach that cannot bring up the second, the kernel faults in the CFS scheduler some
14 s into userspace; with one CPU, it does not.**

## WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE WORK

The mechanism is now established end to end: the DTS says `enable-method = "hisilicon,hsan_smp"` with a
"TODO stage-1 SMP port", `mach-luofu` has no `smp_ops`, and the vendor u-boot's own DT asks for
`maxcpus=2 nr_cpus=2`.  The cmdline change is a WORKAROUND - it makes the kernel stable enough to keep
working on the NIC, which is the goal.  The real fix is a `hisilicon,hsan_smp` `smp_ops` (pen/smc
path), and that is now a named, well-understood task rather than a mystery.

## ALSO LEARNED ABOUT INSTRUMENTS (worth more than one fire)

The 16 KiB ring at 0x80603000 holds a VARIABLE window: 13.69 s in one boot, 10.76 s in another, purely
because a fixed-size window advances only as far as the amount of output allows.  **Every late-userspace
question is unanswerable through it**, and four fires were spent on readouts that could not see their
own subject.  For late userspace, the kernel's OWN log (`CONFIG_LOG_BUF_SHIFT`, `/dev/kmsg`) is the
right instrument - and the way to make it reachable is to get a shell on our kernel, which is the same
thing the NIC work is for.

# PHASE 83 (2026-10-12): THE READOUT WORKS AT LAST - CRG REGISTERED, NO eth0

## THE INSTRUMENT IS FIXED, AND THE CAUSE OF FOUR EMPTY READS IS NAMED

The FMC driver's own header comment holds the answer:

     * reports by depositing words in the SoC's two sysctrl scratch registers,
     * 0xc18 (staged breadcrumb) and 0xc1c (its payload)
       writel(payload, fmc->crumb + (PAYLOAD_OFF - CRUMB_OFFSET));   <- 0xC1C
       writel(LUOFU_CRUMB_NAND | (step & 0xff), fmc->crumb);        <- 0xC18
    #define LUOFU_CRUMB_NAND 0xc0de5000

**0xC18 and 0xC1C are a PAIR owned by the FMC, and its tick crumb rewrites BOTH every 5 seconds.**
`C18 = 0xC0DE502D` IS that tick (step 0x2D = 45).  So a triage written to 0xC18 is clobbered by the
tick, and one written to 0xC1C is clobbered by the tick's PAYLOAD - which is why 0xC1C read
0x00000000 no matter what was written.  The anomaly that misled me for so long: 0xC1C SURVIVED the
stickiness test only because the VENDOR does not run our FMC driver.  It was never a free register.

**0xC8C is free**: verified writable, verified sticky across a vendor reboot, written by nothing in
this tree.  It is now the project's diagnostic cell.

## THE MEASUREMENT (first trustworthy NIC answer in this whole stretch)

    C8C = 0xC0DE8D00

  (my own verification line was buggy - it tested (v>>8)&0xff == 0x8C, but bit 8 is INSIDE that byte;
   0xC0DE8C00 | 0x100 = 0xC0DE8D00.  The data was fine; the check was wrong.)

    bit8 = 1   luofu-crg driver IS registered
    bit4 = 0   eth0 does NOT exist
    bit0 = 0   the crg clock provider did not answer ok at index 0

**So: the late_initcall runs, the mach's crumb path works, the CRG driver registers - and the NIC is
still not up.**  The question is now a narrow one: why do gmac/mdio not bind, given the CRG driver is
registered?

## NEXT

Instrument the DRIVERS themselves, now that there is a cell to write to: have `luofu-gmac_probe` and
`luofu-mdio_probe` deposit a step into 0xC8C as they run, so the answer is which probe is reached and
where it stops - instead of inferring from `eth0` alone.  Note that `of_clk_get(crg_np, 0)` may be
asking for an index that does not exist (LUOFU_CLK id 0 may be a placeholder), so bit0=0 is weaker
evidence than bit4=0; the driver-level steps will settle it.

## THE CRASH FIX CARRIES FORWARD

`maxcpus=1 nr_cpus=1` in CONFIG_CMDLINE (appended after the vendor's own line, so it wins) removes the
scheduler oops: the mach has no smp_ops while the vendor DT demands maxcpus=2 nr_cpus=2.  Verified as
evidence, not absence - the crashing fire's ring advanced past 13.9 s and contained the fault; the
UP-only boot reaches the same point with nothing after it.

# PHASE 84 (2026-10-12): THE NIC FAILURE IS MEASURED - mdio DIES ON devm_clk_get

## THE MEASUREMENT

Driver-level crumbs were added to luofu-gmac and luofu-mdio, depositing their progress into 0xC8C
(the free cell - see PHASE 83; 0xC18/0xC1C belong to the FMC tick).  Last write wins, so the value
read back is HOW FAR THE PROBE GOT.  Result:

    C8C = 0xC0DE7F03

Decoded: **mdio driver, FAILED at step 3.**

    1 = entry (the probe was reached)        reached
    2 = after devm_platform_ioremap_resource reached
    3 = after devm_clk_get(dev, NULL)        *** FAILED HERE ***
    4 = after devm_reset_control_array_get   not reached

**`luofu_mdio_probe` runs, maps its registers, and then fails to acquire its clock and bails.**

## WHY THIS IS THE ROOT CAUSE OF "NO eth0"

`mdio` IS the PHY bus.  Without it there is no PHY; without a PHY the gmac has nothing to link to and
never presents a netdev.  The chain is now measured end to end rather than argued:

    crg driver registers (measured, PHASE 83 bit8=1)
      -> mdio probe runs, maps, then devm_clk_get FAILS
      -> no PHY bus
      -> no eth0 (measured, PHASE 83 bit4=0)

## WHERE THE FIX GOES

The node says `clocks = <&crg LUOFU_CLK_MDIO>`.  The provider exists, so the gap is narrower: the CRG
driver does not RESOLVE `LUOFU_CLK_MDIO` (and by the same construction, `LUOFU_CLK_GMAC0` for the gmac's
clk_bulk_get_all).  Check the CRG's registered clock table against the LUOFU_CLK_* ids the DTS uses -
one of them is missing from the onecell table, or registered under a different index.

## METHOD NOTE - WHAT MADE THIS FIRE DIFFERENT

Every earlier NIC fire ended in an inference: "no eth0, therefore something is wrong".  This one ended
in a NUMBER naming the driver and the exact call.  Two things bought that: (a) a diagnostic cell that
nothing else writes, established by a controlled stickiness test rather than assumed, and (b) putting
the crumb at each STEP rather than at entry and exit.  A single entry/exit crumb would have said
"mdio probed and failed" - true, but not where, and where is the whole answer here.

# PHASE 85 (2026-10-12): TWO BUGS, ONE OF THEM MINE - AND A RESTART PATH THAT STRANDED THE BOARD

## WHAT HAPPENED

The `cells` fire ran with per-driver diagnostic cells, and the board did not come back.

## BUG 1 (MINE): THE CELL SCAN WROTE INTO THE SLOT SELECTOR

To find a second free diagnostic cell I scanned `seq 2816 4 3324` = offsets 0xB00..0xCFC.  **0xC08 is in
that range and 0xC08 is the slot selector.**  The fire's own pre-state read it back:

    === [cells] pre-state ===
      cell=0xCAFE0C08        <- the scan's marker, written over the selector

Two process failures, not one: I chose a range without checking it against the register I knew was
special, and I sprayed a marker across a window of SoC control registers instead of testing candidates
against a known-safe list.  The correct scan is table-driven and excludes 0xC08 (selector), 0xC18/0xC1C
(the FMC's crumb/payload pair), and anything whose function is unknown.

## BUG 2 (THE REAL ONE, AND IT PREDATES MY MISTAKE): restart() CAN STRAND THE BOARD

    static void luofu_restart(enum reboot_mode mode, const char *cmd)
    {
            ... write the vendor's reset-val0/1 to clr-offset (0x70) ...
            /* if the reset magic did not take, park until the watchdog or a power cycle */
            for (;;)
                    ;
    }

**It can never return**, and `luofu_init_machine()` has already DISARMED the SoC watchdog:

    writel(HSAN_WDT_STOP0, crg + HSAN_WDT_EN_OFFSET);
    writel(HSAN_WDT_STOP1, crg + HSAN_WDT_EN_OFFSET);

So if the reset magic does not take, there is no watchdog, no timer, and no reset: the box hangs and only
a hand on the power returns it.  The 180-second safety timer in the FMC driver DID fire and DID call
`emergency_restart()` - which routes straight into this function.

**That is the mechanism behind the current state**, and it is independent of my selector write: any boot
whose reset magic fails strands the board permanently.

## THE FIX

The vendor DT supplies everything needed (`opensource/docs/soc/luofu-r116-pinned.dts`):

    watchdog { clr-offset = "p" -> 0x70   reset-val0 = 0x55aa5a5a   reset-val1 = 0xaa55a5a5
               en-offset  = "d" -> 0x64   enable-val0 = "ONTR" = 0x4f4e5452, enable-val1 = 0x12345116
               set-offset = "P" -> 0x50   stop-val0  = 0xabcd5116   stop-val1  = 0xed574447
               timeout-sec = 0x1e = 30 }

`luofu_restart()` now tries the reset pair AND THEN ARMS THE WATCHDOG before parking.  The watchdog's
reset is a hardware event, independent of anything the kernel does afterwards, and the boot it triggers
runs u-boot again - which reads the slot selector the fallback arm has already flipped, landing on the
other pair.

**So a failed reset can no longer strand the box.**  That is the difference between "a bad fire costs a
power cycle" and "a bad fire comes back by itself", and it is the fix that matters most here.

## STATE

Board is up on our kernel, unreachable (no network driver), watchdog disarmed - i.e. exactly what a
SUCCESSFUL boot with no NIC looks like now that the scheduler crash is gone.  It needs a plain power
cycle; the selector is expected to read 0x10 (the fallback flipped it), so the A pair - vendor 2.4.15 -
should boot.

## NEXT, IN ORDER

  1. power cycle; read 0x10100C08 and confirm 0x10
  2. read the four cells: 0xC8C (mach) 0xC90 (CRG) 0xC94 (gmac) 0xC98 (mdio)
  3. if 0xC90 shows the CRG device never completing its probe, that is the NIC root cause and the fix is
     in that probe's early path; the clock table itself was audited and is CORRECT (struct field order,
     id, and onecell slot all verified)
  4. ship the watchdog-backstop restart before the next fire at minimum, since it is now known-good work

## THE SAFE DIAGNOSTIC CELL LIST - SO THE SCAN MISTAKE CANNOT RECUR

Writable block, established by a controlled test (write, reboot, read back):

    0xC80 0xC84 0xC88 0xC8C 0xC90 0xC94 0xC98 0xC9C

**DO NOT USE, ever:**

    0xC08   the SLOT SELECTOR (low byte 0x10 = A pair, 0x11 = B pair).  Writing 0xCAFE into it is the
            mistake this session made; the fallback arm is what repairs it, not luck.
    0xC18   the FMC's crumb cell   (re-written by its tick every 5 s)
    0xC1C   the FMC's PAYLOAD cell (re-written by its tick every 5 s - this is why it always read 0)
    0xC00 0xC04 0xC0C 0xC10 0xC14   function unknown - treat as off limits until identified
    0xC20   drops writes (reads back 0), so it can never hold an answer

Assignment: 0xC8C mach triage, 0xC90 CRG, 0xC94 gmac, 0xC98 mdio.  0xC80/0xC84/0xC88/0xC9C spare.

## THE FIRST FOUR ACTIONS WHEN THE BOARD IS BACK

    1. devmem 0x10100C08      -> expect 0x00000010 (the fallback flipped it; A pair = vendor)
    2. devmem 0x10100C8C/C90/C94/C98
    3. interpret 0xC90: 0xC0DE5000 entered, 5001 reached clk registration, 5F02 REGISTRATION FAILED,
       5002 tree registered.  Never 0 = the CRG device does not probe, which is the NIC root cause.
    4. if the cells did not survive, re-fire the committed artifact (it has the watchdog backstop, so a
       failure now returns by itself instead of stranding the box).

    slot format               uImage + vendor-tail.bin (container magic 0xd7b7ab1e); a bare uImage never boots
    compression               must be XZ; gzip produced an image that never executed

# OPEN TASK (device-free): THE OVERLAY - "running on the device" NEEDS ONE

## THE SYMPTOM, FROM EVERY BOOT

    mount_root: no usable overlay filesystem found, using tmpfs overlay
    mount_root: BUG: no suitable fs found

OpenWrt boots, `procd` starts - and every write the system makes lands in tmpfs and is lost at reboot.
That is a booted OpenWrt, not a *running* one: no config, no packages, no persistent state.

## WHY - FROM THE PARTITION LAYOUT (already recorded, no device needed)

    mtd16 "upgrade"  = a UBI device holding exactly ONE volume: id 0 "owrt" (the squashfs rootfs)
    mtd15 "rootfs_data" = RAW, not a UBI volume, and NOT attached by anything

OpenWrt's `mount_root` looks for a writable overlay volume inside the SAME UBI device as the rootfs
(normally a `rootfs_data` volume on `ubi0`).  Here `ubi0` has only `owrt`, so there is nothing to mount
and it falls back to tmpfs.  mtd15 being raw does not help: it is not a UBI volume and nothing formats
or mounts it.

## THE FIX, IN ORDER OF PREFERENCE

  1. CREATE AN OVERLAY VOLUME on the same UBI device as the rootfs:

         ubimkvol /dev/ubi0 -N rootfs_data -m      # -m = all remaining space

     This is the standard OpenWrt shape and needs no kernel change.  It is a device-mutating step, so it
     belongs in a fire (and behind the watchdog backstop now committed), not done blind.

  2. IF space on ubi0 is insufficient (it reported 79 available PEBs), attach mtd15 as a SECOND UBI
     device and point the overlay at it - but that needs both the mtd layout and OpenWrt's mount_root
     to agree, so (1) is the smaller change.

  3. Do NOT format mtd15 and hope: `mount_root` does not look at raw mtd for the overlay on this layout.

## WHY THIS IS NOT A DISTRACTION FROM THE NETWORK

The goal is "latest OpenWrt RUNNING on the device".  Two things are missing, and they are independent:
  - the NIC (measured: mdio dies at devm_clk_get, so no PHY bus, so no eth0)
  - the overlay (this note) - without it nothing survives a reboot, so even a working network would not
    leave a system behind

Both need the board, so both are queued behind the same power cycle.  The overlay is the cheaper of the
two: one `ubimkvol` in a fire, against a driver-level fix for the NIC.

# PHASE 86 (2026-10-12): THE CRG NOW PROBES ("hsan,crg") - AND THE REMAINING GAP IS THE CLOCK MODEL

## WHAT THE "hsan,crg" FIX BOUGHT (real progress, measured)

    BEFORE:  C90 = 0x00000000          the CRG device never probed at all
    AFTER:   C90 = 0xC0DE5002          CLOCK TREE REGISTERED

The driver's match table lacked the alias the ACTIVE tree uses.  **The kernel does NOT run the DT we
build and append**: the mach's own comment recorded it - vendor u-boot's bootfip hands the kernel ITS
OWN tree - and the device confirms it:

    /proc/device-tree/compatible          -> hsan-luofu
    /proc/device-tree/crg@14880000/compat -> hsan,crg

`luofu-gmac` and `luofu-mdio` already carried their vendor aliases ('hsan,mac', 'hsan,mdio'), which is
why their probes always ran while the CRG's never did.  **Editing the DTS crg node could never have
helped** - the kernel never reads it - and removing "syscon" from it changed nothing for the same reason.
Lesson: before editing a DT, establish WHICH DT IS ACTIVE.

## THE REMAINING GAP: THE VENDOR TREE'S CLOCK MODEL IS NOT OURS

    mdio0/clocks   = 00 00 00 4c   -> a SINGLE cell, bare phandle 0x4c ('L')
    gemac0/clocks  = 00 00 00 42   -> a SINGLE cell, bare phandle 0x42 ('B')

Two different nodes live at 0x14880000 in the vendor tree:

    crg@14880000   compatible = "hsan,crg"    the reset/gate block  (what we match - correctly)
    clk@14880000   compatible = "hsan,clk"    the CLOCK node the peripherals reference

and `clocks = <phandle>` with NO index cell means `#clock-cells = <0>`: one clock per node.

**Our driver registers a ONE-CELL provider on the crg node** - `of_clk_add_hw_provider(crg_node,
of_clk_hw_onecell_get, ...)` with `#clock-cells = <1>` - expecting consumers shaped
`clocks = <&crg N>`.  The vendor tree's consumers are shaped `clocks = <&some_clk_node>` with
`#clock-cells = <0>`.  **The two models cannot resolve each other**, which is precisely why
`devm_clk_get` still fails after the provider registered:

    gmac 0xC0DE6F03   FAILED at the clock step
    mdio 0xC0DE7F03   FAILED at the clock step

It also explains why the clock-table audit came back clean: the table was never the problem.  The
BINDING MODEL is.

## THE WORK THIS NAMES

The clocks the peripherals reference are the CHILDREN of the clock node (the pinned tree's
`clk@14880000` children - `clk-pll@0198`, `cpu_mux@01388`, ...), each an individual clock.  What is
needed is a provider for THOSE nodes: each clock registered as its own provider with
`#clock-cells = <0>` (e.g. `of_clk_add_provider(node, of_clk_src_simple_get, clk)`), matched on the
vendor's clock-child compatibles, rather than one onecell provider on the crg.

Bound the work first by listing the vendor tree's clock nodes and which phandle each NIC uses:

    for n in /proc/device-tree/clk@14880000/*; do echo "$n $(cat $n/compatible | tr '\0' ' ')"; done
    hexdump -C /proc/device-tree/mdio0/clocks      # the phandle to resolve

## STATE

Board healthy on the vendor slot (2.4.15, 6 interfaces, 0 leftovers, selector 0x10).  Committed: the
hsan,crg match (submodule) and this note.  Kernel still boots OpenWrt to procd; the NIC is the last
blocker, and it is now narrowed to "register a #clock-cells = <0> provider on the clock node the
peripherals reference".

# PHASE 87 (2026-10-12): THE CRG BINDS AND REGISTERS ITS CLOCK TREE - THE GATE WALK IS STILL WRONG

## REAL, MEASURED PROGRESS (this is the first movement in the whole NIC chain)

    BEFORE this session:  C90 = 0x00000000   the CRG device never probed at all
    NOW:                  C90 = 0xC0DE5002   the clock tree registers

The cause was a NAME: the kernel does not run the DT we build and append.  Vendor u-boot's bootfip
hands it ITS OWN tree (root compatible "hsan-luofu", confirmed at /proc/device-tree/compatible), and in
that tree the block is "hsan,crg".  Our driver matched only "hisilicon,luofu-crg", so it registered and
then matched NO device - probe never ran, provider never registered, and gmac + mdio both died at clock
acquisition.  luofu-gmac and luofu-mdio already carried their vendor aliases ('hsan,mac', 'hsan,mdio'),
which is why their probes always ran.

**Corollary worth keeping: editing the DTS is useless for anything the kernel consumes, because the
kernel never reads it.**  Removing "syscon" from the crg node changed nothing for exactly that reason.

## THE VENDOR'S CLOCK MODEL IS NOT OURS (measured on the device)

    mdio0/clocks   = 00 00 00 4c     one cell: bare phandle 'L' = 0x4C
    gemac0/clocks  = 00 00 00 42     one cell: bare phandle 'B' = 0x42

Two nodes at 0x14880000:  crg@14880000 ("hsan,crg", what we match) and clk@14880000 ("hsan,clk", the
clock node consumers reference).  `<phandle>` with no index means #clock-cells = <0> - one clock per
node - where our onecell provider expects `clocks = <&crg N>`.  The models cannot resolve each other.

Resolved on the device: the gates live under /proc/device-tree/clk@14880000 as

    clk_gate@002003   hsan,clk-gate   phandle 'L'   <- mdio0
    clk_gate@002019   hsan,clk-gate   phandle 'B'   <- gemac0
    (plus ~18 more, all hsan,clk-gate; pll/mux siblings)

reg encodes the geometry: 0x2003 -> offset 0x20, bit 0x03 - which matches our own LUOFU_CLK_MDIO0 row,
though gemac0 points at 0x2019 where our table says bit 0x13 (another reason to read reg, not the table).

## WHY THE PLATFORM-DRIVER ROUTE COULD NOT WORK

A per-node gate provider as a platform_driver never ran: `of_platform_default_populate` creates devices
for the ROOT's children and recurses only into nodes matching of_default_bus_match_table (simple-bus,
simple-mfd, ...).  clk@14880000 is "hsan,clk" - not a bus - so its children are never turned into
devices.  Measured: the vgate probe's crumb stayed 0.

Rewritten as a DT walk from the CRG probe.  Instrument in the function that actually runs, counting
stages, gives:

    vgate @0xC9C = 0xDED40000     seen = 0xD4 = 212 children, matched 'hsan,clk-gate' = 0, providers = 0

**212 children and zero gates** - while /proc/device-tree/clk@14880000 shows ~20 gate children.  So the
node being walked is NOT the node the device exposes.  Addressing it by exact path
(`of_find_node_by_path("/clk@14880000")`, then the compatible as fallback) produced the SAME 0xDED40000,
so both lookups land on whatever node has 212 children.  A node with ~212 children in a large DT is
plausibly the ROOT itself.

**NEXT STEP, and it is narrow:** in the walk, record the found node's NAME (and its first child's
compatible) into the crumb, so the next fire says which node was walked instead of inferring it.  That
is one fire, and it settles path-vs-compatible-vs-root in a single read.

## STATE

Board healthy on the vendor slot every fire (2.4.15, 6 interfaces, 0 leftovers, selector 0x10); our
kernel reliably boots OpenWrt to procd.  Committed: hsan,crg match, the DT-walk provider, the per-driver
diagnostic cells, the watchdog-backstop restart.

The difficulty is not the register work - it is that the DT the kernel actually consumes has never been

                       verified writable by a controlled test.
    gmac 0xC0DE6F03 / mdio 0xC0DE7F03   both still die at the clock step
    mach 0xC0DE8D00   drv registered, eth0 absent
    the scheduler oops is gone; restart cannot strand the board; OpenWrt boots to procd every fire

## THE RULE THIS EARNS

A diagnostic cell must be PROVEN to carry the value you write before any inference rests on it, and the
proof must use a payload that could not coincidentally match.  I wrote three different payloads to 0xC9C
and read one value back three times; the correct first move was a single write-read of a unique
sentinel, checked in the SAME fire that added the instrument.  Instead I read an instrument's consistent
silence as data for two phases.

## NEXT (deliberately narrow, and no inference until it passes)

  1. Pick a DIFFERENT cell from the verified-writable set (0xC80..0xC88, 0xC8C..0xC98 are in use) and
     write a UNIQUE sentinel; read it back in the same fire.  If it sticks, that cell becomes the
     instrument; if it does not, the write path itself is the problem.
  2. Only then re-ask the clock-node question.
  3. The device-side read already gives a stronger lead and needs no cell at all: clk@14880000 is
     "hsan,clk syscon simple-mfd" with 16 clk_gate children, so the PLATFORM-DRIVER route is likely
     viable after all - the vgate crumb's silence at 0xC9C is no longer evidence against it.

# PHASE 91 (2026-10-12): THE ORDER BUG WAS MINE, THE LOOKUP IS REAL

## THE ROOT CAUSE OF THREE IDENTICAL READINGS: MY OWN WRITE ORDER

Reading the source instead of theorising about the hardware:

    986   name stamp      writel(tag, sc + 0xc9c)
    1007  pointer stamp   writel((u32)clk_np, sc + 0xc9c)
    1013  of_node_put
    1025  COUNTERS        writel(0xdec00000 | ...)      <-- LAST: overwrote both, every single fire

Three builds, three different payloads, one identical read back (0xDED40000) because the counter block
sat last and clobbered the others.  **The cell was never unsound.  My ordering was.**  In PHASE 90 I
declared the instrument void and withdrew a conclusion on that basis; the correct read of the same
evidence was "my instrument's writes disagree", and the correct next move was to read the source, not to
re-plan around the hardware.

Also fixed in the same edit: clk_np->full_name was dereferenced AFTER of_node_put(clk_np).

## THE POSITIVE RESULT (new, and it is real)

After removing the counter block the pointer is the last write and survives:

    C9C = 0xC7EE77E0

ARM32 kernel lowmem is 0xC0000000-0xEFFFFFFF, so **0xC7EE77E0 is a VALID struct device_node *** (my
earlier validity test wrongly accepted only 0xC0/0x80 top bytes and called this "not a kernel pointer").
It also CHANGED from 0xDED40000, which proves the ordered write lands.

**Therefore: the path/compatible lookup returns a REAL node, and seen = 0xD4 = 212 is a real child count.**

## THE OPEN QUESTION, SHARPLY POSED

A real node with **212 children**.  The device's own /proc/device-tree/clk@14880000 has **24** and the root
has **73**.  Neither is 212.  Since the pointer is valid, this is a question about WHICH node it is, not
about whether the lookup worked.  Two explanations, distinguishable in one fire:

  (a) the kernel's active tree differs from the vendor /proc/device-tree view, and some node really has
      212 children;
  (b) the walk iterates something other than direct children.

## NEXT (one fire; the instrument is now trustworthy)

Stamp, with the counter block deleted:
  1. of_get_child_count(clk_np)                  - independent of the for_each loop
  2. first four bytes of clk_np->full_name       - ASCII: "clk@" means the right node
  3. clk_np itself                               - LAST, so it survives
Comparing (1) against the loop's `seen` separates (a) from (b) in a single read.

## STATE

Board healthy on the vendor slot every fire (2.4.15, 6 interfaces, 0 leftovers, selector 0x10).  The CRG
binds and registers its clock tree (0xC90 = 0xC0DE5002) - untouched by any of this.

# PHASE 93 (2026-10-12): *** THE CLOCK BUG IS FIXED - THE NICs ARE PAST THE CLOCK GATE ***

## MEASURED RESULT

    0xC9C  paths=16   PROVIDERS=16                  16/16 gate providers registered
    gmac   0xC0DE6F04        STEP 4  (was step 3 = clock)
    mdio   0xC0DE7F04        STEP 4  (was step 3 = clock)
    CRG    0xC0DE5002        clock tree still registered
    mach   0xC0DE8D00        eth0 not yet (resets still fail first)

**Both NIC drivers now clear clock acquisition for the first time in this whole chain.**  The failure
moved from step 3 (clk) to step 4 (resets) - a NEW blocker, which is the definition of progress here.

## THE ACTUAL DEFECT (one line of it)

The vendor's clock-gate nodes have **NO `reg` property**.  Read From the captured active tree
(build/tmp/dt-spec/tar_base.dts):

    clk_gate@002003 {
        #clock-cells = <0x0>;        <- confirms the per-node 0-cell model
        bit          = <0x3>;        <- the BIT is its own u32 property
        reg-offset   = " ";          <- a STRING here; NUMERIC <0x14> for the 0x14 group
        clocks       = <0x8>;        <- parent by phandle
        compatible   = "hsan,clk-gate";
    };

Reading `reg` failed for all 16 nodes (measured reg_ok=0), which is why every downstream stage was zero
too.  The correct read is `bit` plus an offset taken from a numeric `reg-offset` when present, else from
the node's UNIT ADDRESS (clk_gate@002003 -> 0x2003 -> offset 0x20).

**Instrument note:** the 0xC80 stage vector's nibble packing was wrong (s_kz << 12 overlaps s_reg's high
bits, read back as reg_ok=17 with only 16 paths).  0xC9C - which has no packing - was the authoritative
reading throughout.  Fix the packing or use separate cells; do not trust a packed vector without
recomputing its field widths.

## STEP 4 IS NOW THE BLOCKER, AND ITS MODEL IS ALREADY KNOWN

    gmac0: resets = <0xf 0x30 0xd  0xf 0x30 0xe>;  reset-names = "mac_logic_reset" "mac_reset"
    mdio : resets = <0xf 0x30 0x6  0xf 0x30 0x1a ...>; reset-names = "mdio_reset" ... "gephy0_reset" ...

3-cell specifiers (phandle, offset, bit) referencing phandle 0xf - the crg/rstinfo block, whose shape the
tree also names (`rstinfo@0x14880000`, compatible "hsan,rstinfo", rstinfo-offset = <0xe>).  So the same
class of fix is likely: make the reset provider resolve for the consumers' exact specifier shape.

## STATE

Board healthy on the vendor slot every fire.  Our kernel boots OpenWrt to procd every fire.  The CRG has
bound and registered its clock tree since the "hsan,crg" name fix; now the 16 gate providers register too.

# PHASE 94 (2026-10-12): THE RESET MODEL - WHAT THE TREE SAYS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT

Step 4 is now the blocker (gmac 0xC0DE6F04 / mdio 0xC0DE7F04).  The consumers' specifiers, straight from
the captured active tree:

    gmac0: resets = <0xf 0x30 0xd  0xf 0x30 0xe>;  reset-names = "mac_logic_reset" "mac_reset"
    mdio : resets = <0xf 0x30 0x6  0xf 0x30 0x1a 0xf 0x30 0x1b ...>;
           reset-names = "mdio_reset" "gephyall_reset" "gephy0_reset" ... "gephy3_reset"

So a 3-cell specifier (phandle, offset, bit): offset 0x30, bits 0x6/0xd/0xe/0x1a..0x1f.

**BUT phandle 0xf DOES NOT APPEAR in the tree as a normal phandle.**  Enumerating every node's phandle
gives 0x33-0x3b, 0x43, 0x50, 0x52-0x65, 0x69-0x77 - ASCII-character phandles - and 0xf is not among them.
That was also why the earlier probe of "which node is 0xf" came back empty.

Two readings, and they matter for the fix:
  (a) 0xf is a phandle whose encoded form is a non-printable character and my enumeration missed it, or
  (b) the vendor's reset specifier is NOT a standard 3-cell reset specifier at all - the leading cell may
      be something other than a phandle (a provider index or a literal), in which case no Linux #reset-cells
      provider will ever resolve it and the reset must be driven directly (the crg block has the rstinfo
      shape already captured: rstinfo@0x14880000, "hsan,rstinfo", rstinfo-offset = <0xe>).

DO NOT guess between these.  The next read is cheap and device-free: dump the raw bytes of the gmac0
node's `resets` property and of every plausible provider node's `phandle`, and see whether any phandle
encodes as 0xf.  `/proc/device-tree/gemac@0x14300000/resets` on the running box answers it exactly.

## WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN GUESSED

The clock bug cost many fires precisely because I composed provider shapes before establishing what the
consumers actually reference.  The same question is open here, and it is answerable from the device in one
read.  Establish the specifier's meaning first; then the provider shape follows.
